STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: run_static is the ONE source-agnostic static orchestrator. For the live-sim path (source_kind in {'live_bridge','ros1'}, is_live=True) it drives a fixed schedule: (1) prewarm SAM3D ALONE during the sweep; (2) FRONT END = open the SHM source via open_source, build a ShmRing on cfg.shm_name, read intrinsics, spin up _RedBoxUI + its background feed thread (ui.start_feed), ui.begin('capture'), create a StaticRecorder and a SweepSeedBuilder; (3) SWEEP loop records deduped keyframes and submits each kept one to the incremental seed builder until the operator triggers; (4) on trigger: tm.event('triggered'), recorder.finalize() writes static_scene/, ui.drop_box(), and touch the rgb-only sentinel; (5) SHARED BACK END (identical live+recorded): segment (FastSAM prompt) -> SAM3D generate -> close SAM worker -> spawn AnySplat/XFeat + warm gsplat into freed VRAM -> finalize/build TSDF seed -> Splatfacto train -> Phase-0b fuse (on_fuse callback flips train->fuse in the checklist) -> export static_state.pt. Stage ordering is enforced by sequential `with tm.stage(...)` blocks and ui.begin/done calls. Returns the static_state.pt path, or (path,(sm,gset,lock),reg) when return_scene=True for the single-process handoff into the dynamic loop.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: During the sweep, ONLY SAM3D is prewarmed (reg['sam3d'].prewarm() inside the tm.stage('sweep.sam3d_load') block) so it gets the GPU/CPU to itself and its ~25 s load hides under the operator sweep. build_registry requests want_anysplat=(prewarm_dynamic and ff_enabled) and want_xfeat=prewarm_dynamic, but those heavy dynamic-phase models (AnySplat ~3.4 GB, XFeat/LighterGlue) and the gsplat-backward warm are DEFERRED until after SAM3D inference completes and the SAM worker is closed (after.sam_worker_close). AnySplat specifically CANNOT load during the sweep: concurrent with SAM3D's ~8.6 GB load + Gazebo it OOMs a 16 GB card; it must wait for sam_worker_close to free SAM3D's VRAM. FastSAM is loaded lazily right before the segment stage (reg['fastsam'].prewarm(); wait_ready()) because its ~0.85 GB resident during SAM3D's load peak also OOMs 16 GB; FastSAM is released immediately after a valid segmentation so it isn't held idle through SAM3D infer. This ordering is a hard VRAM-ceiling constraint, not a speed preference.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: build_registry is called with want_anysplat=(prewarm_dynamic and ff_enabled) so a --no-ff run never spawns the AnySplat feedforward worker (~17 s / ~3.5 GB), which an FF-off dynamic loop would never adopt or free. want_xfeat is gated only on prewarm_dynamic. model_loader.set_timing_ledger(tm) is called first so background prewarm threads record their load.* substeps into the shared ledger.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: _RedBoxUI owns a bare viser.ViserServer on port int(getattr(cfg.viser,'port',8081)) (NO gaussian render — the sweep has no scene yet). It adds a single GUI button 'Trigger (object in box)' whose on_click sets a threading.Event (_fired). The live camera feed is pushed as each client's background image via client.scene.set_background_image(rgb, format='jpeg') (server-side push-image). show() copies the BGR frame, and while _draw_box is True draws a centered square via cv2.rectangle of side s=min(self._box,H,W) at top-left ((W-s)//2,(H-s)//2) in color (0,0,255) BGR thickness 3, then converts BGR->RGB (img[...,::-1]) before pushing. box_px default is 300 in the _RedBoxUI.__init__ and run_static signatures, but the CLI _main parser overrides it to 500 via --box-px default=500.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: start_feed(ring) spawns a daemon thread (_feed_loop, name 'redbox-feed') that continuously pushes the freshest SHM frame so the viewer stays real-time during EVERYTHING (sweep + SAM3D + train), independent of the main pipeline thread. _feed_loop calls ring.peek_latest(); when fr is not None and fr.seq differs from the last pushed seq it calls show(fr.rgb_bgr), else waits 0.03 s. Every 15 iterations (~0.5 s) it calls _push_steps() so the ongoing step's elapsed-seconds counter in the checklist panel ticks. close() sets _stop_feed and joins the thread (timeout 2.0 s) before stopping the viser server.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: The checklist tracks six steps from _STEP_LIST: capture('Initial capture'), segment('Segmentation'), generate('Object generation'), train('Scene training'), fuse('Fusion'), realtime('Realtime pipeline'). Each step holds {label, state in {todo,doing,done}, t0, elapsed}. begin(key, keep=()) marks key 'doing' and sets t0=time.monotonic(), and AUTO-finishes any OTHER 'doing' step unless its key is in `keep` (used as keep=('capture',) so 'capture' stays yellow while 'segment'/'generate' run). done(key) freezes elapsed=monotonic()-t0 and sets state 'done'. The panel is rendered as a viser markdown widget via _render_steps_md(): icon map {todo:white circle, doing:yellow circle, done:green circle}, with done steps suffixed '_(elapsed.1fs)_' and doing steps suffixed '_(secs…)_'. All begin/done state is guarded by _steps_lock. In run_static the order is: ui.begin('capture') at sweep start; ui.begin('segment',keep=('capture',)); ui.done('segment'); ui.begin('generate',keep=('capture',)); ui.done('generate'); ui.done('capture') (capture finishes AFTER SAM3D); ui.begin('train'); on_fuse callback does ui.done('train')+ui.begin('fuse'); ui.done('fuse'); ui.begin('realtime').

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: In __init__ a daemon thread runs _stdin_wait, which blocks on input() and on a bare Enter sets the same _fired event the button uses — so the sweep can be triggered without a browser (headless). If viser itself fails to start, __init__ catches the exception, prints that the UI is unavailable and instructs to use Enter; the stdin thread still works (it is started after the try/except). fired() returns _fired.is_set(); the sweep loop polls `while not ui.fired()`.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: drop_box() sets _draw_box=False so the centered red box stops being drawn once the operator triggers; from then on the checklist panel alone conveys phase. It is called immediately after the sweep loop exits (after recorder.finalize()). There is intentionally no text banner on the feed — the markdown checklist is the only phase indicator.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: show() tracks _last_push_hw=(H,W). When a new frame's (H,W) differs from the previous push (camera resolution changed mid-session, e.g. 720p->1080p), the browser tab keeps a canvas of the old W/H and a new-size frame rendered at the old stride wraps horizontally into two half-frames side-by-side. The guard logs the size change and, before pushing the new RGB, first pushes a 1x1 zero image (np.zeros((1,1,3),uint8), format='jpeg') to each client so the browser re-creates the background at the new size, then pushes the real RGB. This runs per-client inside the get_clients() loop.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: On recorded (replay) runs the UI is _NullUI: every method (begin/done/drop_box/start_feed/show/fired/close) is a no-op, fired() always returns False, and there is no viser server, live feed, or trigger button. Phase is conveyed by [static] print lines instead. The shared back end calls the same ui.* methods unconditionally, so _NullUI keeps it source-agnostic. (Recorded path is out of the live-sim scope here; noted for contrast.)

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: The live sweep loop reads ring.peek_latest(); it skips when fr is None or fr.seq==last_seq (sleeping 0.005 s), otherwise records last_seq=fr.seq, calls recorder.add(fr), and — if that returns True (a kept keyframe) AND a seed_builder exists — calls seed_builder.submit(fr) to fuse that keyframe on the background CPU TSDF thread AS IT ARRIVES. anchor_frame is updated every iteration to the freshest frame, so the trigger anchor is whatever the camera last saw. On exit it emits tm.event('triggered'), prints recorder.num_kept, warns if num_kept==0 (seed build WILL fail), and calls recorder.finalize().

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.topic: StaticRecorder keyframe gate — motion dedup thresholds
STATIC.idea: StaticRecorder._is_keyframe is a greedy ORB-SLAM-style accept gate in motion mode (default, interval_s=0). Frame 0 is always accepted (empty _kept_R). For later frames with pose c2w split into R=c2w[:3,:3], t=c2w[:3,3], it rejects the frame iff there EXISTS a previously kept frame within BOTH thresholds: translation dt=||t-tk|| <= trans_thresh_m (default 0.02 m = 2 cm) AND rotation dr=arccos(clip(0.5*(trace(R^T·Rk)-1),-1,1)) <= rot_thresh_deg converted to radians (default 20° -> self._rt=deg2rad(20)). I.e. a frame is KEPT only if it is far enough in translation OR rotation from ALL kept frames. This drops near-duplicate views so training isn't fed redundant frames. (An alternate time mode interval_s>0 accepts frame 0 then one every interval_s seconds ignoring motion — for a FIXED camera; default 1.0 s under DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA, else 0 — the real-HW branch, not the live-sim path.)

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: add() first drops any frame whose rgb_bgr/depth_m/mask_keep is None or whose rgb/depth array .size==0 (a torn SHM read), returning False. After the keyframe gate passes, it re-mkdirs rgb/depth/masks (exist_ok, defensive against a vanished dir) and writes three files under stem='arm_{n:05d}': rgb/{stem}.png (cv2.imwrite of the BGR frame), depth/{stem}.tiff (depth -> nan_to_num(nan=0,posinf=0,neginf=0) THEN *1000.0 clipped to [0,65535] cast uint16 mm), masks/{stem}.png (mask reduced to 2D if 3D, written as (keep>0)*255 uint8). The transforms.json entry is STAGED only if all three imwrites returned True AND all three files exist on disk; otherwise the frame is dropped, the partial files unlinked, and a WARNING printed — guaranteeing transforms.json never references a missing file. On success it appends the meta dict, records R,t into _kept_R/_kept_t (so subsequent dedup compares against it), increments _n, returns True.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: Each staged frame meta is {file_path:'./rgb/arm_{n:05d}.png', depth_file_path:'./depth/arm_{n:05d}.tiff', mask_path:'./masks/arm_{n:05d}.png', transform_matrix: c2w 4x4 as nested lists (float64 via c2w.tolist()), stamp_wall: float(frame.stamp_sec)}. All paths are relative with a './' prefix. finalize() writes transforms.json atomically (write to .json.tmp then os.replace) containing top-level intrinsics {w,h,fl_x,fl_y,cx,cy} from the Intrinsics plus the 'frames' list. The live recorder names ALL keyframes 'arm_{n:05d}' (zero-padded width 5). The 'aa_'-prefixed lead-in convention referenced in _anchor_from_disk's docstring is NOT produced by StaticRecorder — it is a sort-order note about other capture tooling; the recorded anchor selection sorts frames by file_path STRING (not trailing integer) to match nerfstudio's dataparser so the last sweep keyframe (arm_*) is the anchor.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: Two GPU-contention controls protect the shared 16 GB card. (1) DGS_PUB_SWEEP_HZ (read from env, default '0' = OFF = full rate; ValueError -> 0.0) is passed as max_hz into open_source so the SWEEP publisher can be capped (e.g. ~10 Hz) to cut its per-frame decode + mask-GL + SHM contention so the concurrent SAM3D load hides under the sweep; the SEPARATE dynamic publisher (run_live) is spawned separately at full rate. (2) Immediately after the sweep ends, run_static touches a .rgb_only sentinel file in LIVE_ROOT (from dynamic_gs.utils.live_shm_reader.LIVE_ROOT): once the sweep is over no module consumes depth/mask except the UI's RGB feed, so the sentinel tells the static publisher to DROP its GPU-heavy robot-mask GL render + depth decode and cap to ~10 Hz, freeing the GPU for the concurrent TSDF-seed build + Splatfacto train.

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.topic: Incremental CPU seed during sweep (SweepSeedBuilder coupling)
STATIC.idea: On live runs a SweepSeedBuilder(intr, tm=tm) is started before the sweep; each kept keyframe is submit()ed and fused on a background CPU thread so the TSDF seed is mostly built by trigger time. Its voxel is SEED_VOXEL_M=0.003 (3 mm). After SAM3D, if a seed_builder exists, run_static calls seed_builder.finalize(data_dir/'static_scene') inside tm.stage('after.tsdf_integrate'); if it returns None (fused nothing / errored) it falls back to _build_seed_deferred (GPU subprocess). _build_seed_deferred runs dynamic_gs.utils.online_fusion in a subprocess with DGS_TSDF_VOXEL_M setdefault '0.003' and DGS_FUSION_DEVICE='cpu' (CPU always so it can't OOM the shared GPU; 3 mm matches SweepSeedBuilder; subprocess isolation contains Open3D teardown aborts); raises if rc!=0 or the PLY is absent, timeout 900 s. Recorded runs reuse the existing seed PLY (no seed_builder).

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: _warm_gsplat_backward runs ONE throwaway gsplat.rasterization + .backward on a tiny synthetic scene (N=16 gaussians, 64x64 image, K=[[100,0,32],[0,100,32],[0,0,1]], means shifted by [0,0,2.0] so they sit in front of the camera) on a daemon thread, so the gsplat CUDA kernels (projection fwd/bwd, fully_fused_projection, rasterize) JIT-compile in the post-SAM3D free slot instead of on the first real training step. It is fired in tm.stage('after.gsplat_warm') after AnySplat/XFeat prewarm; idempotent and cheap once the nvcc build is cached in ~/.cache/torch_extensions. Failures are caught and logged (will compile lazily on first train step).

STATIC.title: Sweep capture, trigger UI & keyframe recording
STATIC.idea: After segment, if objects is empty the pipeline releases FastSAM (reg['fastsam'].release()) and raises a RuntimeError telling the operator to retry (object must fill the red box at trigger, prompt a short matching noun). This avoids running SAM3D + fusion + train on an empty object set (which would leave object_instance_ids all-zero and only crash ~30 s later in the tracker with an opaque 'no tracked object' error). tm.event('objects_found', n=len(objects)) is recorded; tm.event('sam3d_done') marks the dead-time origin used by the timing report (_write_report calls tm.write_static with dead_time_after='sam3d_done').

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: The static-segment stage replaces SAM3 with FastSAM (Ultralytics YOLOv8-seg) for class-agnostic instance masks in one forward pass, then CLIP (open-clip) scores each mask crop against a text prompt. Unlike FastSAM's built-in text_prompt (top-1 only), this path keeps ALL candidate masks with their CLIP scores so the same area/border/dedup/max_objects filters apply. The output contract is a list of {mask_path, score, bbox(xyxy), mask_area, object_index} dicts, byte-identical to the old SAM3 worker so downstream SAM3D + fusion consume it unchanged. WHY: FastSAM-x + CLIP ViT-B-32 are light enough to co-reside with SAM3D (the heavy ~12GB Fast-SAM3D), so segmentation and 3D object generation can share one persistent worker; this is a stated drop-in for the heavier resident SAM3 (~3.8 GB).

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: In run_static the trigger frame flows through three timed stages: snapshot_anchor freezes the anchor; segment() runs FastSAM+CLIP via reg['fastsam'] (the shared-worker handle, prewarmed right before segment with prewarm()+wait_ready() to avoid a cold subprocess); write_seg_folder writes overlays+manifest. The caller checks `if not objects` — if 0, it calls reg['fastsam'].release() and raises RuntimeError telling the operator to retry with the object filling the red box and a short-noun prompt. On success it ALSO calls release() to unload FastSAM (~0.85GB) from the worker before the SAM3D infer. WHY fail-fast: without it the pipeline would run SAM3D+fusion+train on an empty object set (object_instance_ids all-zero) and crash ~30s later in the tracker with an opaque 'no tracked object' error.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.topic: snapshot_anchor — what is frozen and where
STATIC.idea: snapshot_anchor(frame, intr, data_dir, gripper_black=True) writes the EXACT frame both the 2D mask and SAM3D will see into <data_dir>/static_scene/segmentation/anchor/ (SEG_DIRNAME='segmentation'). It first shutil.rmtree's the whole seg dir (never reuse stale across datasets), then writes: rgb.png = frame.rgb_bgr.copy() with the robot blacked out (rgb[keep==0]=0 using frame.mask_keep, collapsing a 3-ch keep to its [...,0] channel) so SAM3D segments the object not the gripper; depth.tiff = frame.depth_m.astype(float32) in METRES (scale 1, SAM3D reads as-is); pose.json = c2w 4x4 OpenGL as a JSON nested list; intrinsics.json = {fx,fy,cx,cy,w,h}. Returns an AnchorRef (frozen dataclass) carrying absolute paths + the Intrinsics. WHY metres-TIFF + fx/fy/cx/cy/w/h: that is exactly the format the SAM3D subprocess consumes, so there is no format mismatch.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: write_seg_folder(anchor, objects, prompt_text) writes, per object, a 50/50 red-blend overlay PNG masks/obj_NN_overlay.png (ov[sel]=0.5*ov+0.5*red where red is BGR (0,0,255) and sel=mask>127), then a manifest.json at seg/. Each entry stores object_index, mask='masks/<name>', overlay='masks/obj_NN_overlay.png', score, bbox, mask_area; the manifest also points anchor rgb/depth/pose/intrinsics. WHY all paths RELATIVE to seg/: a copied or renamed dataset resolves them against the folder's own location so it can never FileNotFound — the explicit fix for the old cached SAM3 JSON that held absolute replay_20260612 paths. overlay_paths(data_dir) re-resolves the overlay PNGs from the manifest for the UI validation surface.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: _run_fastsam(image_path, conf, iou, imgsz) calls the Ultralytics FastSAM model with retina_masks=True, imgsz=1024, conf=fastsam_conf=0.4, iou=fastsam_iou=0.9, verbose=False. It returns masks (N,H,W) bool at native resolution via (r.masks.data>0.5) and boxes (N,4) xyxy from r.boxes.xyxy. If FastSAM yields no masks it returns empty (0,H,W) arrays sized from the source image. WHY conf=0.4/iou=0.9: keep many class-agnostic instance candidates (low conf, high NMS-iou) so the prompt/CLIP step does the selecting, not FastSAM's own NMS.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: _split_into_components splits each raw FastSAM instance mask into its 8-connectivity connected components (cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats), dropping components with CC_STAT_AREA < min_area_px where min_area_px = min_area_ratio*image_area = 0.002*W*H. Each surviving component becomes its own candidate mask+bbox; single-component masks pass through unchanged. WHY: a single FastSAM mask can span two DISJOINT objects (the docstring cites a 'screwdriver' mask carrying a 2716px blob on a neighbouring object, 19% of the mask) — bundled into one CLIP crop the dominant object carries the contaminant past CLIP; split, the contaminant scores low on its own and the threshold drops it. Enabled by split_components=True default; runs before CLIP scoring.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: _clip_scores crops each mask's bbox from the RGB, whites-out (=255) the in-bbox background outside the mask so CLIP sees only the object, preprocesses each crop, batch-encodes with CLIP image encoder, L2-normalizes image+text features, computes cosine sims = img_f @ txt_f.T for the single tokenized prompt, then probs = softmax(clip_logit_scale*sims) with clip_logit_scale=100.0 over the crops. Returns BOTH per-mask softmax prob (score) AND raw cosine. WHY both: softmax makes the best-matching object dominant for ranking, but discards absolute scale, so the raw cosine is kept for the N-invariant presence gate (whether any object exists). CLIP model is ViT-B-32-quickgelu / pretrained 'openai' — the -quickgelu variant is required because OpenAI weights were trained with QuickGELU (else open_clip silently degrades match quality, breaking the text gate).

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: Before any score gate, candidate masks are reduced to 'survivors': a mask survives only if its pixel area is within [min_area_ratio*image_area, max_area_ratio*image_area] = [0.002, 0.25] of total pixels (drop specks and table/wall-sized blobs) AND it does NOT touch >=2 image borders (_touches_n_borders with n=2: counts top/bottom/left/right rows/cols that contain any True). WHY border-2: a mask hugging two or more edges is background/table, not a centred object. Zero-area masks are skipped. This survivor set is the only set the threshold and promotion logic ever judge.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: With auto_threshold=True (default), probs are RE-softmaxed over survivors only (p=exp(100*cos)/sum, because _clip_scores softmaxed over the full raw FastSAM set of often 100-300 masks so its probs don't sum to 1 over survivors). select_kept_indices then decides HOW MANY by the largest consecutive log-prob gap: sort probs descending, gaps = log(s[:-1])-log(s[1:]), k=argmax(gaps); keep order[:k+1] only if gaps[k] >= log(min_ratio) with auto_min_ratio=2.5, else keep nothing. WHY log/ratio space: a real winner->tail jump is a >=2.5x ratio (docstring: measured 13-40x) vs <2.5x tail-internal steps, and the ratio space is N-invariant whereas a raw-prob gap mis-cuts uneven multi-object sets. For n==1 the cliff trivially keeps the single top candidate.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: select_kept_indices also runs a presence gate on RAW cosine to answer 'is anything here at all': med=median(cosines), mad=median(|cos-med|), cos_floor = med + mad_k*1.4826*mad with auto_mad_k=3.0 (1.4826 makes MAD a robust std estimate). A candidate passes only if cos >= cos_floor AND (cos - med) >= margin_min with auto_margin_min=0.04. The cliff-kept set (or order[:1] fallback if the cliff kept nothing) is filtered by this gate; np.sort returns survivors. WHY on raw cosine not softmax: a flat zero-object field can softmax to a HIGHER max than a weak true match, so absolute presence can only be judged on raw cosine. WHY the second margin_min clause: on a homogeneous background MAD->0 explodes cos_floor toward med and a chance specular patch would pass — the fixed 0.04 absolute-margin kills those phantoms. This is the mechanism that yields the 0-objects fail-fast when nothing matches.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: After the auto gate, if min_score>0.0 an extra AND-guard drops any kept index whose SURVIVOR-softmax prob < min_score (surv_score, the re-softmaxed prob). The static path explicitly passes min_score=0.0 (static_segment.segment default), so this floor is OFF in the live-sim flow and the auto gate solely owns the decision; the worker's fastsam_infer default of 0.2 is overridden by that explicit 0.0. With auto_threshold=False (legacy), the path instead keeps survivors whose raw CLIP softmax score >= min_score directly. WHY kept: backward-compat hard floor that can still be re-enabled.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.topic: Promote-to-container (keep the WHOLE object vs a high-CLIP sub-part)
STATIC.idea: promote_to_container=True: for each kept mask i, scan ALL survivors j (pre-cliff) for a LARGER survivor that ENGLOBES i — keep if area(j)>area(best) AND intersection(i,j)/area(i) >= promote_contain_frac=0.8 AND (cos_i - cos_j) <= promote_cos_margin=0.03; if found, swap kept part i for the fuller survivor j. Result de-duped preserving order. WHY: split_components can carve an object into parts (screwdriver -> metal shaft + handle) and CLIP often scores the small distinctive PART slightly higher than the whole, so the cliff gate would keep the shaft and drop the full mask BEFORE the containment-dedup can englobe it (docstring measured: shaft cos 0.267 area 5112 KEPT vs full-screwdriver cos 0.256 area 42598 dropped, shaft 100% inside full). Running on survivors keeps the fuller mask available; the containment-dedup then collapses any duplicate the promotion creates. NOTE: the warm-worker fastsam_infer does NOT forward this kwarg, so the segmenter default True applies on the live path.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.idea: Kept candidates become dicts {mask,score,bbox,mask_area}, sorted LARGEST-area first. A later candidate is dropped as redundant if, against any already-kept (larger-or-equal) k, either IoU > dedup_iou=0.6 OR contained = inter/area_c >= 0.8 (>=80% of c lies inside k). WHY: FastSAM emits the same object at multiple extents (tight shaft mask, high CLIP, AND full shaft+handle mask, lower) — processing largest-first keeps the FULLEST and drops the contained sub-part. This also acts as the junk discriminator the lowered min_score floor gave up: a real fuller mask CONTAINS its confident sub-part, but an unrelated false positive is a disjoint blob containing nothing kept, so it survives dedup as its own candidate (only the score gate can reject it); two genuinely disjoint distinct objects don't contain each other so both survive. Survivors are then re-sorted by score descending and truncated to max_objects=8.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.topic: Outputs written by infer (masks + SAM3-compatible summary + debug)
STATIC.idea: infer writes each deduped mask as <stem>_obj_NN_mask.png (mask*255) and builds the returned {mask_path,score,bbox,mask_area,object_index} list (object_index reassigned 0..K-1 in score order). It also writes <stem>_sam3_results.json tagged segmentation_backend='fastsam' carrying total_raw_masks, total_candidates_after_split, total_after_filtering, the full filter_params, and per-object entries — REUSING the SAM3 summary filename so downstream load_sam3_masks / sam3_reuse_cached work unchanged. A best-effort <stem>_fastsam_components.png overlays the top-20 post-split components (by cosine) colored+labeled rank:cosX.XX:KEPT|surv|filt, plus a JSON sidecar of per-component cosine/area/bbox/tag, so a partial mask (object split, only best component KEPT) is visible. infer_raw is a separate path that dumps all masks with CLIP score>=min_score (default 0.0 keeps the full class-agnostic set) into <stem>_raw_masks.npz {masks,scores,boxes} for the preseg AMG-merge path — not the prompt-matched object path.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.topic: Prompt format rules + how the prompt selects the object
STATIC.idea: The prompt is a single text string (cfg.segmentation.prompt_text from env DGS_SAM3_PROMPT, default ''). It is tokenized once and CLIP-matched against every mask crop's cosine; selection is then purely score-driven (cliff + presence + container/dedup) — the prompt never pre-masks the image. The fail-fast message instructs operators to use a SHORT NOUN matching the object (e.g. 'screwdriver'). The prompt also flows verbatim into the manifest ('prompt') and the SAM3 summary ('text_prompt'). A single prompt selects ONE object family; the cliff/presence machinery determines how many instances of it survive.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.topic: Where AMG / SAM2 / min_obj_votes actually live (NOT this path)
STATIC.idea: The main static segment() path uses ONLY FastSAM+CLIP — there is no AMG, SAM2, or min_obj_votes in static_segment.py or FastSamTextSegmenter.infer. SAM2-AMG (points_per_side=32, min_area_px=400, max_area_frac=0.60, max_masks=32), SAM3-grouping coverage-merge, SAM2-video propagation, and min_obj_votes (default 2, occlusion-voted 3D label assignment) belong to the SEPARATE static-gs-preseg method (per-Gaussian instance IDs, fuse-before-train) in dynamic_gs/static_gs_preseg_pipeline.py + preseg_seed.py — a different registered method, not the FastSAM static path documented here.

STATIC.title: 2D segmentation (FastSAM + CLIP)
STATIC.topic: Execution paths (warm worker vs subprocess) + env
STATIC.idea: FastSamHandle.segment runs warm via the shared persistent SamWorkerClient (c.fastsam_infer) so FastSAM co-resides with SAM3D in one process; if no worker it falls back to run_fastsam_subprocess which spawns python in the sam3_dynamic_gs conda env (resolving DYNAMIC_GS_CONDA_ROOT/envs/<env>/bin/python, falling back to `conda run` if absent; setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH to that env's lib and PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1), forwarding only CLI-known kwargs (area/dedup/max_objects/min_score/fastsam_conf/iou/imgsz/weights/clip/auto-* — it drops promote_* and SAM3-only keys like confidence_threshold). FastSAM-x weights default 'FastSAM-x.pt' cached at ~/.cache/dynamic_gs/fastsam/. Torch/ultralytics/open_clip are imported lazily so importing the module on the parent dynamic_gs side is cheap. A real-HW branch is not relevant here; segmentation runs identically for live-sim and recorded sources.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: static_sam3d.generate(anchor, objects, sam3d_handle) is the STATIC 3D-object-generation entrypoint: given the segmentation anchor (one RGB frame + its float32-metre depth + intrinsics) and the per-object FastSAM mask dicts, it produces one self-describing per-object result dict list. It early-returns [] if objects is empty, makes <seg_dir>/objects/, collects mask_paths = [Path(o['mask_path'])] and output stems = f"obj_{int(o['object_index']):02d}_sam3d" (zero-padded 2-digit index), then delegates to sam3d_handle.generate(render_image_path=anchor.rgb_path, object_mask_paths, output_dir=objects_dir, output_stems=stems, depth_path=anchor.depth_path, intrinsics_path=anchor.intrinsics_path). Each success result is {status:'ok', ply_path, pose_path, preview_path, mesh_ply_path, used_shape}; a failed/skipped object yields {status:'failed'/'skipped', ...} (NOT {}). World placement is NOT done here — that is phase0b.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: The anchor that feeds SAM3D is one captured frame written to <data_dir>/static_scene/segmentation/anchor/ by snapshot_anchor (NOT write_anchor): rgb.png (BGR via cv2.imwrite; when gripper_black and frame.mask_keep is not None the robot is blacked out where keep==0 before writing), depth.tiff = frame.depth_m cast float32 in METRES (cv2.imwrite, SAM3D scale 1.0), intrinsics.json = {fx,fy,cx,cy,w,h} from the frame intrinsics, and pose.json = the 4x4 c2w (used later by phase0b, NOT by generation). SAM3D therefore sees exactly the frame each FastSAM mask belongs to — no resampling/cross-frame mismatch. AnchorRef carries seg_dir/rgb_path/depth_path/pose_path/intrinsics_path/intr.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: model_loader.Sam3dHandle wraps the shared persistent worker so SAM3D loads ONCE, on-demand, hidden under the operator sweep. prewarm() spawns/loads SAM3D (c.load_sam3d()) on a daemon bg thread, recording the result via a threading.Event (self._loaded), so its heavy import+checkpoint-load overlaps capture instead of stalling the trigger; generate() calls wait_ready() then c.sam3d_infer(...). If the worker is unavailable it falls back to dynamic_gs.utils.sam3d.run_sam3d_multi_object_subprocess (cold per-call subprocess). release() calls c.unload_sam3d() so SAM3D's GPU residency is freed for the TSDF seed + splatfacto that follow.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: SamWorkerClient launches ONE long-lived subprocess: it invokes the env python directly at ~/miniconda3/envs/<conda_env>/bin/python (default env 'sam3_dynamic_gs' via _DEFAULT_ENV, overridable by DYNAMIC_GS_SAM_WORKER_ENV) running this same file with --worker, bypassing `conda run`. It prepends <env>/lib to LD_LIBRARY_PATH, sets PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, and prepends the scripts root (_THIS_FILE.parents[2]) to PYTHONPATH so the worker can import dynamic_gs.* helpers. The Popen invocation actually passes ['-u', file, '--worker'] (not bare). After Popen it blocks reading stdout lines until a JSON {"status":"ready"} arrives (startup_timeout_s default 30.0s; kills proc on timeout, raises if it exits early). This pays the heavy torch+model import cost once instead of per call.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: The protocol is one JSON object per stdin line -> exactly one JSON response per stdout line. Client._request writes {"cmd":cmd, **kwargs}+newline, flushes, then loops reading stdout lines until it parses a dict that contains a 'status' key (default per-request timeout 600.0s). Non-dict / no-'status' lines are SKIPPED — required because SAM3D's pipeline emits loguru messages that can JSON-parse as lists/numbers (e.g. cfg_interval=[0,500]) and would otherwise poison the line protocol. status=='error' raises RuntimeError(msg). On the worker side _worker_main reserves fd 1 for protocol writes via os.fdopen(os.dup(1)) and repoints python-level sys.stdout to sys.stderr so any rogue print()/loguru inside SAM3D goes to stderr, never the protocol FD. Stderr is forwarded to the parent (stderr=None on Popen). 'shutdown' cmd ends the loop.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: _SamWorker.load_sam3d() (idempotent — returns already_loaded if present) builds the official Fast-SAM3D API: _write_runtime_config() writes a runtime YAML overriding the bundled config with rendering_engine='pytorch3d', compile_model=False, dtype='float16', depth_model.device='cpu', depth_model pretrained path 'Ruicheng/moge-vitl' (MoGe still constructed but bypassed when pointmap is passed), workspace_dir=YAML dir (SAM3D_CONFIG_PATH.parent so relative ckpt paths resolve), decode_formats=['gaussian'] (mesh decoder's 256^3 FlexiCubes grid would OOM), and provides slat_decoder_mesh config/ckpt paths anyway (init_slat_decoder_mesh lacks a None-guard and would crash). It then constructs Inference(cfg, compile=False); on ANY exception it gc.collect()+empty_cache() before re-raise so a failed/OOM load never leaves a poisoning partial allocation.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.topic: Pipeline param patches applied after load
STATIC.idea: After Inference is built, load_sam3d() patches the pipeline to the gaussian-only/light path: inference.hfer_2d=0 and inference._pipeline.hfer_2d=0; ss_params={ss_faster_stride:3, ss_warmup:2, ss_order:1, ss_momentum_beta:0.5}; slat_params={slat_thresh:0.5, slat_warmup:2, slat_token_ratio:0.15}; mesh_params={mesh_spectral_threshold_low:0.5, mesh_spectral_threshold_high:0.7}; enable_mesh=False. These are the sampler/decoder knobs (sparse-structure stride/warmup/order, SLAT decode threshold+token ratio) the SAM3D forward uses to generate the gaussian object; mesh is disabled to match decode_formats.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: apply_sam3d_gaussian_trim(inference) shrinks resident GPU footprint without meaningfully changing the gaussian output (disable with DGS_SAM3D_NO_TRIM=1): it .half()s the diffusion generators models['ss_generator'] and models['slat_generator'] plus every condition_embedder (DINOv2) in pipeline.condition_embedders (safe because the SAM3D forward already runs under autocast float16), and .to('cpu')s the never-invoked modules slat_decoder_mesh, ss_encoder, slat_decoder_gs_4 (each guarded by 'if m is not None'; slat_decoder_gs_4 is already None per the config). Then gc.collect()+cuda.empty_cache(). This is what lets SAM3D resident-load co-exist with capture/TSDF/splatfacto.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: sam3d_infer(render_image_path, object_mask_paths, output_stems, output_dir, image_dir=None, max_side=518, depth_path=None, intrinsics_path=None) raises if SAM3D not loaded, requires len(masks)==len(stems). It opens the render image as RGB (np.array), and for each mask path loads a binary mask via _load_binary_mask(path, image_pil.size): mask opened 'L', NEAREST-resized to the image size if needed, then thresholded >127 -> uint8. It raises ValueError if image/mask H,W mismatch. Output filenames per stem come from get_sam3d_output_paths: <stem>_raw_output.ply, <stem>_pose.json, <stem>_preview.png, <stem>_run_info.txt, <stem>_mesh.ply (also _mesh.glb).

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: When BOTH depth_path and intrinsics_path are given, sam3d_infer builds a full-resolution metric pointmap_full = _build_pytorch3d_pointmap(depth_m, intrinsics) so SAM3D uses REAL metric depth instead of MoGe's scale/shift-invariant estimate. depth is read from the TIFF as float32 and NEAREST-resized to the RGB H,W if shapes differ. _build_pytorch3d_pointmap does CV back-projection with the x and y axis flips folded into x_cam=-(u-cx)/fx*z, y_cam=-(v-cy)/fy*z, z_cam=z — converting CV (x-right,y-down,z-fwd) into SAM3D's pytorch3d camera convention (x-left,y-up,z-fwd, from look_at_view_transform eye=[0,0,-1],up=[0,-1,0]); pixels with z<=0 are set to NaN so SAM3D treats them as holes. Output is (H,W,3) float32.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.topic: Resize to max_side=518 and the OOM size-ladder
STATIC.idea: For each object SAM3D runs an OOM retry ladder over candidate sizes built from [max_side(=518),112,96,80,64,48], each min'd to max_side and de-duped. For each candidate it gc+empty_cache, then _resize_image_and_mask(image_rgb, mask, max_side=cand): if max(H,W)<=max_side returns unchanged, else scale=max_side/max(H,W), new=(round(W*scale),round(H*scale)), image BILINEAR-resized, mask NEAREST-resized then re-binarized >127. The pointmap is matched to the resized image: if pointmap_full HxW already equals the resized image it is used directly, else torch.nn.functional.interpolate(mode='nearest') to (th,tw). 518 is the largest long-side fed to the network; lower ladder rungs (112..48) are OOM fallbacks tried in order until inference succeeds.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: The actual SAM3D generation call is output = inference(cur_image, cur_mask, seed=42, pointmap=resized_pointmap) (or without pointmap if none); seed=42 is fixed. On torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError it drops to the next ladder size. Success requires 'gs' in output; otherwise the object is recorded {status:'failed', attempted_sizes}. output['gs'].save_ply(ply_path) writes the per-object gaussian splat PLY in the SAM3D CANONICAL frame. A pose sidecar is built from output keys translation/rotation/scale (each tensor->cpu->reshape(-1)->list); if 'rotation' is missing or len!=4 the object is failed ('no valid rotation'). pose.json is written, plus a run_info.txt (render/mask/image_shape/used_shape/attempted/mesh_saved). The rotation is a wxyz quaternion in the SAM3D/pytorch3d canonical frame — phase0b uses it as the rigid rotation init.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: Although decode_formats=['gaussian'], sam3d_infer still tries a best-effort triangle-mesh export: if output.get('mesh') is non-empty and mesh[0].success (getattr default True), it converts vertices/faces to numpy and trimesh.Trimesh(process=False).export(<stem>_mesh.ply); failures are printed to stderr and mesh_saved stays False (mesh_ply_path reported as None). In the configured gaussian-only path no mesh tensor is produced, so this branch normally no-ops — the canonical reconstruction consumed downstream is the gaussian PLY, not the mesh.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: sam3d_fusion.load_sam3d_gaussian_ply(ply_path) reads the SAM3D gaussian PLY with plyfile, stacks vertex x,y,z -> (N,3) float32 xyz, and if f_dc_0/f_dc_1/f_dc_2 are present decodes them as SH DC coefficients to RGB via nerfstudio SH2RGB(features_dc).clamp(0,1) -> (N,3) float32; if no f_dc fields it fills RGB=0.5 (gray). Returns (xyz, rgb). This is the gaussian-CENTERS point cloud (source) phase0b registers onto the trained object gaussians. SH2RGB is needed because the PLY stores color as 0-order SH, not linear RGB the registration backends expect.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: sam3d_fusion.load_sam3d_rotation_wxyz(pose_path) calls load_sam3d_pose(path) (json.loads -> {translation,rotation,scale} each np.float32 reshape(-1)), takes pose.get('rotation'), and validates it is non-None, size==4, and all-finite, else raises ValueError. Returns the wxyz quaternion as float32. This is the canonical-frame rotation init that phase0b feeds into register_and_fuse_sam3d_object as source_rotation_wxyz (applied as a pre-rotation of the source cloud before scale/centroid/CPD registration). load_sam3d_pose lives in dynamic_gs/utils/sam3d.py.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.topic: How the loaders' outputs feed registration (boundary only)
STATIC.idea: In static_phase0b the loader outputs cross the boundary into world placement: load_sam3d_gaussian_ply gives (source_points, source_colors), load_sam3d_rotation_wxyz gives source_rotation_wxyz, and these are passed to register_and_fuse_sam3d_object(...) which applies the rotation init (_apply_sam3d_rotation_init: rotate by the wxyz->matrix via source_points @ rotation_p3d, map pytorch3d->NS camera via diag([-1,1,-1]) = SAM3D_P3D_TO_NS_CAMERA, then by camera_to_world_rotation^T), bbox-diagonal isotropic scale, centroid translation, voxel downsample, then CPD/TEASER registration refine. Generation+loading END here; the full registration/fusion math is the phase0b agent's scope.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.idea: The worker exposes explicit load_sam3d/unload_sam3d (and load/unload for SAM3/FastSAM) so callers sequence by VRAM budget. unload_sam3d() drops self.sam3d_inference/sam3d_runtime_cfg to None, gc.collect()+cuda.empty_cache(). _worker_main's handler_map dispatches cmd strings to the bound methods; unknown cmd -> {status:'error'}. This explicit load/infer/unload contract is what lets generate() free SAM3D (release()->unload_sam3d) before the TSDF seed + splatfacto run.

STATIC.title: 3D object generation (Fast-SAM3D)
STATIC.topic: Real-HW branches out of scope (one-line note)
STATIC.idea: This describes the SIM/live-sim path only. Real-hardware switches (DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini) affect upstream camera pose+mask generation that produces the anchor frame, but the SAM3D generation+loading code in static_sam3d/sam_worker/sam3d_fusion is identical regardless of source — it just consumes whatever anchor RGB/depth/intrinsics it is given.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: The TSDF depth seed is a single point cloud written to `<data>/static_scene/depth_camera_init_points.ply` that initializes the gaussians for static training (splatfacto inits one gaussian per seed point). The builder's finalize() also patches `transforms.json` by setting `meta['ply_file_path'] = 'depth_camera_init_points.ply'` (written atomically via a `.transforms.json.tmp` temp file + `os.replace`), so the nerfstudio dataparser picks the PLY up. The world frame is metric and unrecentered (dataparser uses orientation_method/center_method=none, auto_scale_poses=False) so the seed PLY lands in the same frame as the recorded camera poses. Both the live `SweepSeedBuilder.finalize` and the recorded `fuse_recorded_dataset` honor this exact same output+patch contract.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: Live-sim path = incremental CPU fuse during sweep
STATIC.idea: In the live-sim static phase, `SweepSeedBuilder` runs on a background daemon thread. start() sets env `DGS_FUSION_DEVICE='cpu'` to force the CPU fusion impl (no GPU contention with the SAM3D load that runs concurrently), constructs an `OnlineFusion`, and spawns the worker. During the operator sweep the loop in run_static calls `recorder.add(fr)` (the keyframe gate); when add() returns True the SAME kept frame is handed to `seed_builder.submit(fr)`, which copies its arrays and enqueues them on a thread-safe `queue.Queue`. The worker thread `_run` pops items and calls `_fuser.add_frame` (ICP-then-integrate). This exists so that by trigger time all keyframes are already fused and only finalize() (extract+downsample+write) remains, instead of paying a cold GPU subprocess after SAM3D. A `None` sentinel on the queue drains the worker.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: Keyframe gate feeding the seed (ORB-SLAM 2cm/20 deg)
STATIC.idea: Only keyframes are fused, gated by `StaticRecorder._is_keyframe` (in MOTION mode): accept frame 0 unconditionally, then accept a later frame only if NO previously-kept frame is within BOTH the translation threshold AND the rotation threshold of it. Translation distance = `norm(t - tk)` against threshold `trans_thresh_m=0.02` (2 cm). Rotation = `arccos(clip(0.5*(trace(R^T @ Rk) - 1), -1, 1))` (the geodesic angle between rotation matrices) against `rot_thresh_deg=20.0` converted to radians. If for any kept frame both `dt<=0.02` and `dr<=20deg`, the new frame is rejected. NOTE there is also a TIME mode (interval_s>0, default-on under DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA) that accepts one frame every interval_s seconds regardless of motion. This decimates the dense sweep stream to a sparse keyframe set; recorder.add() returns True exactly when a frame is kept, which is the trigger for submit() into the seed builder.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: submit() prepares the per-keyframe inputs for fusion. Depth: `nan_to_num(depth_m, nan/posinf/neginf=0.0)` first (live ZED depth has NaN holes; uint16 cast on NaN is undefined), then `clip(depth_m*1000, 0, 65535).astype(uint16)` to mm. Robot/gripper exclusion: it reads `frame.mask_keep` (squeezing a trailing channel if 3D), and sets `depth_mm[keep==0] = 0` so gripper pixels (depth==0) are dropped from BOTH ICP and TSDF. Pose `c2w_4x4` is copied as float64 OpenGL c2w. Color: `frame.rgb_bgr` is BGR, but online_fusion (WITH_COLOR=True) wants RGB uint8, so it does `ascontiguousarray(rgb[..., ::-1], uint8)` (channel-reverse BGR->RGB). It enqueues the tuple `(depth_mm, c2w_gl, rgb_u8)`. Arrays are copied so the SHM/Frame can be recycled by the sweep loop.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: WHY color matters for the fit
STATIC.idea: Color is fused into the TSDF (WITH_COLOR=True) and the seed points carry per-point colors, which become the gaussians' initial colors. If submit() passed rgb_u8=None (or fed BGR-as-RGB), the seed would be colorless/wrong; per the code's own rationale, an all-black seed makes gaussians init black, which can't match the bright scene, so the static photometric train drives opacity toward ~0 and the end-of-train opacity purge culls a large fraction of gaussians, leaving holes. The BGR->RGB reversal in submit() (mirroring `fuse_recorded_dataset`'s `cv2.imread(...)[:, :, ::-1]`) is the load-bearing fix for that opacity-collapse failure.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: Per-frame OnlineFusion algorithm: decimated-ICP then full-res integrate
STATIC.idea: `OnlineFusion.add_frame` (the proven core both seed builders wrap) processes one RGB-D frame: (1) convert OpenGL c2w to OpenCV via `c2w @ diag(1,-1,-1,1)` (`_cv_c2w`); (2) build an ICP SOURCE cloud by back-projecting depth decimated by `ICP_SRC_STRIDE` (only depth in the valid band is used), voxel-downsampling to `ICP_VOXEL_M`, and estimating normals; (3) point-to-plane ICP register the source against a GLOBAL accumulated voxel MODEL, initialized from the FK pose; (4) TSDF-integrate the FULL-RES depth (not the decimated source) at the ICP-refined pose. Decimation is ICP-only so TSDF precision is preserved. First frame: model = source, integrate at the raw FK pose. The refined OpenCV c2w is returned (used as the adaptive-downsample anchor: the LAST frame's translation).

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: ICP source cloud construction + valid depth band
STATIC.idea: `_src_cloud` selects valid pixels with `(depth_u16 > DEPTH_MIN_M*DEPTH_SCALE) & (depth_u16 < DEPTH_MAX_M*DEPTH_SCALE)` i.e. depth strictly in (0.05 m, 2.0 m) in mm units, then strides the valid pixel indices by `ICP_SRC_STRIDE`, back-projects with the pinhole model `x=(u-cx)*z/fx, y=(v-cy)*z/fy, z=depth/1000`, lifts to world via the OpenCV c2w, voxel-downsamples to `ICP_VOXEL_M=0.01` (1 cm), and estimates normals with `KDTreeSearchParamHybrid(radius=NORMAL_RADIUS_M=0.03, max_nn=30)`. The 1 cm ICP voxel + 3 cm normal radius bound ICP cost by scene extent (not frame count) and give stable point-to-plane normals.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: ICP runs coarse->fine over `ICP_STAGES = ((0.05, 6), (0.02, 12))`: stage 1 with 5 cm max-correspondence distance for 6 iterations, stage 2 with 2 cm for 12 iterations, each chaining the previous transform as init, using `TransformationEstimationPointToPlane`. The accumulated transform T is applied as `refined = T @ c2w_cv`. FITNESS GATE: the refinement is only accepted if `reg.fitness >= ICP_FITNESS_MIN=0.30`; below that it falls back to the raw FK pose `c2w_cv` (trusting forward kinematics when ICP found too few correspondences, e.g. textureless/empty views). This prevents a bad ICP solve from corrupting the seed geometry. The GPU impl mirrors this via `multi_scale_icp` with voxel_sizes `[ICP_VOXEL_M*2, ICP_VOXEL_M]` and the same iteration/distance/fitness constants.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: Global ICP model: bounded accumulator refreshed every 5 frames
STATIC.idea: ICP registers against a GLOBAL model cloud that grows but stays bounded by scene extent. Each non-first frame: after integrating, the source is transformed into the refined frame (`src.transform(refined @ inv(c2w_cv))`) and pushed onto a pending list `_pend`. Every `MODEL_REFRESH_EVERY=5` frames (when `idx % 5 == 0`), all pending sources are merged into `self.model`, the model is re-voxel-downsampled to `ICP_VOXEL_M=0.01`, normals are re-estimated (radius 0.03, max_nn 30), and `_pend` is cleared. This keeps the model from growing unboundedly while preserving full scene coverage for registration, and refreshes normals so point-to-plane stays accurate as the model accumulates.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: `_integrate` builds an Open3D RGBDImage via `create_from_color_and_depth(color, depth, depth_scale=DEPTH_SCALE=1000, depth_trunc=DEPTH_MAX_M=2.0, convert_rgb_to_intensity=False)` and integrates into a `ScalableTSDFVolume(TSDF_VOXEL_M, TSDF_TRUNC_M, ctype)` using the camera intrinsics and the inverse refined pose `inv(c2w_cv)` as the extrinsic. ctype is `RGB8` when WITH_COLOR else `NoColor` (a dummy zero image is supplied when colorless because the Open3D API requires a color arg). depth_trunc=2.0 m means surfaces beyond 2 m are not integrated. This is the source of the truncated-signed-distance volume that finalize extracts the seed from.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: TSDF parameters: voxel, truncation, depth range, scale
STATIC.idea: Load-bearing fusion constants (online_fusion module globals, read at import time): `TSDF_VOXEL_M` defaults to 0.002 m (2 mm) from env `DGS_TSDF_VOXEL_M`; `TSDF_TRUNC_M = 0.008` m (8 mm, ~4x voxel) — the fixed truncation half-width of the signed distance; `DEPTH_SCALE = 1000.0` (uint16 mm -> m); `DEPTH_MIN_M = 0.05` (5 cm near cut for the ICP source); `DEPTH_MAX_M` defaults to 2.0 m from env `DGS_TSDF_DEPTH_MAX_M` — per the module comment only depth in (0.05, 2.0] m is TSDF-integrated, so NO seed gaussians exist past 2 m (bounds the initial reconstruction and excludes far stereo-depth noise; this cap should equal the static model's scene_depth_max_m which masks the same band out of the training loss). The on-disk sensor depth goes to 65 m; the 2 m cap is the pipeline's, not the sensor's.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: Seed builder overrides module globals to 3mm/8mm/stride8
STATIC.idea: `SweepSeedBuilder.start` overrides the online_fusion module globals AFTER import (env/setdefault is too late since they're read at import): `OF.TSDF_VOXEL_M = SEED_VOXEL_M = 0.003` (3 mm), `OF.TSDF_TRUNC_M = SEED_TRUNC_M = 0.008` (8 mm, ~4x the 3 mm voxel — but note 0.008/0.003 = 2.67x, so the inline '~4x voxel' comment is loose; it is the GPU build's same fixed 8 mm), and `OF.ICP_SRC_STRIDE = SEED_ICP_STRIDE = 8` (vs the fusion default 4). The 3 mm voxel MUST match the recorded/fallback build (which sets `DGS_TSDF_VOXEL_M=0.003` via setdefault) because the 2 mm default yields a denser, taller-bbox seed (extra far-surface fragments) that splatfacto can't fit. Stride 8 (vs 4) halves per-keyframe ICP cost while leaving the full-res TSDF integrate untouched, so the seed geometry is unchanged. The recorded/fallback `_build_seed_deferred` runs the SAME module in a CPU subprocess with `DGS_TSDF_VOXEL_M=0.003` and `DGS_FUSION_DEVICE=cpu`.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: CPU: forcing the CPU fusion impl (`DGS_FUSION_DEVICE=cpu`) means the seed build cannot OOM or contend with the shared 16 GB GPU that SAM3D + splatfacto train need; the code also notes the CPU seed fits as-well-or-better than the GPU build. DEFERRED/incremental: instead of fusing all keyframes in one cold GPU subprocess after SAM3D frees the GPU, each kept keyframe is fused on a background CPU thread AS IT ARRIVES during the sweep (and during the SAM3D wait), so at trigger only finalize() remains and it never touches the GPU. 3mm voxel: the coarser 3 mm grid (vs 2 mm default) produces the seed density splatfacto actually fits; finer/denser seeds add far-surface junk that the static fit can't converge on. Truncation 8 mm keeps the SDF band tight (over-large truncation smears the SDF and carves spurious far-edge double surfaces).

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: GPU truncation match (trunc_voxel_multiplier) — why it's computed not defaulted
STATIC.idea: The GPU VoxelBlockGrid impl (used only when DGS_FUSION_DEVICE!=cpu) must explicitly compute `trunc_mult = TSDF_TRUNC_M / TSDF_VOXEL_M` and pass it to `voxel_grid.integrate`, rather than rely on Open3D's default `trunc_voxel_multiplier=8.0`. The default 8.0 gives 8x-voxel truncation (16 mm at 2 mm voxel, 24 mm at 3 mm) — 2-3x larger than the CPU's fixed 8 mm — which over-large truncation smears the SDF along the ray and carves a spurious second zero-crossing at grazing/far edges (the far-edge 'doubling' the CPU path never shows). Setting trunc_mult = TSDF_TRUNC_M/TSDF_VOXEL_M makes GPU truncation identical to the CPU's fixed 8 mm. (SIM live/recorded seed paths force CPU, so this is the consistency contract for the GPU fallback.)

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.topic: finalize(): drain, extract, adaptive downsample, write
STATIC.idea: `SweepSeedBuilder.finalize`: (1) push the `None` sentinel and join the worker thread (timeout 120 s) to drain any keyframes still queued at trigger; (2) if the worker errored or fused 0 frames, return None so the caller falls back to the GPU/CPU subprocess build (`_build_seed_deferred`); (3) call `_fuser.finalize()` which returns the full TSDF point cloud via `ScalableTSDFVolume.extract_point_cloud()`; (4) if non-empty, `adaptive_downsample(pc, last_cam_world)` anchored on the LAST fused camera's world translation (`refined_cv[:3,3]` from the final add_frame); (5) `o3d.io.write_point_cloud` to the PLY and patch transforms.json. `StaticSeedBuilder.finalize` (the non-streaming wrapper) does the equivalent extract + adaptive_downsample + write under `static_scene/`.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: `adaptive_downsample` shrinks the dense fused cloud while preserving detail near the object: points within `NEAR_RADIUS_M=1.0` m of the LAST camera world position are kept at native TSDF density; all farther points are voxel-downsampled to `FAR_VOXEL_M=0.01` m (1 cm). CPU path: `depth = norm(pts - cam)`, split by `depth <= 1.0`, `far_pc.voxel_down_sample(0.01)`, return `near_pc + far_down`; if there are no far points it returns the cloud unchanged. GPU path mirrors this with tensor masks (`dist2 = sq[:,0]+sq[:,1]+sq[:,2]` done as a 3-term elementwise add because Open3D 0.19's CUDA reduction rejects sum(dim=1) on large Float32). Colors and normals are preserved through the split/merge. The anchor is deliberately the LAST viewpoint (the operator's final framing of the object), not the first.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: For recorded datasets (no live per-frame hook), `fuse_recorded_dataset` runs the identical algorithm as a one-shot pass: reads intrinsics + frames from `transforms.json` (sorted by trailing integer in the filename for capture order), and for each frame loads depth TIFF as uint16, zeroes depth where the mask PNG==0 (gripper exclusion), loads RGB with `cv2.imread(...)[:, :, ::-1]` (BGR->RGB), and calls `fuser.add_frame(depth, transform_matrix, rgb)`. Depth is NOT re-filtered here (the live publisher already filters `depth/`). Then finalize() -> adaptive_downsample anchored on the LAST frame's transform translation -> write PLY + patch ply_file_path. It is invoked as a CPU subprocess (`python -m dynamic_gs.utils.online_fusion <static_dir>`) so an Open3D/CUDA teardown abort can't take down the parent. This is the same builder the live path falls back to if the incremental builder fuses nothing.

STATIC.title: TSDF depth seed (point-cloud init)
STATIC.idea: `OnlineFusion.__init__` auto-selects: GPU impl (`_GpuOnlineFusion`, Open3D tensor SLAM VoxelBlockGrid at the configured voxel, 16^3 blocks, 8000 initial blocks growing via hashmap rehash) when `DGS_FUSION_DEVICE` is 'gpu' or ('auto' and CUDA available); otherwise CPU impl (`_CpuOnlineFusion`, legacy ScalableTSDFVolume). Both impls mirror the same ICP stages, fitness gate, model-refresh cadence, and depth band. The SIM seed paths (live SweepSeedBuilder and recorded _build_seed_deferred) BOTH force `DGS_FUSION_DEVICE=cpu`, so the GPU impl is only a fallback in this flow. (A real-HW capture path exists elsewhere via DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / ZED-Mini but is out of scope here; the depth->seed fusion math is identical regardless of camera source since it consumes the same Frame stream.)

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: Static scene training runs natively in-process (no ns-train subprocess) via train_static(scene_model, gset, cameras, batches). It drives the GRAD render of an inner nerfstudio SplatfactoModel that SceneModel wraps (WRAP-not-BE): scene_model.model.get_outputs(cam) is the gradient path, distinct from SceneModel.render()/_render() which are no_grad. Each step: set scene_model.model.step=step, model.train(), opt.zero_grad_all(), forward get_outputs(cam), loss = sum(scene_model.get_loss_dict(out,batch).values()), scaler.scale(loss).backward(), then opt.optimizer_scaler_step_all(scaler) + scaler.update(). The inner model's gauss_params ARE GaussianSet's tensors (same Python objects, no copy), so count/identity surgery + rebind() re-point the optimizer in place. Cameras and batches come from load_static_cameras (per-keyframe), gset is built freelist=False (static = exact reallocating path).

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: _build_optimizers builds a nerfstudio Optimizers over scene_model.param_groups() (the 6 gauss params; camera_opt group is absent because mode=off). LRs come from _STATIC_LRS = {means:0.0, features_dc:0.0025, features_rest:0.0025/20.0 (=1.25e-4), opacities:0.05, scales:0.005, quats:0.001, camera_opt:1e-3}; each group gets AdamOptimizerConfig(lr=..., eps=1e-15), scheduler=None. means is forced to means_lr (passed as 0.0 by static_fuse). The built Optimizers is assigned to model.optimizers AND model._optimizers_wrapper so GaussianSet.rebind() after the opacity-purge cull + Phase-0b inserts re-points THESE same param groups (o.param_groups[0]['params']=[new tensor]; o.state.clear()). The camera_opt:1e-3 entry in _STATIC_LRS is effectively dead because camera_optimizer mode=off emits no 'camera_opt' param group.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.topic: Invariant: means LR = 0 (positions locked on seed)
STATIC.idea: means optimizer LR is hard-set to 0 two ways: _STATIC_LRS['means']=0.0 / means_lr=0.0 at build, then enforce_phase_lr() is called immediately after _build_optimizers to re-assert it (for phase=='static' it sets only the 'means' group's pg['lr']=0.0). This is the ONLY means-lock in the static phase — there is NO means.grad hook in static (the dynamic-phase register_hook(lambda g: zeros_like(g)) is bound only when phase=='dynamic'). Effect: Adam never moves the seed positions even though .grad is nonzero, keeping every Gaussian pinned to the geometrically-correct TSDF-fused seed PLY (depth_camera_init_points.ply); only color (features_dc/_rest), opacities, scales, quats train. Letting means drift under photometric loss would smear the output since the seed is already ICP-fused depth.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: SceneModel builds SplatfactoModelConfig(sh_degree, random_init=False, num_downscales, resolution_schedule) WITHOUT overriding camera_optimizer, so it takes SplatfactoModelConfig's default field CameraOptimizerConfig(mode='off'). With mode=='off', CameraOptimizer.get_param_groups asserts len(params)==0 and adds NO 'camera_opt' group, and get_loss_dict adds no camera-opt residual. Poses are therefore NOT optimized during static training. WHY: transforms.json already holds ICP-refined OpenGL c2w poses (sub-mm residual); leaving pose-opt on would drift cameras visibly and smear the scene. This is enforced structurally by the config default, not by enforce_phase_lr (which only zeroes gauss-param LRs).

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: train_static signature defaults mixed_precision=True (fp16 autocast + GradScaler), but the production caller static_fuse.train_fuse_and_export passes mixed_precision=False, so the actual sim static fit runs fp32: ctx=nullcontext() (no torch.autocast), GradScaler enabled=False. WHY (verified in code comment, not metric-from-memory): the custom gsplat rasterizer backward + SSIM lose too much precision under fp16 autocast; the static_fuse comment cites measured ~17-18 dB masked PSNR at fp16 vs ~26-27 dB at fp32, and the verify/ probes (_probe_static_quality, train_psnr_probe) pass mixed_precision=False to reproduce this. Note seed tensors are also cast to float32 in SceneModel.__init__ (sxyz/srgb = torch.as_tensor(..., dtype=torch.float32)).

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.topic: GradScaler step that skips grad-less optimizers
STATIC.idea: The step uses opt.optimizer_scaler_step_all(scaler) (nerfstudio's multi-optimizer scaler step), NOT a single scaler.step(opt). The code comment explains this skips optimizers with no grad (means LR=0, camera_opt off) because calling scaler.step() on a grad-less optimizer repeatedly corrupts the GradScaler's per-optimizer state and silently skips real steps; the comment cites this as 17 dB vs 27 dB. The per-step sequence is zero_grad_all -> backward -> optimizer_scaler_step_all(scaler) -> scaler.update().

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: Static count is mutated surgically (GaussianSet cull/insert), NOT by Splatfacto's clone/split/prune. SceneModel.__init__ tries to import dynamic_gs.utils.no_refine_strategy.NoRefineStrategy; if present (_HAVE_NOREFINE True) it sets self.model.strategy = NoRefineStrategy() and strategy_state = strategy.initialize_state(scene_scale=1.0) (a no-op post-backward), else falls back silently. So no Splatfacto densify thresholds (grad2d, cull-alpha, cull-scale, split/dup intervals) ever fire during static train. This is why the during-training scale RESET is needed: Splatfacto's own prune never runs to remove oversized splats.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.topic: Number of train steps + early stop
STATIC.idea: num_steps defaults to cfg.static_train.num_steps = STATIC_NUM_STEPS = 500. Keyframes are visited round-robin i = step % n (shuffle-free, deterministic). Photometric early-stop: track an EMA ema = 0.9*ema + 0.1*loss; once step >= early_stop_min_steps (=100), increment hits when ema < early_stop_loss (=0.02) else reset hits=0; break when hits >= early_stop_patience (=8). Returns stopped_at (the step it stopped, else 500) and records tm.gauge('static_train_steps', stopped_at). After the loop: scene_model.model.step = 30000 (so all SH bands are active at render time for Phase-0b) and model.eval(). early_stop_loss=0 disables early-stop (used by verify probes).

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: Production builds SceneModel(..., num_downscales=2, resolution_schedule=15). Splatfacto._get_downscale_factor() returns (when training) 2**max(num_downscales - step//resolution_schedule, 0): so steps 0-14 -> factor 4 (1/4 res), 15-29 -> factor 2 (1/2 res), step>=30 -> factor 1 (full res). scene_model.model.step=step drives this each iteration. The GT image, depth, and loss mask are all downscaled to match via _downscale_if_required. At inference (training False) the factor is always 1. SceneModel's own defaults are num_downscales=0/resolution_schedule=100 (full-res always) for render/dynamic; the coarse-to-fine is a static-train-only choice.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: loss = sum of SceneModel.get_loss_dict(out,batch).values(), which delegates to SplatfactoModel.get_loss_dict. main_loss = (1 - ssim_lambda)*Ll1 + ssim_lambda*simloss with ssim_lambda=0.2 (where simloss = 1 - SSIM, so 0.8*L1 + 0.2*(1-SSIM)). gt is composited onto outputs['background'] first. If batch has a 'mask', it is downscaled to match and BOTH gt and pred are multiplied by it (masked regions zeroed) before L1/SSIM. scale_reg is 0 here (use_scale_regularization defaults False). camera-opt and mcmc/bilateral loss terms are absent (camera_opt off; strategy not mcmc). SSIM is pytorch_msssim SSIM(data_range=1.0, channel=3, size_average=True).

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.topic: Loss mask = robot/keep mask AND depth-cap
STATIC.idea: SceneModel.get_loss_dict first applies a mask_provider: static_fuse sets _depth_keep, which returns ((depth > 0.05) & (depth < dmax)).float() with dmax = cfg.depth.scene_depth_max_m (default 2.0 m, validated == depth_max_m). This depth-cap mask is ANDed (element-wise multiply) into any existing batch['mask'] (the per-frame keep/robot mask loaded from masks/), and the combined mask is passed down to Splatfacto's get_loss_dict which zeroes both gt and pred there. Purpose: the loss never fits color to far/no-return pixels (>=2 m or <=5 cm) or to masked-out robot pixels.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.topic: Gazebo-sky background in render AND loss
STATIC.idea: _GAZEBO_SKY = (0.86, 0.92, 1.0) (Invariant #6). SceneModel.__init__ calls model.set_background(tensor(_GAZEBO_SKY)) and then OVERRIDES model._get_background_color = lambda: _sky.to(device). WHY the override: Splatfacto's default background_color='random' makes the stock _get_background_color() return torch.rand(3) WHILE self.training, which would train the static scene against a random photometric bias; the override forces the fixed sky even during training. The same sky is composited into gt (composite_with_background) and is the render's background fill (outputs['background']). Matching the sim's actual sky avoids a constant photometric bias the renderer would otherwise compensate for via opacity tweaks at silhouettes.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: _shrink_oversized_scales runs every scale_clamp_every_n steps (cfg.budget.static_scale_clamp_every_n=10, gated by (step+1)%every_n==0) but only once step >= scale_clamp_start_step (default 60). For each Gaussian whose largest WORLD axis exp(log_max) > trigger_m (static_scale_clamp_max_m=0.05 m), it shifts ALL THREE log-scales by the SAME amount (log_max - log_reset) so the largest axis becomes reset_m (static_scale_reset_value_m=0.01 m) — shape preserved, NOT a per-axis clamp, in-place s.sub_(shift) under no_grad. start_step=60 (~30 past the full-res step 30) keeps the clamp from firing during the coarse 1/4->1/2 warmup. Config validates reset (0.01) < clamp_max (0.05) to avoid boundary re-trip. Needed because densify/prune is off so Splatfacto never removes the far-band smear splats itself.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: load_seed_ply reads static_scene/depth_camera_init_points.ply via Open3D -> xyz[N,3] float32 + rgb[N,3] in [0,1] (grey 0.5 fallback if no colors). SceneModel passes (sxyz, srgb*255 if max<=1) as seed_points to SplatfactoModelConfig(random_init=False), so Splatfacto.populate_modules sets: means = Parameter(seed xyz) directly; scales = log(mean distance to 3 nearest neighbors) per point (k_nearest_sklearn, k=3), repeated over 3 axes; quats = random unit quats; opacities = logit(0.1) for all; features_dc/_rest from RGB2SH(rgb/255) into SH band 0 with higher bands zeroed (dim_sh = num_sh_bases(sh_degree)). sh_degree defaults to 3 via getattr(cfg.static_train,'sh_degree',3) (no sh_degree field in config). aabb_scale=4.0 sizes the SceneBox to 4x the seed extent (min 1 m).

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.topic: Keyframe selection feeding the train loop
STATIC.idea: load_static_cameras builds per-keyframe (nerfstudio Cameras(1), batch{image,depth_image,mask}) from static_scene/transforms.json. A greedy ORB-SLAM-style keyframe filter (trans_thresh_m=0.02, rot_thresh_deg=20.0) drops a frame if it is within BOTH 2 cm translation AND 20 deg rotation of any kept frame (rotation via arccos(0.5*(trace(R^T Rk)-1))). Images: BGR PNG -> RGB float [0,1]; depth: uint16-mm TIFF * 1e-3 -> metres; mask: grayscale>0 -> float [H,W,1]. Poses are OpenGL c2w (transform_matrix [:3,:4]); intrinsics fx/fy/cx/cy and W/H from the json header. These cameras/batches are the round-robin training set for train_static.

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.idea: After train_static returns, static_fuse calls purge_low_opacity(gset, cfg.budget.static_opacity_purge_threshold=0.05): snapshot the scene, find rows where sigmoid(opacities) < 0.05, and gset.cull(low) (cull takes DROP indices). This one-shot removes the faded/under-opacity Gaussians the photometric fit drove toward transparent, before the SAM3D Phase-0b fusion runs. The cull triggers GaussianSet surgery -> SceneModel.rebind() re-points the optimizer param groups and re-asserts phase LR, which is why the Optimizers object is stored on model.optimizers (so it survives the count change).

STATIC.title: Splatfacto scene training
STATIC.topic: Note: real-HW branches out of scope
STATIC.idea: DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini real-hardware branches exist elsewhere (ros_mask.py camera-mount FK reparenting, live publisher intrinsics), but they do not affect the static Splatfacto train path described here — the static fit consumes already-captured static_scene/ images, depth, masks, transforms.json and the TSDF seed PLY identically for sim and real.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: train_fuse_and_export is the static-fuse driver: (1) load_seed_ply reads the TSDF seed `static_scene/depth_camera_init_points.ply` via Open3D into xyz[N,3] + rgb[N,3] in [0,1] (grey 0.5 fallback if no colors); (2) build a SceneModel(phase='static', num_downscales=2, resolution_schedule=15) seeded with those tensors and bind a GaussianSet(freelist=False) sharing one threading.RLock; (3) load_static_cameras builds per-keyframe Cameras+batches from static_scene/transforms.json; (4) train_static runs the photometric fit with means_lr=0.0 and mixed_precision=False (fp32 mandatory — fp16 autocast measurably ruins the fit); (5) at the train->fuse boundary call the optional on_fuse() callback (lets a UI flip train->done / fuse->doing, wrapped in try/except pass); (6) purge_low_opacity; (7) run_phase0b_native; (8) save_warm_cache -> static_state.pt. With return_scene=True it returns (path, sm, gset, lock) to carry the in-memory scene straight to the dynamic loop (no reload).

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: Before training, set_mask_provider installs _depth_keep: per batch it returns a float mask of pixels with sensor depth in the OPEN interval (0.05, scene_depth_max_m) — `(d > 0.05) & (d < dmax)`, so the upper bound is EXCLUSIVE, not inclusive (scene_depth_max_m default 2.0 m, must equal depth_max_m by config validation), else None when dmax<=0 or no depth. This excludes far/no-return pixels so the photometric loss never fits color to background, keeping the trained scene that Phase-0b queries clean.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: purge_low_opacity runs once between train and Phase-0b: snapshot the scene, compute sigmoid(opacities) and gather row indices where activated opacity < static_opacity_purge_threshold (default 0.05), and pass those DROP indices to gset.cull (cull takes the indices to delete, not to keep). Returns 0 immediately if threshold<=0. This drops near-transparent floaters left by training so they don't pollute the registration target or get tagged as object.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: Static GaussianSet is built freelist=False (exact reallocating cull/insert, capacity==count). run_phase0b_native asserts `not gset._freelist` loudly because Phase-0b's slab/subset indices and the Stage-C instance-id scatter assume STABLE row indices across per-object inserts; a free-list swap-remove would reorder rows and write instance ids onto the wrong rows. Phase-0b dirs (dynamic_scene/initialization_artifacts and .../initialization_debug) are mkdir'd up front because a from-live dataset lacks them and the first correspondence-plot write would otherwise FileNotFoundError.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: load_anchor_for_fusion rebuilds the EXACT frame the SAM3 masks were segmented on from an AnchorRef: reads pose JSON (4x4, takes [:3,:4] as OpenGL c2w) and intrinsics JSON (fx,fy,cx,cy,w,h) into a single nerfstudio Cameras(PERSPECTIVE) with metadata cam_idx=0; reads rgb via cv2 IMREAD_COLOR (BGR) and flips to RGB uint8 (used for back-projected point colors); reads depth via IMREAD_UNCHANGED as float32 METRES (already metres on disk, no scale — the anchor depth.tiff is written as float32 m). Returns (camera, image_uint8, depth_m). This is the registration's camera/depth/rgb so the mask-to-world back-projection is in the same frame as the masks.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: run_phase0b_native iterates zip(sam3_objects, sam3d_results); object obj_idx gets instance_id = obj_idx+1 (1..K). For EACH object it regenerates a fresh render+info via scene_model.get_outputs_with_info(camera) under the lock, because a prior object's insert() changed N so the projected-gaussian info must be rebuilt. Objects with falsy sam3d_out, failed PLY load, or <3 back-projected target points are skipped (`continue`). The object mask PNG is thresholded at >127, and nearest-interpolated to render H/W if sizes differ.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: load_sam3d_gaussian_ply reads the SAM3D Gaussian PLY vertex x/y/z into source_points[N,3] and, if f_dc_0/1/2 present, decodes SH band-0 via SH2RGB clamped to [0,1] for source_colors (else grey 0.5). load_sam3d_rotation_wxyz reads the pose sidecar's `rotation` (must be a finite 4-vector quaternion wxyz, else ValueError). In register_and_fuse, _apply_sam3d_rotation_init converts the wxyz quat to a 3x3 matrix, applies it to source_points (points @ R), maps PyTorch3D->NS-camera axes via SAM3D_P3D_TO_NS_CAMERA = diag(-1,1,-1), then into world by `@ c2w_rot.T`. This pre-orients the canonical SAM3D cloud using SAM3D's own predicted rotation before scale/centroid alignment.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.topic: registration TARGET: existing-object subset (CPD/NDP fallback target)
STATIC.idea: get_existing_object_subset (port of StaticGSModel._get_existing_object_subset) builds the frontmost visible scene-gaussian subset under the object mask: project all gaussians via gsplat info (extract_projected_centers_and_radii -> centers_2d, radii, depths); RAISE if info lacks depths. Candidate filter = finite center/radius/depth & radius>0 & in-bounds & mask[cy,cx]>0.5. Then keep the frontmost gaussian per pixel using np.lexsort((cand_depths, pixel_ids)) where pixel_ids is the PRIMARY (last) key and top_k_per_pixel=1 (hardcoded; loosening leaks the planar table geometry). Then a depth-tolerance visibility pass: target_spacing = median mean-kNN(k<=3) of the candidate means, depth_tol = max(0.008, 5.0*target_spacing), and a greedy-MAX search over multipliers (1.0,1.5,2.0,3.0,5.0,8.0) keeping gaussians whose |projected_depth - sampled_render_depth| <= mult*depth_tol, early-breaking when kept >= max(3, 0.50*n_before). Finally half-downsample by linspace pick (keep max(3, count//2)) if >=6 survive. Colors = features_dc*0.28209479177387814+0.5 (SH2RGB band-0). Returns (indices, means, colors).

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: When anchor depth is available (sim path always), the PREFERRED registration target replaces the gaussian subset: backproject_mask_to_world projects the object mask through the anchor depth into world points+colors. It resizes mask to depth H/W (NEAREST), keeps pixels with depth>1e-4, scrubs depth outliers via MAD (keep |z-med| < 5.0*1.4826*MAD ~ 7.4 MAD, permissive to preserve real extent), then a local near-surface filter (max_object_slope_deg=70, window = max(7, odd(round(0.012*min(H,W))))): builds a minimum_filter depth field and drops masked pixels farther behind the local min than a 70deg-tilted surface could account for ((win//2)*(z/fx)*tan(70deg)) — removing silhouette-edge depth bleed onto the table. Back-projects in OpenGL camera frame (x=(xs-cx)/fx*z, y=-(ys-cy)/fy*z, z=-z) then to world via c2w R,t. If <3 target points, the object is skipped.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: register_and_fuse_sam3d_object computes the initial similarity placement before any refinement: source_diag = _bbox_diagonal(source), target_diag = _bbox_diagonal(target) (robust 5-95 percentile extent norm when >=50 points, else min-max), base_scale = target_diag / max(source_diag, 1e-6), and chosen_scale = base_scale. Centroids use _centroid (trimmed mean of points inside the 5-95 percentile band when >=50 points). scaled_source = target_centroid + chosen_scale*(source - source_centroid). This isotropic bbox-scale + centroid translation places and sizes the canonical SAM3D cloud onto the real target before the registration backend solves only the residual. Robust stats exist because back-projected mask boundaries include depth outliers that would otherwise blow up bbox/centroid (constants _ROBUST_PCT_LOW=5, _ROBUST_PCT_HIGH=95, _ROBUST_MIN_POINTS=50).

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
