STATIC.idea: After the rigid init, median NN spacing is measured on both clouds (_median_nn_distance via Open3D compute_nearest_neighbor_distance, median of finite positive distances, floor 1e-3), and voxel_size = max(3.0*max(target_spacing, source_spacing), 1e-3). Both scaled_source and target are voxel_down_sampled at that size so the registration backend operates on a uniform-density, deduplicated cloud (falls back to the original cloud if downsample empties it).

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: registration_backend default is 'ndp' (config.segmentation.sam3d_registration_backend='ndp'). The NDP branch leaves similarity_transform=identity (the rigid init is already baked into scaled_source) and calls deform_source_to_target(scaled_source, target_points) to NON-RIGIDLY warp the full source onto the accurate target; the deformed cloud `ndp_warped_full` directly becomes aligned_points (overriding the similarity path). deform_source_to_target fits a Deformation_Pyramid (motion Sim3, euler rotation, depth=3, width=128, m=9, k0=-8) optimizing per-level Adam (lr=0.01, up to 500 iters/level) on a 6000-point random subsample of each cloud, minimizing symmetric truncated Chamfer (torch.cdist min both directions) plus w_reg=1.0 BCE pulling the per-point nonrigidity gate toward 0 (rigid) for levels>0; early-stops on loss<1e-4 or break_threshold_ratio=0.001 relative-change hit max_break_count=15 times. Centers source/target before optimizing and re-adds target centroid; warps the FULL cloud through the fitted pyramid at the end. seed=0 deterministic.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: registration_backend='cpd' runs _run_probreg_similarity_refinement: probreg CPD rigid registration (tf_type_name='rigid') with update_scale=True, use_color=True, w=0.5, maxiter=70, tol=1e-2 on the downsampled clouds (source pre-transformed by the identity init). It composes the recovered probreg scale*rot+t into a 4x4 (_compose_similarity_transform) onto similarity_transform; aligned_points = scaled_source @ that transform. Returns identity if probreg missing or <3 points either side. Used when NDP non-rigid warp is not wanted.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: registration_backend='teaser' runs three composed stages on the downsampled clouds: (1) _run_teaser_similarity_refinement = color-aware FPFH descriptors (concat L2-normed FPFH*(1-color_weight) + L2-normed RGB*color_weight) + mutual-NN matching + TEASER++ GNC-TLS solve with estimate_scaling=True, noise_bound default 0.02, cbar2=1.0, rotation_gnc_factor=1.4, rotation_max_iterations=100; (2) _run_teaser_reproject_refinement = Euclidean mutual-NN correspondences within 3.0*voxel_size + second TEASER solve (noise_bound 0.005); (3) _run_icp_polish = point-to-plane ICP (max_corr=2.0*voxel_size, 50 iters) that PRE-APPLIES the scaled init then runs identity-init ICP and ACCEPTS only if it strictly increases inlier count, or ties count without worsening RMSE (count+RMSE guard prevents ICP-sliding on symmetric/low-texture objects). Each stage no-ops if teaserpp/open3d missing or <3 correspondences. Unknown backend raises ValueError. Note: the call-site default color_weight is 0.0, and stages 2/3 are gated by enable_reproject/enable_post_icp (both default True).

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: After the backend, similarity_scale = chosen_scale * _extract_isotropic_scale(similarity_transform) (mean of the per-column norms of the 3x3). aligned_points = ndp_warped_full (NDP) OR scaled_source @ similarity_transform (rigid). kept_points/kept_colors = aligned_points/colors (dedup_threshold=0.0, existing-splat pruning deferred to the pipeline's cull stages). It also composes the full canonical-SAM3D-frame -> world 4x4 = similarity_transform @ T(target_centroid - chosen_scale*source_centroid) @ S(chosen_scale), stored as canonical_to_world_4x4 (the mesh_to_world FoundationPose needs). A correspondence plot + source/target/aligned reference PLYs are written to debug_dir/artifact_dir under output_stem `static0_obj_{obj_idx:02d}_sam3d`. similarity_correspondence_threshold = max(2.0*median_nn(target_down), 1e-3).

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: Back in run_phase0b_native, cull_pts/cull_colors = result.kept_points/colors. Stage A removes aligned SAM3D points that duplicate the existing visible surface: get_object_mask_slab_indices builds e_idx_cull (in-mask gaussians whose projected depth is within CULL_DEPTH_TOL_M=0.015 of the rendered front surface), and if those >=2 gaussians exist, tau = max(estimate_spacing(e_pts)*CULL_STRENGTH, TAU_FLOOR_M) with CULL_STRENGTH=1.3 and TAU_FLOOR_M=0.003; a sklearn NearestNeighbors(k=1) drops every aligned point whose nearest existing point is <= tau. estimate_spacing = median of per-point mean-kNN(k<=3) distance (RNG seed 42 subsample to 50,000 max). This avoids stacking new gaussians on top of already-trained surface.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: Stage B drops aligned points that lie in FRONT of the trusted real depth surface (between camera and object). cull_points_in_front projects target_pts_np (the back-projected real depth) into the image to build a front-surface depth buffer (np.minimum.at + minimum_filter with radius_px=2, window 2*radius+1=5), then drops any inserted point whose forward depth z < surface_depth - band_m, with IN_FRONT_BAND_M=0.0; points with no surface along their ray (outside silhouette) are kept. MAX_RADIUS_M=0.02 caps the Stage-C proxy/target match radii. This removes hallucinated SAM3D geometry floating ahead of the true surface.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: _build_insert_tensors converts survivor xyz/rgb into GaussTensors: means=xyz; per-point isotropic log-scales = log(mean-kNN(k<=3) spacing, clamped >=1e-6) repeated over 3 axes (or 1e-3 if a single point); features_dc = (rgb-0.5)/0.28209479177387814 (RGB2SH band-0); features_rest = zeros of width gset.sh_rest_dim (auto-coerced by GaussTensors.validate); quats = identity (w=1); opacities = logit(0.1) = log(0.1/0.9). So inserted object gaussians start at 0.1 opacity, neighbor-spaced scale, identity orientation.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: Survivors are inserted via gset.insert(tensors, object_flag=0.0, instance_id=instance_id). insert (freelist=False path) concatenates the new param rows and appends identity-buffer tails with id_vals {object_flags:0.0, object_instance_ids:instance_id, inserted_flags:1.0} (sam3d_init_target_flags stays 0 per Invariant #8), assigns fresh monotonic gauss_uids, rebinds the wrapped SplatfactoModel, and returns the new row index range. So every inserted SAM3D-object gaussian is automatically tagged with its instance id (1..K) and inserted_flags=1; object_flags stays 0 (D0 selection sets it later in the dynamic phase). If no survivors, inserted is an empty index tensor.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.topic: Stage C — instance-id flag propagation onto existing rows
STATIC.idea: Stage C tags already-trained scene gaussians that belong to this object so the original surface (not just inserts) carries the instance id. e_idx_flag = slab indices at the looser FLAG_DEPTH_TOL_M=0.02. Eligible existing rows = those whose object_instance_ids is 0 OR already == this instance_id. For each eligible candidate, NearestNeighbors(k=1) to the aligned proxy points (radius proxy_r = min(0.02, max(0.003, 1.5*estimate_spacing(proxy)))) OR to the existing-subset means (radius target_r = min(0.02, max(0.002, 6.0*estimate_spacing(existing_means)))); match = near_proxy | near_target. Matched candidates are scattered into a full-length (==gset.count) bool mask and written via gset.write_instance_ids(full, instance_id). This runs only if e_idx_flag nonempty and result.kept_point_count>0.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: Per object a manifest[instance_id] dict records object_index, existing/sam3d_pre_cull/culled/culled_in_front/inserted/flagged counts, cull_tau_m, instance_count (count of rows with this id), and registration_backend; written to phase0_manifest.json in artifact_dir. After the loop, total_tagged = count of rows with object_instance_ids>0; if 0 it RAISES RuntimeError ('Phase-0b fused 0 object Gaussians ... nothing to track') — every object can silently drop (empty SAM3D, PLY fail, <3 target points) and without this guard the failure would only surface later in the tracker with an opaque error.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: save_warm_cache writes static_scene/static_state.pt (DEFAULT_CACHE_NAME) from gset.state_dict() — the SSOT: all 6 gauss params keyed gauss_params.<name> plus the 4 identity buffers (object_instance_ids, inserted_flags, object_flags, sam3d_init_target_flags), only the [:count] live rows, on CPU. The blob also stores num_points, config_fingerprint(cfg) (loud-on-drift warning at reload), and layout='dynamic_gs2.v1'. The dynamic phase warm-loads this exact post-fusion scene (no retrain) via load_warm_cache/build_loaded_scene, so the instance-id tagging from Phase-0b is what the tracker keys on.

STATIC.title: Phase-0b: place & fuse the 3D object into the scene
STATIC.idea: A real-hardware branch exists (DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini reparenting the camera FK in ros_mask.py) but does not alter the Phase-0b fuse math itself; the anchor pose/intrinsics/depth that load_anchor_for_fusion consumes simply come from the real rig instead of Gazebo. The registration, scale, cull, and instance-id tagging code paths described above are identical for sim and real.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.idea: Every heavy model is wrapped in a Handle class exposing the SAME async-prewarm lifecycle so the static orchestrator never imports a model directly: prewarm() = load the model on a daemon bg thread and return immediately (non-blocking); wait_ready() = block until that bg load finished; release() = free the model's VRAM (unload it); plus a model-specific inference method (segment/generate/tracker/handle). Each Handle owns a threading.Thread + a threading.Event(_loaded): prewarm() spawns the thread once (guarded by `if self._thread is not None: return`, so it is idempotent), the thread's _go() does the actual load then sets the Event in a finally block, and wait_ready() does self._loaded.wait(). This decouples the load (which can overlap the operator sweep) from the use (at the trigger), so heavy import+checkpoint cost is hidden, not paid on the critical path. NOTE: XFeatHandle differs slightly — it uses _thread.join() (not an Event) plus a threading.Lock for single-construction, and its prewarm guard is `if self._thread is not None or self._tracker is not None`.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: Timing ledger sink for bg loads
STATIC.idea: Because prewarm() is non-blocking, a timer wrapped around the call would only measure dispatch, not the real load. So model_loader holds a module-global _TM set via set_timing_ledger(tm) (called by run_static at static-phase start), and each bg _go() calls _record_load(name, seconds) AFTER the load returns, which does _TM.record_ms('load.<name>', seconds*1000.0) inside a try/except. FastSAM/SAM3D get their load-seconds directly from the worker's load_fastsam()/load_sam3d() return value; XFeat times time.time()-t0 around _build(); AnySplat spawns a watcher thread that blocks on wait_ready() then stamps load.anysplat. This is the only way the opaque subprocess/worker loads get a real wall-time recorded as load.{fastsam,sam3d,anysplat,xfeat}.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: _SharedSamWorker: one process shared by FastSAM + SAM3D
STATIC.idea: FastSamHandle and Sam3dHandle do NOT each spawn their own subprocess; build_registry creates ONE _SharedSamWorker and passes it to both handles. _SharedSamWorker.client() does a thread-safe lazy spawn (threading.Lock; returns the cached self._client if already up, or None if a prior spawn failed) of a single dynamic_gs.utils.sam_worker.SamWorkerClient bound to conda env 'sam3_dynamic_gs'. Both FastSAM and SAM3D thus load into the SAME persistent process (one spawn, models loaded on demand into one CUDA context). Registry stores it under key '_sam_worker' so the orchestrator can close() it after fusion to 100%-free both models' VRAM at once. If spawn raises, it sets _spawn_failed=True and prints a fallback message, and every handle method degrades to the per-call subprocess path (never worse than before).

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: CONDA_PREFIX patch before spawning the SAM worker
STATIC.idea: Before constructing SamWorkerClient, _SharedSamWorker.client() does os.environ.setdefault('CONDA_PREFIX', os.path.expanduser('~/miniconda3/envs/sam3_dynamic_gs')). This is load-bearing because the Fast-SAM3D inference module does `os.environ['CUDA_HOME'] = os.environ['CONDA_PREFIX']` at import, and the mode scripts launch via bare env-python (CONDA_PREFIX unset) which would KeyError in the worker. SamWorkerClient spawns with os.environ.copy() so the worker inherits the set value. The worker itself runs in the sam3 env, so pinning CONDA_PREFIX to that env's prefix is correct.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: Serial implication of the shared worker (JSON-over-pipe, one request at a time)
STATIC.idea: The shared SamWorkerClient is a single subprocess.Popen with stdin=PIPE/stdout=PIPE, text mode (bufsize=1), communicating one JSON object per line: client writes `{cmd,...}\n`, worker writes JSON response lines. _request() checks the process is alive (poll()) then writes/flushes the request on stdin and loops readline() on the single stdout, skipping non-dict / no-'status' noise lines until it gets the response dict, so calls are inherently SERIAL — FastSAM and SAM3D cannot run (or load) truly concurrently in this one process; a request must complete before the next is serviced. This is exactly why VRAM scheduling matters: the two models share one process AND one GPU context, so the orchestrator must sequence which is resident when (load SAM3D alone during sweep, FastSAM only right before segment, unload each promptly).

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.idea: FastSamHandle.prewarm() spins a bg thread that calls worker.client().load_fastsam() and records load.fastsam. segment(image_path,text_prompt,output_dir,output_stem,**filter_kwargs) first wait_ready()s, then if the worker is live calls c.fastsam_infer(...) (warm in-worker inference), else (worker None OR infer raised) falls back to dynamic_gs.utils.fastsam_segmentation.run_fastsam_subprocess with sam3_conda_env='sam3_dynamic_gs'. release() calls c.unload_fastsam() to free FastSAM's VRAM from the shared worker. So FastSAM is the lightweight 2D text segmenter (FastSAM+CLIP) that produces the object masks consumed by SAM3D.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.idea: Sam3dHandle (constructed with no_trim=bool(cfg.segmentation.sam3d_no_trim)) prewarm()s by bg-threading worker.client().load_sam3d() (records load.sam3d). generate(render_image_path, object_mask_paths, output_dir, output_stems, depth_path, intrinsics_path) wait_ready()s then calls c.sam3d_infer(...) passing image_dir=output_dir, or falls back to dynamic_gs.utils.sam3d.run_sam3d_multi_object_subprocess with the identical args. release() calls c.unload_sam3d() to free SAM3D's VRAM for the downstream TSDF seed + splatfacto. SAM3D is the heavy 3D-object generator (Fast-SAM3D); it consumes FastSAM's masks + the anchor render (+optional depth/intrinsics) to produce the per-object 3D results fused in Phase-0b.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.idea: AnysplatPrewarmHandle wraps dynamic_ff_backends.AnysplatHandle(device, conda_env='anysplat_dynamic_gs') — a PERSISTENT subprocess worker, not in-process. prewarm() calls the inner handle's prewarm() (spawn+load+self-warm on its own bg thread) and additionally launches a tiny watcher thread that blocks on wait_ready() and stamps load.anysplat. handle() returns the live inner AnysplatHandle for the dynamic loop to adopt directly (no CPU-park API — it is spawned-or-not, GPU-resident once up); release() closes it. AnySplat is the feedforward decoder for the dynamic phase only.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.idea: XFeatHandle wraps dynamic_gs2.dynamic_track.XFeatTracker (XFeat+LighterGlue), built in-process (no subprocess) on a bg thread during the static phase so the dynamic loop starts warm. prewarm() bg-threads _build() (guarded by `if self._thread is not None or self._tracker is not None: return` so it's idempotent; _build itself uses a threading.Lock so _tracker is constructed once); wait_ready() joins the thread then builds lazily if it still hasn't. tracker() returns the built tracker. release() is a no-op (`...`) because XFeat is tiny and reused every dynamic tick, so it stays resident for the live loop. It is constructed with cfg.tracker and cfg.pose_filter.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.idea: build_registry(cfg, device, *, want_anysplat=True, want_xfeat=True) constructs a dict ALWAYS containing '_sam_worker' (the shared worker), 'fastsam' (FastSamHandle), and 'sam3d' (Sam3dHandle with no_trim=bool(cfg.segmentation.sam3d_no_trim)). It conditionally adds 'anysplat' only if want_anysplat and 'xfeat' only if want_xfeat. run_static passes want_anysplat=(prewarm_dynamic and ff_enabled) and want_xfeat=prewarm_dynamic, so a --no-ff or static-only run never even instantiates the AnySplat worker (avoids spawning its VRAM-heavy worker that would never be adopted or freed). This is the single place all model handles are created.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: Four-conda-env architecture (which model in which env)
STATIC.idea: Each heavy model runs in a dedicated conda env, selected at handle/worker construction: the shared SAM worker (FastSAM + SAM3D) runs in 'sam3_dynamic_gs' (default conda_env on _SharedSamWorker, FastSamHandle, Sam3dHandle); AnySplat runs in 'anysplat_dynamic_gs' (default on AnysplatPrewarmHandle, forwarded to dynamic_ff_backends.AnysplatHandle); XFeat runs in-process in the main 'dynamic_gs' env (no subprocess). The fourth env, the ROS publisher env ('dynamic_gs_ros'), is owned by the live-bridge source, not model_loader. SamWorkerClient.__init__ resolves the env python directly (~/miniconda3/envs/<conda_env>/bin/python) and prepends that env's lib to LD_LIBRARY_PATH, bypassing `conda run`.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: VRAM schedule step 1 — SAM3D loads ALONE during the sweep
STATIC.idea: At static-phase start the orchestrator prewarms ONLY reg['sam3d'] (in tm.stage('sweep.sam3d_load')); AnySplat, XFeat, and the gsplat-backward warm are deliberately NOT started yet. Rationale grounded in the code comment: SAM3D is the largest single load, so giving it the GPU/CPU to itself lets its load fully hide under the operator's sweep; loading the dynamic models concurrently would contend with the SAM3D load and stretch it. FastSAM is also not prewarmed here — it loads lazily right before segment.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: VRAM schedule step 2 — FastSAM loads ONLY right before segment, then releases immediately
STATIC.idea: Inside tm.stage('trigger.fastsam_segment') the orchestrator calls reg['fastsam'].prewarm() then wait_ready() (synchronous load) immediately before static_segment.segment(...) — NOT at sweep-start. Reason in code comment: FastSAM resident during SAM3D's load peak would OOM the 16 GB card. After segment, reg['fastsam'].release() is called on BOTH paths: on the 0-objects error path (before raising the retry RuntimeError) and on the success path (so FastSAM is not held idle through the SAM3D inference). So FastSAM's residency window is minimized to [load -> segment -> unload].

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: VRAM schedule step 3 — SAM3D inference, then close the whole SAM worker BEFORE seed/train
STATIC.idea: After segment, static_sam3d.generate(anchor, objects, reg['sam3d']) runs the warm SAM3D inference (in tm.stage('trigger.sam3d_infer')), then in tm.stage('after.sam_worker_close') the orchestrator calls reg['_sam_worker'].close(). Closing the entire worker PROCESS (not just unload_sam3d) 100%-frees its CUDA context, because SAM3D's VRAM cannot co-reside with the Open3D VoxelBlockGrid (TSDF seed) + splatfacto train at 1200p. This hard process-close is the mechanism that guarantees the GPU is clear for the seed build and training.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: VRAM schedule step 4 — AnySplat spawns ONLY AFTER the SAM worker is closed (the 16 GB OOM constraint)
STATIC.idea: Only after after.sam_worker_close does the orchestrator (if prewarm_dynamic) prewarm reg['anysplat'] (tm.stage('after.anysplat_spawn')) and reg['xfeat'] (tm.stage('after.dyn_models_prewarm')). The hard constraint per the in-code comment: loading AnySplat concurrently with the SAM3D load + Gazebo OOMs the 16 GB card (observed ~45 MiB free -> SAM3D load aborts -> run dies), so AnySplat MUST wait for the SAM worker close to free SAM3D's VRAM. Its load then overlaps the seed-finalize + splatfacto train; whatever hasn't finished by train-end is the visible end.wake_dynamic handoff, where the orchestrator wait_ready()s anysplat + xfeat. This is a VRAM-ceiling ordering, not a speed preference. NOTE: prewarm calls are guarded by `reg.get('anysplat') and ...` / `reg.get('xfeat') and ...` so a gated-out handle is skipped.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: gsplat backward JIT warm (one throwaway rasterize+backward off the critical path)
STATIC.idea: _warm_gsplat_backward(cfg, device) runs, on a daemon thread (launched in tm.stage('after.gsplat_warm'), i.e. in the freed slot after the SAM worker closes), ONE throwaway gsplat.rasterization on a synthetic scene of N=16 Gaussians: random means/quats, scales=rand*0.01, opac/colors random, viewmat=eye(4)[None], K=[[100,0,32],[0,100,32],[0,0,1]], width=height=64, means shifted +2 in z to be in front of the camera; then out.sum().backward() + torch.cuda.synchronize(). The backward() is load-bearing: it forces gsplat's SLOW backward CUDA kernels (proj fwd/bwd, fully_fused_projection, rasterize) to nvcc-JIT-compile HERE (cached in ~/.cache/torch_extensions) instead of stalling the first real training step. It runs on a daemon thread so it never blocks, and is idempotent/cheap once the kernel cache exists; on any exception it prints a skip message and lets the kernels compile lazily on the first train step.

STATIC.title: Model loading, workers & VRAM scheduling
STATIC.topic: Real-HW branches are out of scope (one-line note)
STATIC.idea: model_loader.py itself has NO real-hardware branching — the same handles/scheduling apply in sim and real. The real-HW switches (DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini) live in the live-bridge source + ros_mask, outside this module.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: The tracked object's instance id is chosen as the most-common NON-ZERO value in the per-Gaussian `object_instance_ids` buffer of the loaded scene. Mechanism: take `gset.snapshot().buffers['object_instance_ids'][:,0]`, filter to `ids>0`, then `torch.unique(..., return_counts=True)` and return the id with the largest count via `vals[counts.argmax()]`. Returns -1 if no non-zero id exists. This picks the dominant fused object (Phase-0b writes ids 1..K) as the single thing the tracker will move. WHY: the dynamic loop tracks exactly one rigid object; the most-populated instance is the real fused object vs stray ids.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: DynamicLoop.__init__ raises ValueError if `d0_id <= 0` (i.e. pick_d0_instance_id returned -1, all instance ids zero). WHY: a -1 d0 would make the tracker silently never move anything — the loop would run a no-op 'tracking' pass with no error; the guard converts that into an explicit crash so a scene with no fused object is caught at construction, not after a silent run.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: run_live's main loop calls `ring.peek_latest()` each iteration (read the newest frame in the SHM ring, NOT a FIFO pop) and skips work when `fr is None or int(fr.seq)==last_seq` by sleeping 0.002 s and continuing; it checks `ring.is_shutdown()` to break. So if the tracker falls behind the producer, intermediate frames are simply never processed — the loop always works on the latest frame and drops stale ones. WHY: real-time tracking must follow the live present, not accumulate a backlog; processing stale frames would lag the pose behind reality. Note: a parallel real-HW branch (DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA/Jetson/ZED-Mini) exists but is out of scope; the sim live path is identical downstream.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Replay-wrap detection in the live driver
DYNAMIC.idea: After reading each frame, run_live detects an episode wrap by `fr.stamp_sec < last_stamp - 0.5` (a backward jump > 0.5 s in capture stamp) and calls `loop.reset_for_loop()` before stepping. WHY: when a recorded episode replays as live and loops back to frame 0, the capture clock jumps backward; this restores the D0 state so every replay pass starts identically. The 0.5 s threshold avoids triggering on normal small inter-frame stamp jitter.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: reset_for_loop — restore D0 state on replay wrap
DYNAMIC.idea: reset_for_loop() makes each replay pass identical by: (1) snapshot the gset, compute `ref.apply(I3, zeros, snap)` and `write_object_pose(*out)` to move the tracked object back to its D0 rest pose (identity transform); (2) find all FF-insert rows via `object_instance_ids == cfg.feedforward.insert_id` (insert_id=999) and `gset.cull()` them, dropping every feedforward insert; (3) `sm.set_hidden_indices(None)` to un-hide deferred-cull rows; (4) set `self._seeded=False` so the next frame re-seeds the tracker (whose initialize() clears anchors+KF+cumulative pose). ref is re-captured at the restored rest pose on the next seed so it stays the original D0 reference. WHY: a looping replay must reproduce the same D0 scene+tracker every pass; otherwise FF accumulation and a drifted object would compound across loops.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Per-tick input prep: RGB/depth/keep to GPU + depth filter
DYNAMIC.idea: step() converts the frame to GPU tensors: RGB via `_rgb_gpu` (BGR->RGB by `frame.rgb_bgr[...,::-1]`, float /255), depth via `_depth_gpu` (frame.depth_m as-is in meters), and `keep` (gripper-keep mask, from frame.mask_keep) to float. If `self._filter_depth` (default True, from cfg.depth.filter_enabled / DGS_DEPTH_FILTER) it applies `dynamic_gs.utils.depth_filter.filter_depth_torch(depth)` (median+bilateral) inside a try/except. WHY filter: the tracker's RANSAC-Kabsch operates on depth-backprojected 3D points; stereo flying-pixels/noise would corrupt the point set and the estimated pose, so depth is cleaned at the source.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Gripper-masked region composited with scene background
DYNAMIC.idea: Before tracking, step() composites the live RGB so the gripper area is replaced by the render background: `km = keep` (2D), `bg = sm._get_background_color().view(1,1,-1)`, then `rgb = rgb*km[...,None] + bg*(1-km[...,None])`. keep=1 keeps the real pixel, keep=0 paints the Gazebo sky background color. WHY: the gripper occludes/overlaps the object and has its own texture; without masking it out, XFeat keypoints could lock onto moving gripper texture and the tracker would follow the gripper instead of the object. The background fill (not black) avoids injecting a strong false edge.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: _object_mask(camera) holds `self.lock` (the ONE model_lock) and within that hold does BOTH: take a fresh `gset.snapshot()`, build the bool instance mask `object_instance_ids[:,0]==d0_id`, and call `sm.render_object_mask(camera, inst)`. The snapshot is taken INSIDE the lock so the mask length (count N) is consistent with the params the render rasterizes (count N') — a concurrent FF insert can't make a length-N mask index length-N' params. WHY: snapshotting outside the lock risks a torn read where mask and live params disagree -> IndexError; the lock+inside-snapshot guarantees mask len == live count.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: render_object_mask renders ONLY the selected Gaussians by temporarily swapping `model.gauss_params` for a subset: it slices each param to the live count `[:c]` (c from the count_provider, the free-list live count), masks by the instance bool, wraps in a no-grad ParameterDict, renders, reads `accumulation/alpha`, and returns `alpha[...,0] > 0.5` (alpha_thr=0.5) as a bool HxW silhouette; restores the saved params in `finally`. Returns all-False if the subset is empty. WHY: gives a pixel silhouette of just the tracked object so the tracker can be confined to object pixels and the FF can be told which region is the object. The 0.5 alpha threshold binarizes coverage.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Crop to object bbox for XFeat (+ padding, min size)
DYNAMIC.idea: When `cfg.tracker.crop_to_object_bbox` (default True), step() computes a bbox from the object silhouette via `_bbox_from_mask(objmask, crop_padding_px, W, H)` and crops rgb/depth/keep/objmask+camera to it via `_crop`. _bbox_from_mask: `torch.where(objmask)` -> min/max xs,ys, expand by pad=crop_padding_px (default 150) clamped to [0,W]/[0,H], +1 on the max side; returns None if either side <16 px (min bbox size) or mask empty. WHY: XFeat extracts a fixed `top_k=1024` keypoints; over a full 1200p frame they spread everywhere, but a small object would get few. Cropping concentrates the top_k budget ON the object. World-frame R,t is crop-invariant, so cropping doesn't change the estimated pose.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Crop camera rebuild keeps depth metric (_crop)
DYNAMIC.idea: _crop slices rgb/depth/keep/objmask to [y0:y1, x0:x1] and rebuilds a nerfstudio Cameras with cx,cy shifted by the crop origin (`cx-x0`, `cy-y0`) while fx,fy are UNCHANGED, and width/height set to the crop size, camera_type PERSPECTIVE, c2w copied. WHY: shifting only the principal point (not focal) preserves the camera's metric scale, so depth back-projection of the cropped region produces correct 3D points for the tracker's Kabsch fit; changing fx/fy would distort metric geometry.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: step() branches on `self._seeded`. When NOT seeded: `ref.capture(snap)` stores the D0 reference (means/quats keyed by gauss_uid), `tracker.seed(inp)` initializes the XFeat anchor from object-masked keypoints, set `_seeded = tracker.ready`, optionally write a pose-log anchor record, and RETURN a seed row (R=I3, t=0, tracking_ok=False, seed=kept count) without moving anything. Once seeded, every subsequent tick calls `tracker.track(inp)` to estimate motion. WHY: the first frame defines D0 (the rest pose anchor); you can't track motion until an anchor exists, and `tracker.ready` gates that the seed produced enough keypoints (min_track_points=12).

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: On a tracked tick, `est = tracker.track(inp)` returns a MotionEstimate (success, rotation 3x3, translation 3, inlier_count). If `est.success`, `ref.apply(R,t,snap)` returns `(means_subset, quats_subset, uids)` — the D0 rest means/quats rigidly transformed (means_sub = ref_means @ R^T + t; quats via delta-quat * ref_quats, normalized) — and `gset.write_object_pose(ms, qs, uids)` writes them onto the LIVE rows matched by stable gauss_uid (resolved under the gset lock, FF-race-safe). WHY identity-keyed: the free-list reorders rows on FF cull/insert, so the tracked object is keyed by stable gauss_uid, never row position; apply/write match uids (searchsorted on sorted ref uids) so a concurrent FF surgery between snapshot and write can't misplace the pose.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Tracker config -> old XFeat estimator wiring + gates
DYNAMIC.idea: XFeatTracker wraps the old XFeatMotionEstimator with config-driven params: top_k=1024 keypoints, ransac_iterations=68, ransac_inlier_threshold=0.004 m, min_track_points=12, rotation_gate_deg=22.5 (passed as anchor_rotation_gate_deg), scale_gate_ratio=1.3 (passed as anchor_scale_gate), static_hold_window=15, static_hold_trans=25 mm (->0.025 m), static_hold_rot=10 deg; pose_filter (KF) params come from cfg.pose_filter with meas sigmas converted mm->m / deg. scale_select is passed to the old estimator via env DGS_XFEAT_SCALE_SELECT (set in __init__). WHY these gates: the inlier threshold (0.004 m) and RANSAC iters (68) tune pose stability/inlier consensus; rotation/scale gates reject implausible anchor jumps; the static-hold window+thresholds suppress steady-state jitter when the object isn't actually moving.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: FF only fires when `self.ff is not None and self.ff.due(self._tick)`. due() is PURE/side-effect-free: returns False if a decode is already `_inflight`, else `c>0 and tick>0 and (tick % c == 0)` where `c = cfg.feedforward.cadence_ticks` (dataclass default 10; load_runtime_config / DGS_FF_CADENCE default 20). So FF is attempted on every cadence_ticks-th tick AND only when no prior decode is still running. WHY: AnySplat decode is slow and runs on a bg thread; cadence throttles how often inserts happen, and the in-flight guard prevents launching a second decode while one is active (single slot).

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: When due, step() builds an immutable (frozen dataclass) FeedforwardDispatch carrying `seq, camera, rgb_bgr.copy(), depth_m (filtered), object_mask, gripper_keep (keep), scene_intr (a dict keyed fl_x/fl_y/cx/cy/w/h from tracker_intr), d0_instance_id` and calls `ff.dispatch(d)`. dispatch() is non-blocking: it acquires a single Lock slot (`acquire(blocking=False)`, returns False if busy), sets `_inflight=True`, and starts a daemon Thread running `_run_guarded`; on Thread.start() failure it releases the slot so FF can't permanently wedge. The bg thread reads ONLY the immutable dispatch (no shared mutable state) and always frees the slot + empties CUDA cache in `finally`. WHY: keeps the per-tick tracker loop lock-free during the long AnySplat decode; `rgb_bgr.copy()` snapshots the frame so the producer can overwrite the SHM buffer.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: step() returns a dict trace row: tick, frame_seq, tracking_ok, inliers, R (3x3 list), t (3 list), ff_fired, ff_inserted (ff.last_inserted), ff_culled (ff.last_culled), total_gauss (gset.num_points). On seed ticks it instead returns seed=kept, tracking_ok=False, identity R/t. After the tracker write, if `self.on_render is not None` it calls `on_render(cam)`. WHY: the trace feeds the A/B verification driver (new_trace.jsonl vs old_trace.jsonl); on_render is the hook the viser bridge / view driver uses to request a render at the tracked camera each tick.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Tracker-tick timing event inside FF cycle
DYNAMIC.idea: Every step() emits `_timing.get_ledger().event('tracker_tick', tick=self._tick)`. WHY: the FF report can show WHERE the tracker ticked relative to an FF cycle — the tracker may tick several times during one long lock-free AnySplat decode, and this marker proves the FF bg thread isn't blocking the per-tick tracker loop.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: When `pose_log_path` is set (data_dir/object_track_poses.jsonl), the loop writes one JSONL per run: on each successful seed `_pose_log_anchor` writes an `anchor` record (incrementing segment, the D0 reference centroid from `ref.reference_centroid()` = mean of captured ref means, d0_instance_id) defining the anchor as world origin; each tracked tick `_pose_log_tick` writes a `pose` record (tick, t_sec, ok, R flattened 9, t 3) — the raw D0->current rigid transform IS the object's absolute world pose. Anchor records flush every write; pose records flush every 30 ticks. Replay loops / re-seeds emit a NEW anchor segment so a changed anchor is recorded. WHY: records the tracked object's per-tick rigid trajectory for offline inspection independent of FF.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: run_full_live runs the static phase via `static_pipeline.run_static(..., return_scene=True)` which returns the in-memory `(sm,gset,lock)` plus a warm `reg` registry. It then RE-PHASES the scene IN PLACE: `sm.set_phase('dynamic')` (re-binds the means-grad hook that hard-zeros means.grad and re-asserts dynamic LR policy = ALL LRs 0), `gset.enable_freelist()` (turn on swap-remove/insert capacity management), and `sm.set_count_provider(lambda: gset.count)` (render sees only the [:count] live view so dead rows don't rasterize). This reaches the exact state `build_loaded_scene(phase='dynamic')` produces WITHOUT a reload. WHY one process: AnySplat/XFeat are warm-loaded during static and reused; two commands would kill the warm worker and re-spawn it.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Reuse warm AnySplat + XFeat handles (no reload/respawn)
DYNAMIC.idea: run_full_live pulls the already-warm handles from the registry — `warm_anysplat = reg['anysplat'].handle()` (raw AnysplatHandle, only if ff_enabled and 'anysplat' in reg) and `warm_tracker = reg['xfeat'].tracker()` (XFeatTracker, only if 'xfeat' in reg) — and passes them into `run_live(warm_scene=(sm,gset,lock), warm_anysplat=..., warm_tracker=...)`. run_live, when warm_* are given, reuses them IN PLACE: scene not rebuilt, tracker not re-constructed, AnySplat not re-spawned (only `wait_ready()`, idempotent). WHY: the static phase already paid the AnySplat model-load + first-inference warm-up; reusing avoids a mid-episode stall on the first decode and a full worker re-spawn.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: run_live FF worker construction + deferred-cull wiring
DYNAMIC.idea: When ff_enabled, run_live builds `FeedforwardWorker(gset, lock, cfg.feedforward, cfg.budget, cdn_fn=make_cdn_fn(sm,lock,cfg,ring.intrinsics(),data_dir=data_dir), decode_fn=make_decode_fn(anysplat,cfg,ring.intrinsics()), set_hidden_fn=sm.set_hidden_indices)`. AnySplat is warm-started (prewarm + wait_ready) BEFORE open_source so its load overlaps the scene warm-load and never becomes a mid-run stall. The `set_hidden_fn` wires FF 'Option A' deferred-cull: rows to be culled are opacity-zeroed via set_hidden_indices for the re-CDN render but the real cull commits ATOMICALLY with the insert (no cull-without-insert flicker). WHY: keeps FF inserts/culls invisible-until-atomic and gives the worker the model render (cdn) + decoder it needs without holding the lock during decode.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: run_recorded_trace builds the loaded dynamic scene from the warm cache (`build_loaded_scene(phase='dynamic')`), picks d0, makes ReferenceObjectPose+XFeatTracker, opens a ReplaySource in mode='fast' attached to a named SHM ring (default 'dgs_dynamic_gs2_ab'), and ticks frame-exact: pull `src.next_frame()` to advance, then `ring.peek_latest()` and `loop.step(ring_fr or fr)`, writing each row to out_trace JSONL. ff_enabled=False (default) validates the pure tracker pose path with no AnySplat. WHY: a headless, frame-exact, deterministic replay so the new pipeline's per-tick R/t/FF counts can be diffed against the frozen old pipeline's trace for functional-equivalence verification.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.topic: Render under lock for viser / view driver
DYNAMIC.idea: The live and view drivers pass a `render_fn(cam)` that does `with lock: rgb,_,_ = sm.render(cam)` to the ViserBridge — the SAME single model_lock guards every tracker write_object_pose, every FF insert, AND every render. WHY: render reads the gauss params while the tracker/FF mutate them; without the shared lock a render could rasterize a half-applied pose or a torn insert. The viser bridge is server-side rasterize + push-image on port 8081 (cfg.viser.port default 8081); the NS viewer is never used.

DYNAMIC.title: Dynamic loop orchestration & per-tick flow
DYNAMIC.idea: run_view_recorded replays a dataset at ~fps with the viser viewer up; each episode it resets `src._idx=0, src._seq=0, loop._seeded=False, loop._tick=0, ref._ref_means=None`, runs the inner frame loop (peek_latest, loop.step, push camera-feed/tracked-camera/finger markers, request_render, sleep 1/fps), and on episode end (if loop_forever) reloads the SAME gset from the warm cache via `load_warm_cache` (which rebinds sm's tensor view) and re-seeds. WHY: visual validation of tracking with NO live sim, repeating from the identical D0 scene each pass.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: dynamic_gs2.XFeatTracker is a thin config-driven WRAP over the proven dynamic_gs.utils.xfeat_motion.XFeatMotionEstimator. __init__ translates the typed TrackerConfig/PoseFilterConfig into the estimator's many kwargs and ALSO sets one env var (os.environ['DGS_XFEAT_SCALE_SELECT']='1'/'0' from tracker_cfg.scale_select) because the old estimator reads scale-aware selection only from env. It exposes exactly two operations: seed(TrackerInputs)->kept_count (calls estimator.initialize) and track(TrackerInputs)->MotionEstimate (calls estimator.estimate_and_advance), plus a `ready` property. TrackerInputs carries rgb (HW3 float[0,1] GPU), depth (HW float32 metres, 0==invalid), a nerfstudio Cameras (1 cam), keep_mask (gripper/robot keep, 1==keep), object_mask (rendered tracked-object footprint), and stamp_sec. The wrapper holds NO model lock and never touches the GaussianSet. Note seed() uses object_mask if present else keep_mask. Real-HW branches exist elsewhere (DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA) but this is the sim live/replay path.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: The shipped sim defaults (frozen dataclass TrackerConfig in dynamic_gs2/config.py, several env-overridable via DGS_XFEAT_*/DGS_HOLD_*) are: top_k=1024 (DGS_XFEAT_TOP_K), ransac_iterations=68 (DGS_XFEAT_RANSAC_ITERS), ransac_inlier_threshold=0.004 m (DGS_XFEAT_RANSAC_INLIER_M; stricter than the estimator's own 0.008 default), lighterglue_depth_confidence=-1.0 (LighterGlue layer-early-exit DISABLED in sim, overriding the estimator's 0.95 default), rotation_gate_deg=22.5, scale_gate_ratio=1.3, scale_select=False (DGS_XFEAT_SCALE_SELECT), static_hold_window=15 (DGS_HOLD_WINDOW), static_hold_trans_mm=25.0 (DGS_HOLD_TRANS_MM), static_hold_rot_deg=10.0 (DGS_HOLD_ROT_DEG), min_track_points=12, plus crop_to_object_bbox=True / crop_padding_px=150 / object_mask_filter=True. Note: rotation_gate_deg / scale_gate_ratio / lighterglue_depth_confidence / crop_* / min_track_points are NOT given env overrides in load_runtime_config (only top_k, ransac iters/inlier, scale_select, and the static_hold trio are). These config values are what actually run.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: The KF config tree (frozen PoseFilterConfig in dynamic_gs2/config.py): enabled=False by default (DGS_KF_ENABLED=1 turns it on — so the default sim/A-B path runs WITHOUT KF smoothing, using raw _cumulative_ pose), fixed_fps=9.0 (rate-invariant synthetic dt), accel_sigma=0.005, alpha_sigma=0.025, meas_trans_mm=20.0, meas_rot_deg=10.0, snap_trans_m=0.05, snap_rot_deg=10.0. The wrapper divides meas_trans_mm by 1000 to metres (pose_filter_meas_trans_sigma_m=0.020) and passes meas_rot_deg in degrees (pose_filter_meas_rot_sigma_deg). Env overrides DGS_KF_ACCEL_SIGMA/ALPHA_SIGMA/MEAS_TRANS_MM/MEAS_ROT_DEG are read a SECOND time inside XFeatMotionEstimator.__init__ (taking precedence over the wired kwargs).

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: _extract runs XFeat sparse detectAndCompute on an HxWx3 float tensor in 0..255 range (one CNN forward producing detect+describe together). It returns top_k keypoints (sub-pixel (x,y) via heatmap NMS then top-k by score) as an (N,2) float32 ndarray, (N,64) L2-normalised descriptors on GPU, the GPU keypoint tensor (LighterGlue input), and image_size=(W,H) (needed by LighterGlue for positional encoding). top_k is clamped to >=8 at construction (max(int(top_k),8); sim value 1024). detection_threshold=0.05, min_cossim=-1.0. A use_semi_dense=False path uses detectAndComputeDense (coarse grid) but is off by default. _maybe_warmup JITs cuDNN+LighterGlue at the actual (H,W) once, re-warming only if resolution changes. _prepare_rgb_gpu keeps RGB on GPU and multiplies by 255 unconditionally (contract: input is 0..1) with NO host sync.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: Matching is anchor<->current via LighterGlue (XFeat-author slim LightGlue, 6 transformer layers). _lighterglue_match packs both keypoint sets as (B,N,2), descriptors as (B,N,D), and image_size as [W,H] per side, calls the matcher with min_conf=lighterglue_min_conf=0.1, and returns the (idx_a,idx_b) match index pairs; returns empty if either side has < min_track_points (12) keypoints OR LighterGlue is None. LighterGlue is built eagerly; if it fails to construct (kornia/lightglue/weights missing) the estimator falls back to _mnn_match: mutual-nearest-neighbour over L2-normalised 64-D descriptors using sim=desc_a@desc_b.T, argmax both directions, keep pairs where nn_ba[nn_ab]==idx. WHY LighterGlue over MNN: its cross-attention rejects ambiguous background<->background pairs that MNN keeps, which would otherwise flood RANSAC with identity-confirming background matches and drown the object's motion. The depth_confidence layer-early-exit knob is set at construction time (sim value -1.0 = off).

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.topic: Why extract on full image then filter by mask (not pre-mask)
DYNAMIC.idea: Both the D0 seed and new-anchor creation extract XFeat on the FULL (cropped) image, then KEEP only keypoints whose rounded (x,y) falls inside the object mask (np.where on inside_obj_mask / anchor_keep_region), filtering keypoints, descriptors, and keypoints_gpu by the same survivor index. WHY: a masked-image (pre-mask) extract corrupts descriptors at the erosion boundary AND makes anchor descriptors inconsistent with the per-tick full-image descriptors LighterGlue matches them against, plus costs an extra forward. Post-filtering picks keypoints without mutating the image the CNN sees, so a few px of mask misalignment just trims/adds edge points instead of corrupting descriptors, and RANSAC drops any background point that slips in. Fallback: if filtering would leave fewer than min_track_points (12) survivors, the filter is skipped (mask probably wrong/empty). A legacy _pre_mask_image (erode 5px then zero outside) exists but is no longer used on these paths.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.topic: Depth back-projection of matched keypoints to 3D
DYNAMIC.idea: sample_depth_bilinear bilinearly samples depth at each keypoint (4-neighbour interp with weights wx,wy), marking a point invalid if any of the 4 taps is non-finite or <=0 or the result is <=0. backproject_to_world maps pixel+depth to world in OpenGL camera convention: cam_pt = [(x-cx)*z/fx, -(y-cy)*z/fy, -z] (negated Y and Z — nerfstudio c2w looks along -Z), then world = cam_pt @ R.T + t using the camera_to_world 3x4. fx/fy guarded by max(.,1e-8). Anchors store ONLY depth-valid points (Kabsch needs 3D); the current frame back-projects ALL keypoints once and masks invalid ones afterward. The cropped Cameras shifts cx,cy by the bbox origin (cx-x0, cy-y0) while keeping fx,fy so back-projection stays metric and world-frame R,t is crop-invariant.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: estimate_rigid_transform_ransac runs 3-point RANSAC over closed-form Kabsch. Per iteration (iterations=ransac_iterations, sim=68): draw 3 random correspondences (seeded RNG default 12345 via DGS_RANSAC_SEED so it is deterministic per match set), solve Kabsch on them, compute per-pair residual = ||src@R.T + t - tgt||, count inliers with residual <= threshold (sim threshold=0.004 m). Keep the trial maximizing inlier_count (ties broken by lower mean inlier residual). If best_inlier_count >= min_inliers (passed as min_track_points=12) it REFITS Kabsch on the full inlier set and recomputes inliers; otherwise it returns the best-trial pose with residual stats over ALL pairs so the caller can tell a tight-threshold case from garbage matches. A trial is only considered if it has >=3 inliers; returns None only if no trial got >=3 inliers. Kabsch (estimate_rigid_transform): center both clouds, SVD of src0.T@tgt0, R=Vh.T@U.T with a reflection fix (flip last row of Vh if det(R)<0), t=tgt_center - R@src_center.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: _match_and_solve_against_anchor runs match (LighterGlue or MNN) -> gather matched anchor_xy/curr_xy -> in-image finiteness/bounds filter on current -> keep_region filter on current (gripper_keep ∩ dilated-object halo; if that drops below min_track_points=12 it sets used_mask_fallback and reverts to the pre-region valid set) -> AND with current depth validity (curr_depth_valid[curr_idx]) -> require depth_valid_count>=12 -> select anchor_world_pts=anchor.world_3d[anchor_idx[depth_compatible]] and curr_world_pts=curr_world_all[curr_idx[depth_compatible]] -> call RANSAC-Kabsch with source=anchor, target=current. The RANSAC inlier mask (over the depth-compatible subset) is promoted back to the full match index space as tracked_inlier_mask for the debug visualizer. The anchor side is NEVER keep_region-restricted (its mask was 'where the object WAS').

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: Each tick builds keep_region for the current-frame match filter as gripper_keep_np ∩ dilate(rendered_object_mask, object_search_radius_px=80). The dilation uses a (2*r+1)x(2*r+1)=161x161 ones kernel (cv2.dilate, 1 iteration). WHY: restricting current matches to a halo around the object's PREDICTED footprint stops STATIC background features (which survive gripper-keep + depth) from outvoting the object's true motion in RANSAC — the grasped-and-lifted failure mode where, once the object leaves the table, the crop fills with static background whose consistent zero-motion matches make the Kabsch majority pin the pose to the nearest anchor ('object stops moving'). The mask lags one tick, hence the dilation halo. When the object-masked set drops below min_track_points (12) the filter reverts to gripper-keep-only so an occluded/tiny mask can't kill tracking.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: Instead of pairwise prev-frame matching, the estimator keeps a pool of rotational/scale keyframes (_anchors). anchors[0] is the D0 anchor with rotation=I, translation=0. Matching is anchor<->current so drift is bounded to ONE anchor-to-current hop regardless of how far the object rotated from D0. Composition (Kabsch returns source->target = anchor->current local (R_local,t_local)): the canonical D0->current pose is T_current = T_local · T_anchor, i.e. new_R = R_local @ anchor.rotation and new_t = (R_local @ anchor.translation) + t_local. This updated _cumulative_R/_cumulative_t is the raw pose used for anchor selection/creation/next-tick prediction (NEVER the KF-smoothed output, to avoid feeding smoothing lag back into tracking state). Each _Anchor stores descriptors, keypoints_gpu, world_3d (at capture), keypoints (ndarray), image_size, rotation/translation (D0->anchor), camera_rotation (c2w[:3,:3]) and camera_distance.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.topic: Multi-anchor bank: selection (nearest viewpoint + optional scale)
DYNAMIC.idea: _select_nearest_anchor_by_rotation picks the anchor whose stored VIEW of the object is closest to the current view. It compares RELATIVE (object-in-camera) rotations: predicted_R_rel = camera_R_now.T @ _cumulative_R vs each anchor's R_cam.T @ R_anchor, distance = geodesic SO(3) angle arccos((trace(Ra.T@Rb)-1)/2) clamped to [-1,1] in degrees. WHY relative: that is what XFeat/LighterGlue actually match on (appearance from a viewpoint), so it correctly handles camera-only, object-only, or combined motion. When DGS_XFEAT_SCALE_SELECT=1 (sim default OFF), a scale mismatch is folded in as equivalent-degrees: cost += max(0, scale_ratio-1) * (rotation_gate_deg / max(scale_gate-1,1e-6)). exclude defaults to empty on attempt 0; the 2nd-nearest is tried by adding the used index to exclude. Returns -1 if pool empty/all excluded.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: estimate_and_advance loops at most 2 attempts. Attempt 0 matches+solves against the nearest anchor; the per-attempt sub-timings accumulate. It keeps whichever attempt has MORE RANSAC inliers (primary_result updated when inliers > current best), recording last_used_fallback_anchor=(attempt>0). It STOPS early once an attempt's inliers >= anchor_min_inliers (_MIN_INLIERS_DEFAULT=20, clamped to >= min_track_points=12 at construction); otherwise it adds the tried anchor to exclude and retries the 2nd-nearest. The 20-inlier floor is intentionally above min_track_points (12) so the fallback fires before full pose loss rather than after.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: After a successful tick, _needs_new_anchor decides whether to append a fresh anchor. An anchor 'covers' the current view iff it is within BOTH rotation_gate_deg=22.5 (relative SO(3) distance) AND scale_gate_ratio=1.3 (apparent-scale). A new anchor is captured when NO existing anchor covers both, so the pool tiles (orientation x apparent-scale) space (22.5deg -> ~16 anchors over a 360deg sweep). _scale_ratio(dist_a,dist_b)=max(a/b,b/a), returning 1.0 (no veto) if either distance is non-finite or <=1e-6. scale_gate is clamped to >= 1.001 at construction. Apparent size ~ 1/distance, so 1.3 == the on-screen object size changed ~1.3x, beyond which XFeat/LighterGlue shed matches. Translation is never used in either gate.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: A new anchor is built from the CURRENT frame's already-extracted full-image keypoints POST-filtered to anchor_keep_region = keep_region ∩ object_mask (same recipe as D0), re-sampling depth at those keypoints and AND-ing with the region again (_restrict_depth_valid_to_image_mask), requiring >= min_track_points (12) survivors. _build_anchor drops depth-invalid keypoints (Kabsch needs 3D), back-projects survivors to world, stores rotation/translation = current _cumulative_ pose, camera_rotation = c2w[:3,:3], and camera_distance = ||cam_pos - (R@centroid_d0 + t)|| where centroid_d0 is the FIXED D0 object centroid (world_3d.mean at D0); before D0 is set it uses this anchor's own keypoint centroid. _current_camera_object_distance reuses this: one 3x3 matmul + norm, tracking object position implicitly via the pose (never iterating the cloud).

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: initialize resets _cumulative_R=I/_cumulative_t=0, clears the anchor pool, resets the KF and static-hold history, then extracts XFeat on the full (cropped) frame, post-filters keypoints to the object mask (skipping the filter if fewer than min_track_points=12 survive), samples bilinear depth, AND-restricts to the (non-eroded) seed mask, and builds the D0 anchor with rotation=I/translation=0. It also records centroid_d0 = D0 world_3d.mean. Returns the kept depth-valid keypoint count (0 if < min_track_points at any stage). The `ready` property is True only once anchors[0] exists with >= min_track_points (12) depth-valid descriptors; estimate_and_advance returns not-ready/success=False until then. Pipeline calls ref.capture(snap) then tracker.seed(inp) on the first tick and sets _seeded once tracker.ready.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: A tick is success iff RANSAC inlier_count >= min_track_points (12); on success _cumulative_ is updated and last_inlier_count/last_anchor_idx_used recorded. A RELATIVE spike gate (DGS_SPIKE_GATE_FRAC, default '0' = OFF in sim) optionally rejects a tick whose inlier_count < frac * rolling-median (median over the inlier history, only once len>=8, history kept to last 30) as a degenerate match set, holding the last pose. Inlier counts are appended to the history even on gate-rejected ticks so a SUSTAINED drop (motion onset / new viewpoint) lowers the median within ~8 ticks and tracking resumes — a fixed high threshold instead killed tracking permanently. On failure the estimate returns the held _cumulative_ pose with success=False.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: PoseKalmanFilter is a constant-velocity error-state KF on SE(3), 12-state [position(3), velocity(3), rotation-error(3), angular-velocity(3)] with nominal _t_nom/_R_nom and small-angle error injected+zeroed each update (standard ESKF; angular velocity in world frame, composed on the left via _so3_exp). Predict: t += v*dt, R = exp(omega*dt)@R, F has dt blocks; process noise Q is piecewise-constant white-acceleration per axis using accel_sigma^2 (translation) and alpha_sigma^2 (rotation) with the dt^4/4, dt^3/2, dt^2 structure. Update: innovation y=[t_meas - t_nom, so3_log(R_meas @ R_nom.T)], H selects position+rotation-error, gain K=P H.T S^-1, inject dx into nominal. First call initializes nominal to the measurement (P diag = meas vars for pos/rot, 1.0 for velocity, 10.0 for angular velocity). It smooths ONLY the (R,t) returned to the pipeline; the raw _cumulative_ stays unfiltered. Sim default enabled=False.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: Constructor sigmas (estimator passes accel_sigma=0.005, alpha_sigma=0.025, meas_trans_sigma=meas_trans_mm/1000=0.020 m, meas_rot_sigma=radians(meas_rot_deg)=radians(10) in the sim config; the PoseKalmanFilter's own bare __init__ defaults are 0.05/0.25/0.003/0.009rad, and the estimator's __init__ kwarg defaults are 0.05/0.25/0.003/0.5deg). Process noise (accel/alpha): LOWER = smoother + more lag. Measurement noise (meas_trans_var=sigma^2, meas_rot_var=sigma^2): LOWER = trusts the measurement = more responsive/less lag. Env DGS_KF_ACCEL_SIGMA/ALPHA_SIGMA/MEAS_TRANS_MM/MEAS_ROT_DEG override at estimator construction. On each success tick the caller inflates measurement noise adaptively by meas_scale = clamp(sqrt(80/inliers), 1.0..4.0) (spike frames have ~half the inliers), so weak match sets lean on the velocity model.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: The KF timestamp is the CAPTURE event-time of the current frame (current_stamp_sec threaded from Frame.stamp_sec), so internal dt = this-frame-stamp minus previously-filtered-frame-stamp = the REAL elapsed gap between the two frames actually filtered. This is correct under frame-drop (replay/live read the freshest SHM frame and drop stale ones) and is rate-invariant (sensor clock, not wall-clock). dt is clamped to (0, 0.5)s; outside that range it falls back to 1/20 s. Priority: DGS_KF_SYNTHETIC_FPS (offline tuning) > real capture stamp (current_stamp_sec>0) > config fixed_fps=9.0 (synthetic kf_tick/fps per tick, fallback when no stamp threaded) > time.time(). Only success ticks feed a measurement; failures return the last filtered pose (or raw _cumulative_ if not yet initialized).

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.topic: Pose KF: snap gate, physics-reject, robust-R spike gate
DYNAMIC.idea: Three innovation defenses (KF). (1) Physics reject: if the per-tick translation displacement ||t_meas - t_prev|| > max_speed_mps*dt (DGS_KF_MAX_SPEED_MPS=0.4) it is a bad match; hold the predicted pose for up to outlier_confirm-1 ticks (DGS_KF_OUTLIER_CONFIRM=3) before accepting as a genuine reacquisition. (2) Snap gate: if ||y_trans|| > snap_trans_eff or ||y_rot|| > snap_rot_eff (snap_trans_m=0.05, snap_rot_rad=0.1745=10deg, each PLUS snap_motion_k*expected_motion where DGS_KF_SNAP_MOTION_K=3.0, expected motion = |v|*dt) it is a discontinuity (reacquisition/anchor jump): snap-reset nominal to the measurement and zero velocity instead of smoothing through it (which would overshoot). (3) Robust-R spike gate: inflate R quadratically when the innovation exceeds 3*sigma + spike_motion_k*|v|*dt (DGS_KF_SPIKE_MOTION_K=1.0), so a degenerate-match spike is coasted through without lagging legit fast/long-dt motion. All snap/spike floors add a dt-aware |v|*dt term so they self-scale with speed and frame gap. Env overrides DGS_KF_SNAP_TRANS_M / DGS_KF_SNAP_ROT_DEG.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: After the KF, static-hold collapses stationary measurement wander. It keeps a deque of the last static_hold_window (sim 15, min 3) PRE-hold outputs (success ticks only). When the deque is full it measures net trend across the window: net_t = ||t_now - t_window[0]|| and net_r = arccos((trace(R_now @ R0.T)-1)/2). If net_t < static_hold_trans_m (25mm) AND net_r < static_hold_rot_rad (radians(10deg)), the object is deemed stationary and the OUTPUT becomes the per-axis MEDIAN of the window: median of the translations, and median of the Rodrigues rotation-vectors converted back to a matrix. WHY: a filter that stays responsive to motion cannot also erase few-mm/deg wander at low inlier counts; a trend-gated median can, at the cost of a small onset deadband (net motion must exceed the gate across the window before passing). Output-side ONLY — raw _cumulative_ is never touched. Env DGS_HOLD_WINDOW/TRANS_MM/ROT_DEG.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: dynamic_track.rotation_matrix_to_quaternion converts the tracker's (3,3) R into a (4,) wxyz quaternion by branching on the LARGEST of {trace, R00, R11, R22} (cand.argmax), each branch using s = 2*sqrt(clamp_min(1+..., 1e-12)) and reading the appropriate off-diagonal differences/sums, then normalizing with clamp_min(1e-9). WHY the argmax branch: the trace-only formula gives a degenerate sqrt for angles >=120deg (trace<=0), so picking the largest diagonal/trace term keeps it numerically stable for ALL rotation angles. _quat_mul (Hamilton product) and _normalize_quats (divide by norm clamp_min 1e-8) compose this delta-quaternion with the reference quats.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.topic: ReferenceObjectPose.capture: D0 reference snapshot by uid
DYNAMIC.idea: capture(snapshot) selects the tracked object's rows by mask = (object_instance_ids[:,0] == d0_id) and clones the D0 rest-pose means and quats plus each row's stable gauss_uid (NOT row position). It precomputes _ref_order=argsort(ref_uid) and _ref_uid_sorted once (invariant after capture) so per-tick apply() needn't re-sort. Counts via tensor .shape[0] to avoid a CUDA .item() sync; returns 0 (and nulls the refs) if no rows match. WHY uid-keyed: the GaussianSet free-list swap-removes/inserts rows, so row position is NOT stable across ticks; keying by gauss_uid lets the transformed pose always land on the right gaussian regardless of reordering. d0_id is chosen by pick_d0_instance_id = the most-common non-zero object_instance_id (torch.unique on ids>0, argmax of counts); -1 if none, which makes DynamicLoop fail loud.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: apply(rotation, translation, snapshot) re-derives the live object mask (ids==d0_id), reads cur_uid in current mask order, and bails (returns None) if the count differs from the reference. It aligns reference rows to current rows by uid WITHOUT a host sync: pos = searchsorted(_ref_uid_sorted, cur_uid).clamp(max=N-1), verify _ref_uid_sorted[pos]==cur_uid (else uid set drifted -> None), gather = _ref_order[pos] gives the ref-row index per current row. It then applies the rigid transform to the reference rest-pose: means_sub = ref_means @ R.T + t, and quats_sub = normalize(quat_mul(rotmat_to_quat(R), ref_quats)) (delta-quaternion is the LHS). Returns (means_sub, quats_sub, cur_uid) — uid-keyed, NOT a positional mask. Guards on non-finite R/t. write_object_pose later resolves uid->live row under the model lock so a concurrent FF cull/insert/reorder between snapshot and write can't misplace the pose. Pipeline calls ref.apply only on est.success and writes the result under the lock; reset_for_loop re-applies identity to restore the D0 rest pose.

DYNAMIC.title: Rigid-object tracker (XFeat + LighterGlue + RANSAC/Kabsch)
DYNAMIC.idea: Before tracking, the pipeline crops rgb/depth/keep/objmask/camera to the rendered object bbox (crop_to_object_bbox=True default). _bbox_from_mask takes the object mask's min/max (x,y), pads by crop_padding_px=150, clamps to the frame, and rejects crops smaller than 16px on a side. _crop rebuilds a nerfstudio Cameras with cx,cy shifted by (-x0,-y0) but fx,fy unchanged so depth back-projection stays metric and the resulting world-frame R,t is crop-invariant. WHY: XFeat spends its fixed top_k (1024) keypoint budget ON the (small) object instead of spreading them over the full 1200p frame. Before the crop, the input RGB also has the gripper-masked region (1-keep_mask) composited with the scene background color so the tracker can't lock onto gripper texture, and depth is median+bilateral filtered (filter_depth_torch) so the 3D points are clean.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: Every FF cycle is driven by a single frozen, immutable snapshot `FeedforwardDispatch` (a `@dataclass(frozen=True)`) carrying seq, the dispatch-time scene `camera`, `rgb_bgr` (H,W,3 uint8 BGR), `depth_m` (H,W float32 metres, filtered, 0==invalid), `object_mask`, `gripper_keep`, `scene_intr` dict, and `d0_instance_id`. The bg worker thread (`_run`) reads camera/rgb/depth/masks ONLY from this frozen `d` and NEVER from any live latest-frame attribute (a grep-check test even asserts the live-frame attribute token never appears in this file). WHY: this guarantees BY CONSTRUCTION that the camera pose the CDN scores the change-region against is identical to the pose the AnySplat inserts are placed against, eliminating the 'staleness re-insertion loop' where a pose mismatch between scoring and placement causes the same revealed surface to be re-inserted on every cycle ('insert much less'). The pipeline builds the dispatch with defensive copies/frozen values (`frame.rgb_bgr.copy()`, the dispatch-time `cam`) so later main-thread mutation can't leak in.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: FF runs at most one decode at a time. `due(tick)` is a PURE no-side-effect predicate returning True only when `not self._inflight` AND `c = int(cfg.cadence_ticks)`, `c > 0`, `tick > 0`, and `tick % c == 0`. `cadence_ticks` defaults to 10 in `FeedforwardConfig` but `build_config` overrides it to `_envi('DGS_FF_CADENCE', 20)` (env-tunable), so the effective live-sim cadence is every 20 ticks. `dispatch(d)` is non-blocking: it tries `self._slot.acquire(blocking=False)` (a `threading.Lock`); if the slot is taken it returns False (FF stays single-in-flight), else sets `_inflight=True` and starts a daemon `Thread(target=self._run_guarded)`. If `Thread.start()` raises, it resets `_inflight=False` and releases the slot so a launch failure never permanently wedges FF. `in_flight()` exposes the `_inflight` flag read-only.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: `_run_guarded` wraps `_run` in try/except/finally: any exception is caught and printed ('[FF] _run error: ...') so the daemon thread never dies silently; the `finally` ALWAYS (a) calls `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` if CUDA is available, (b) sets `_inflight=False`, (c) increments `_ff_calls`, and (d) releases `_slot` (swallowing RuntimeError on double-release). WHY the unconditional release: the next tick's `due()`/`dispatch()` can only fire FF again once the slot is free, so freeing it in `finally` regardless of crash path prevents a permanent wedge.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: After EVERY FF cycle (in `_run_guarded.finally`) the worker calls `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` to return that cycle's CUDA transients (scene render, cull-projection tensors, AnySplat decode buffers, surgery temporaries) to the allocator. WHY: the AnySplat decode worker is a separate process sharing the same GPU; without freeing per-cycle the FF allocator holds memory the AnySplat worker needs, starving it and causing OOM. Runs regardless of how `_run` exited (success, skip, or crash).

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: `_run(d)` orchestrates the whole FF cycle in fixed order: (1) reset `last_inserted=last_culled=0` and tag the timing cycle; (2) `regions = cdn_fn(d)` — render the scene + score the change region + clean (object-footprint subtract); skip with reason 'no_cdn' if empty; (3) decide `deferred = cfg.cull_before_decode AND set_hidden_fn is not None`; take `first_region = regions[0]`; (4) if `cull_before_decode`, compute the in-front cull `cull_idx, protect` against `first_region`; (5a deferred) hide those rows under the lock, re-run `cdn_fn(d, restrict_to=first_region)` (re-CDN as-if-culled, region-restricted), then un-hide — skip 'no_recdn' if empty; (5b non-deferred) commit the in-front cull on its own `g.cull` surgery, set `cull_idx=None`, then re-CDN; (6) `snap = g.snapshot()` (atomic read for ICP target + count); (7) `tensors = decode_fn(d, regions, snap)` — AnySplat decode, LOCK-FREE; skip 'empty_decode' if None/zero rows; (8) `_enforce_ceiling`; skip 'ceiling' if shed to empty; (9) compute `purge_due`; (10) atomic `cull_and_insert` (deferred) or plain `insert`+separate purge (non-deferred); (11) record `last_inserted/last_culled`, emit `ff_inserted` event + `gaussian_count` gauge, call `on_insert(rng)`.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: `_compute_cull_in_front` finds eligible scene gaussians that float IN FRONT of the live sensor surface inside the CDN region — direct projection, no render. Steps: snapshot means + `object_instance_ids[:,0]`; pull camera scalars (fx,fy,cx,cy,W,H) via `_cam_scalars` (handles tensor/(1,)-shape); if depth grid != camera res, scale intrinsics by sx=W/W_cam, sy=H/H_cam (fx*=sx, cx*=sx, fy*=sy, cy*=sy); take c2w (handle batched), R=c2w[:3,:3], t=c2w[:3,3]; transform means_cam=(means - t)@R; per-gaussian camera depth `depths_g = -means_cam[:,2]`; `in_front_cam = depths_g > 1e-6`; `safe_d = where(in_front_cam, depths_g, 1)`; project `u = fx*(means_cam[:,0]/safe_d)+cx`, `v = fy*(-means_cam[:,1]/safe_d)+cy` (note the -Y for the OpenGL-to-pixel flip); round+clamp to (u_idx,v_idx); `in_bounds = (0<=u<W)&(0<=v<H)&in_front_cam`; interpolate the CDN mask `comp` to (H,W) nearest if needed; sample `sensor_at = depth[v_idx,u_idx]` and `in_region = comp[v_idx,u_idx] & in_bounds`; the floater test is `in_front = depths_g < (sensor_at - cull_in_front_depth_tol_m)`. Returns `idx = nonzero(in_region & (sensor_at>0) & in_front & eligible)` plus a protect_mask `(ids == d0_instance_id)`.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: In-front cull eligibility is `eligible = (ids == 0) | (ids == cfg.insert_id)` where `insert_id` defaults to 999 — i.e. only background/static gaussians (id 0) and prior FF inserts (id 999) are deletable; the tracked object's id is excluded so it is never culled. The depth margin `cull_in_front_depth_tol_m` defaults to 0.01 m (10 mm): a gaussian is deleted ONLY if it sits MORE than 10 mm in front of the live surface (`depths_g < sensor_at - 0.01`). WHY the 10 mm margin: with 0 tolerance depth noise at a real static object's silhouette deleted genuine geometry; 10 mm only removes clear floaters well in front of the surface. The returned `protect_mask = (ids == d0_instance_id)` is passed into the surgery as belt-and-suspenders so the tracked object can never be deleted even if its id were somehow in the index set. WHAT artifacts it removes: occluders/floaters that AnySplat/prior inserts left hovering between the camera and the real surface in the changed region.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: `_compute_cull_replaced` deletes the OLD geometry the fresh insert overwrites: eligible non-tracked gaussians projecting into the changed region that lie in a THIN slab JUST BEHIND the live surface. Returns an empty long tensor immediately if `cull_replaced_enabled` is False (default True). Uses the same projection pipeline as the in-front cull (means_cam, depths_g, u/v projection, intrinsic rescale, CDN interpolate, sensor_at sample). The slab test is `in_slab = (depths_g >= sensor_at - eps) & (depths_g < sensor_at + tol)` with `eps = 1e-4` (0.1 mm float-compare grace at the at-surface boundary) and `tol = cull_replaced_depth_tol_m` (default 0.0 m, i.e. OFF by default; this value IS the slab thickness). Eligibility `(ids==0)|(ids==insert_id)`, plus `sensor_at>0` and `in_region`. WHY a bounded slab and not the whole column behind: deleting everything behind the surface would cull deep walls/background and the scene would vanish; the in-front region is handled by the separate in-front cull. WHY behind-only-and-thin: the new insert replaces the old surface at the same depth, so deleting only the old slab caps cumulative growth without leaving holes.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: When deferral is on (`cfg.cull_before_decode` True AND `set_hidden_fn` wired — the pipeline wires `set_hidden_fn=sm.set_hidden_indices`), the in-front cull is NOT committed before the decode. Instead the to-be-culled rows are VIRTUALLY hidden (`_set_hidden_fn(cull_idx)` under the lock) only so the re-CDN renders the scene as-if-culled, then un-hidden (`_set_hidden_fn(None)`). After the lock-free decode confirms there ARE inserts, `_run` folds THREE deletes into ONE atomic `g.cull_and_insert` surgery: (1) the held in-front `cull_idx`, (2) `_compute_cull_replaced(d, regions[0])` computed NOW (post-decode, so it never affects the re-CDN), (3) `_purge_indices()` when `purge_due`. The indices are concatenated and `.unique()`d; a fresh `protect_mask` `(object_instance_ids == d0_instance_id)` is rebuilt to match the commit state. WHY: committing cull+insert in one locked surgery + one rebind (`cull_and_insert` writes `_count` exactly once) means no reader/render ever observes a culled-but-not-yet-filled scene (no hole/flicker); new geometry replaces old in the same atomic step.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: If deferral is off (`set_hidden_fn is None` OR `cull_before_decode` False), the in-front cull is committed on its OWN `g.cull(cull_idx, protect_mask=protect)` surgery BEFORE the decode (recording `last_culled`), then the re-CDN runs. After the decode, geometry is added via plain `g.insert(tensors, object_flag=1.0, instance_id=insert_id)` (under lock); if `purge_due`, the periodic purge runs as a SEPARATE `_purge_ff_inserts` surgery and its count is ADDED to `last_culled`. Note `_run` calls `self.g.cull(...)` directly for the pre-decode commit (NOT the `cull_in_front` helper, which is a separate convenience wrapper). This path can briefly show a culled-but-unfilled scene (no atomicity), which is why deferral is preferred and wired by default.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: `_enforce_ceiling(tensors, d0_instance_id)` caps total scene size at `live_gaussian_ceiling` (default 2_000_000). If `g.num_points + m <= ceiling` (m = batch size) it returns the batch unchanged. Otherwise it FIRST calls `_purge_ff_inserts(d0_instance_id)` to free room by dropping low-opacity inserts, recomputes `room = max(0, ceiling - g.num_points)`; if `room >= m` returns the full batch; if `room == 0` returns `(None, m)` (refuse the whole insert, shed=m); else TRIMS the batch with `keep = slice(0, room)`, building a new GaussTensors of the first `room` rows of every field (means/features_dc/features_rest/scales/quats/opacities) and returns `(trimmed, m-room)`. WHY: this is the load-shed guard against unbounded growth (the documented 3M-gaussian blowup); when the scene is full it purges weak inserts then admits only as many new gaussians as fit. The skip-reason 'ceiling' is logged with `g.num_points/live_gaussian_ceiling` when fully shed.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: `_purge_indices()` COMPUTES (no commit) the low-opacity FF inserts to drop: snapshot `object_instance_ids[:,0]` and `inserted_flags[:,0] > 0.5`; eligibility `elig = ins & (ids == cfg.insert_id)` (only rows flagged inserted AND id==999, never the tracked object whose id != 999); `low = activated_opacity(opacities)[:,0] < thr` where `thr = budget.dynamic_purge_opacity_below` (default 0.05); returns `nonzero(elig & low)`. If `thr <= 0` it returns empty (purge disabled). The purge cadence is gated by `purge_due = n > 0 and (self._ff_calls % n == 0)` with `n = budget.dynamic_purge_every_n_ff` (DEFAULT 0 = disabled in live-sim). When deferred, these indices are folded into the atomic `cull_and_insert`; when non-deferred, `_purge_ff_inserts` commits them as a standalone `g.cull` surgery with `protect_mask = (object_instance_ids == d0_instance_id)`. WHY: bounds cumulative FF-insert accumulation by removing translucent/failed inserts, while structurally never touching the tracked object or static background.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
