DYNAMIC.idea: All three surgery primitives the worker calls (`g.cull`, `g.insert`, `g.cull_and_insert`) accept the FF index/protect contracts. `cull(indices, protect_mask)` validates indices to the live range `[0,n)` and `.unique()`s them, then if a protect_mask is given asserts `pm.shape[0]==n` and SILENTLY drops protected rows (`idx = idx[~pm[idx]]`) — protected rows are skipped, not an error. `insert(tensors, object_flag, instance_id)` writes the new rows' identity buffers `object_flags=object_flag`, `object_instance_ids=instance_id`, `inserted_flags=1.0` (sam3d_init_target_flags stays 0), assigns fresh monotonic gauss_uids, and returns the inserted index range. `cull_and_insert` does both under ONE lock with ONE `rebind()` and writes `_count` exactly once at `new_count+m`, so no reader (even a lockless `num_points` poll) ever sees the intermediate culled dip. WHY uid-keyed: cull uses swap-remove which REORDERS rows, so all downstream consumers (e.g. the tracker's `write_object_pose`) match by stable `gauss_uid`, never row index — this is what makes the lock-free decode safe against concurrent tracker writes.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: The shared `_model_lock` (RLock passed in) is held only for the short snapshot-read / hide / cull / insert operations; the heavy AnySplat decode (`decode_fn`) runs LOCK-FREE. The worker relies on the invariant that during the lock-free decode the ONLY concurrent scene mutation is the tracker's `write_object_pose`, which writes VALUES in place (no cull/insert/reorder), and that cull/insert come ONLY from this single-in-flight FF thread. Therefore the indices computed from earlier snapshots stay valid across the decode; nonetheless the protect_mask is rebuilt fresh just before the commit to match the live state. The deferred-cull hide/re-CDN block is explicitly wrapped `with self.lock` so the render honors the hidden set, then un-hidden inside the same lock scope.

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: Every FF insert tags its new rows with `object_flag=1.0` and `instance_id=cfg.insert_id` (999) and `inserted_flags=1.0`, which is exactly what makes those rows eligible for both the in-front/replaced culls (`ids==insert_id`) and the periodic low-opacity purge (`ins & ids==insert_id`) on later cycles — i.e. FF inserts are self-managing and distinguishable from both the static background (id 0) and the tracked object (d0_instance_id). After a successful insert, `last_inserted = rng.numel()`, the `ff_inserted` timing event (n, culled) and `gaussian_count` gauge (bounded-growth watchdog) are emitted, and the optional `on_insert(rng)` callback is invoked with the inserted index range. The pipeline reads `last_inserted`/`last_culled` back into the per-tick telemetry row (`row['ff_inserted']`/`row['ff_culled']`).

DYNAMIC.title: Feedforward worker: cull/insert surgery & robustness
DYNAMIC.idea: This module is source-agnostic and contains NO real-hardware branches; the DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini divergence lives entirely upstream in the source adapters and ros_mask (camera pose + mask), so the FF worker's cull/insert/purge logic is identical for sim and real. The live-sim path documented here is the only path through this file.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: make_cdn_fn returns cdn_fn(d, restrict_to=None) which is the per-FF-cycle change detector. Inputs come from the immutable FeedforwardDispatch d: d.rgb_bgr (HxWx3 uint8 BGR live image), d.depth_m (HxW float32 metres, filtered, 0==invalid), d.object_mask (tracked-object footprint), d.gripper_keep (robot keep-mask), d.camera (dispatch pose). The CURRENT scene is rendered from d.camera by scene_model.render(...) INSIDE the FF `lock`, yielding rgb_r (rendered RGB), alpha_r (the 'accumulation' channel = rendered coverage/opacity), and a depth channel (discarded, bound to _depth_r). The render is the only locked step; SSIM scoring + cleaning run lock-free. live_rgb is built by reversing BGR->RGB (d.rgb_bgr[...,::-1]) and /255 to [0,1]. Output: a Python list [HxW bool np] with one region mask, or [] when nothing changed (FF then skips decode).

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: compute_change_mask step 1 builds a per-pixel VALID gate. It starts by EXCLUDING the tracked object: valid = 1 - object_mask (resized to render HxW). WHY: the tracked 3D object is being moved by the tracker's rigid transform, so render-vs-live WILL disagree on/around it every frame; if that disagreement were treated as 'change' the decoder would re-decode flat new geometry onto the already-tracked object and smear it. The object footprint is therefore removed from where change is even allowed to be detected.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Valid mask — exclude gripper with extra erosion
DYNAMIC.idea: The gripper_keep mask (1=keep, i.e. NOT robot) is multiplied into valid so robot/gripper pixels are excluded from CDN. Before multiplying, the keep-mask is ERODED by gripper_erode_px (default 6 full-res px, env DGS_CDN_GRIPPER_ERODE_PX) via _erode (1 - max_pool of inverse, kernel 2r+1=13). Eroding the KEEP mask enlarges the EXCLUSION zone. WHY: the robot mask silhouette is imperfect; the moving gripper's edges otherwise leak into the change region and get falsely decoded. This erosion is FF-CDN-only — the tracker still reads the raw un-eroded keep mask.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Valid mask — coverage gate + depth HOLE rescue
DYNAMIC.idea: When rendered_alpha is present and scene_coverage_threshold>0 (default 0.5), keep = alpha_r > 0.5 (well-covered pixels). Then, if gt_depth is present, a pixel is ALSO kept (OR'd in) if the live sensor depth d satisfies live_depth_min_m < d < live_depth_max_m (defaults 0.05 m and 3.0 m). This rescues UNCOVERED holes: a pixel the rendered scene barely covers but where the live depth sensor sees a real near surface is a FILLABLE void (change to be decoded), whereas a genuine void with no live return stays dropped. Depth is used ONLY as this binary validity gate, never as a difference metric. keep is multiplied into valid.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: Step 2 downsamples both images by an integer factor ds = max(1, int(sqrt(H*W)/downsample_target_side)) (resolve_downsample_factor TRUNCATES via int(), it does NOT round; downsample_target_side default 150, env DGS_CDN_TARGET_SIDE), so SSIM always runs on ~150x150 cells regardless of native resolution/aspect. Pooling is MASKED: for each rgb, num=avg_pool2d(rgb*valid, ds, ds) and den=avg_pool2d(valid, ds, ds).clamp_min(1e-8), so pooled block colour = mean of VALID pixels only (excluded pixels contribute 0 to both num and den, no bleed). WHY: this is the speed + jitter-ignore lever — coarse blocks make the comparison robust to sub-block tracker/render jitter, and it caps SSIM compute by grid size.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: A pooled block's validity = (avg_pool2d(valid, ds, ds) >= block_valid_min_frac) where block_valid_min_frac defaults 0.0 — meaning ANY valid source pixel keeps the block (per-mask erosion already handled partial-validity blocks, so the fraction gate is effectively OFF). This valid_use grid is the region mask carried through SSIM and cleanup. When ds==1 the original full-res tensors and valid are used directly.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Masked Gaussian pre-blur on pooled images
DYNAMIC.idea: Before SSIM, each pooled RGB is Gaussian-blurred by _masked_blur with blur_kernel_size=5 (forced odd) and blur_sigma=0.75 (env DGS_CDN_BLUR_*). The blur is mask-normalized: num=conv2d(img*w, ker), den=conv2d(w, ker), result=num/den.clamp_min(1e-6) with w=region weight, and NaNs zeroed via nan_to_num — so excluded pixels don't bleed colour in. WHY: light blur removes single-pixel high-frequency noise that would spuriously raise the SSIM dissimilarity. sigma<=0 or size<=1 disables it.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: Step 3 converts both blurred images to grayscale with luma weights (0.2989 R + 0.5870 G + 0.1140 B), then computes per-pixel dissimilarity = 1 - SSIM via _ssim_dissim with a Gaussian window of ssim_window=5 (env DGS_CDN_SSIM_WINDOW; note compute_change_mask's getattr fallback of 11 is dead since cfg always sets 5) and fixed sigma 1.5. SSIM uses windowed local stats: mu_x,mu_y (conv with kernel), variances sx,sy, covariance sxy, constants c1=0.01^2, c2=0.03^2, ssim=((2 mu_x mu_y + c1)(2 sxy + c2))/((mu_x^2+mu_y^2+c1)(sx+sy+c2)) clamped to [0,1], score=1-ssim. score is then masked by region (score*region). Single-scale only — no multi-scale pyramid (the avg-pool already coarsens; window 5 keeps the halo tight, since a large window @ high ds bleeds ~50 full-res px). The continuous score is optionally stashed in debug_out['score'] upsampled to native for a JET heatmap dump.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Threshold to binary + AND with valid
DYNAMIC.idea: Step 4 thresholds the dissimilarity: binary = (isfinite(score) & (score > rgb_threshold)) where rgb_threshold=0.2 (env DGS_CDN_RGB_THRESHOLD) — a pixel is 'changed' when its 1-SSIM exceeds 0.2. binary is immediately multiplied by valid_use so only allowed pixels survive. The low 0.2 threshold is deliberately paired with a SMALL close kernel so faint scattered detections are not bridged into a solid square (see morphology).

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: On the binary change grid: _close(r=morph_close_px=2) = erode(dilate) fills genuine 1-2px holes INSIDE a detected region; then _open(r=morph_open_px=1) = dilate(erode) removes isolated single-px speckle. dilate/erode are implemented as max_pool2d (kernel 2r+1) on the binary / its inverse. WHY tiny radii: a large close (old 10 -> 21x21) BRIDGED scattered faint detections into a filled square (false positive), and a large open (old 3 -> 7x7) WIPED thin real change like object edges; close=2/open=1 fix holes/speckle only and leave region selection to the area filter.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: _keep_components runs scipy.ndimage.label on the cleaned binary and computes per-label areas via bincount (label 0/background zeroed). Selection is on the DOWNSAMPLED grid in units of grid cells: with keep_largest_only False (default cm.keep_largest_only=False), every component with area >= min_component_area (default 40 cells) is kept (np.isin); with largest_only True, only the single largest component is kept and only if its area clears 40. WHY: drops small noise blobs (40 cells balances 76 being too coarse and 10 being too noisy). After component selection the mask is re-AND'd with valid_use.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Upsample to native + final valid AND
DYNAMIC.idea: If ds>1 the cleaned grid mask is nearest-upsampled back to native HxW (TF.interpolate mode='nearest'), then multiplied by the full-resolution valid mask one final time. WHY mask AFTER SSIM and never black-out the input first: SSIM is a sliding window, so blacking pixels pre-score creates a fake edge that fires as change at the mask border, and it saves no compute (cost is grid-size). Returns (H,W,1) {0,1} float; an all-zero mask means 'no change' and downstream skips FF.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: After compute_change_mask returns, cdn_fn squeezes it to (H,W) bool raw_np and, on the FIRST CDN (restrict_to is None), CLEANS it by subtracting the tracked object's footprint: m_np = m_np & ~obj_np, where obj_np = _clean_object_footprint(object_mask>0.5, scale=object_mask_scale, dilate=object_mask_dilate_px). WHY (distinct from the step-1 valid exclusion): this is a hard second subtraction at native resolution guaranteeing a flat decoded patch is never inserted ONTO the tracked 3D object (which would smear it). The result list is [m_np] only if m_np.any(), else [] (FF skips). NOTE: this subtraction runs on BOTH first-CDN and re-CDN (it is inside the `if d.object_mask is not None` block, not gated on is_recdn).

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Object footprint enlargement about its own centroid
DYNAMIC.idea: _clean_object_footprint enlarges the object mask before subtracting: if object_mask_scale (default 1.1) differs from 1.0, it computes the footprint centroid (mean of nonzero ys,xs) and applies a warpAffine SCALING about that centroid (affine M = [[s,0,cx(1-s)],[0,s,cy(1-s)]], INTER_NEAREST), then UNIONs warped with the original (np.maximum) so the enlarged mask strictly CONTAINS the original. Then dilates by object_mask_dilate_px (default 0; kernel 2*dilate+1) if >0. WHY the 1.1 scale: it swallows the rendered-vs-live MISPLACEMENT RING around the object (the object renders slightly off from where the live sensor sees it), which would otherwise be detected as a false change halo.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Re-CDN render restriction by projected bbox
DYNAMIC.idea: When cdn_fn is called with restrict_to (the first CDN region, HxW bool), it is a region-restricted re-CDN. It computes the region's pixel bbox=(xs.min, ys.min, xs.max+1, ys.max+1); if the region is empty it returns []. Under the lock it calls scene_model.means_in_bbox_idx(d.camera, bbox, pad=crop_pad_px) (default pad 50) to get the indices of LIVE gaussians whose MEAN projects (OpenGL world->camera, z=-mc[2], u=fx*x/z+cx, v=fy*(-y/z)+cy, front z>1e-6) into the padded bbox, then renders ONLY those (render(restrict_idx=...)). WHY: it skips projecting/sorting the rest of the frame for the re-check.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Re-CDN AND-gate to first region (coupled with restricted render)
DYNAMIC.idea: On the re-CDN, after compute_change_mask + object-footprint subtraction, the mask is AND-gated to the first region: m_np = m_np & restrict_to. This is COUPLED with the restricted render: rendering only the in-bbox gaussians leaves everything OUTSIDE the bbox as bare background, so re-CDN would flag that whole outside as change — the AND-gate discards exactly that spurious outside change, keeping only change INSIDE the originally-detected region. Consequence: the replaced-surface cull keyed on this re-CDN can only ever delete geometry inside the first detected change region (never outside).

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.topic: Re-CDN driven as-if-culled by the FF orchestrator
DYNAMIC.idea: The re-CDN exists so the change mask reflects the scene AS-IF the in-front occluder cull already happened. In dynamic_feedforward, after the first regions=cdn_fn(d), it computes cull_in_front for first_region, then (deferred path) under the lock temporarily HIDES those rows via _set_hidden_fn(cull_idx), calls cdn_fn(d, restrict_to=first_region) to re-score against the would-be-culled scene, then unhides (_set_hidden_fn(None)) — the real delete is deferred to the atomic commit. If the re-CDN now returns no regions, FF skips ('no_recdn'). The non-deferred path commits the cull on its own surgery first, then re-CDNs. So the decode region is the re-CDN region, computed against the post-cull scene. (The orchestration method is FeedforwardWorker._run, NOT _run_ff_cycle.)

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: When cfg.debug.ff_debug_images is on (and data_dir set), each CDN call dumps to <data_dir>/dynamic_scene/_ff_debug/ via _dump_ff_debug: live RGB (d.rgb_bgr), rendered scene (rgb_r RGB->BGR), the per-pixel 1-SSIM score upsampled to native as a COLORMAP_JET heatmap (blue=0..red=1), the RAW change mask, and the CLEANED change mask, numbered NNNN with tag cdnA (first full CDN) or cdnB (region-restricted AND-gated re-CDN). Purely diagnostic; does not affect the mask.

DYNAMIC.title: Change detection (CDN) & change-mask cleaning
DYNAMIC.idea: The CDN/change-mask code itself is source-agnostic and identical for sim and real-HW: it consumes whatever rgb/depth/masks arrive in the FeedforwardDispatch. Real-HW only differs upstream in how d.camera pose and d.gripper_keep/object_mask are produced (DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA reparenting FK in ros_mask.py); no real-HW branch exists inside change_mask.py or the cdn_fn compute. SIM path is exactly the one documented above.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.idea: make_decode_fn(anysplat, cfg, intr) returns decode_fn(d, regions, snap) -> Optional[GaussTensors], the decode callback the FF worker calls. Inputs: d = the dispatch (live BGR rgb d.rgb_bgr, depth d.depth_m, camera d.camera with OpenGL c2w camera_to_worlds[0]); regions = the cleaned CDN change masks (only regions[0] is used as the single changed-region mask cdn_np); snap = an immutable GaussianSet snapshot (snap.params['means']) used only as the ICP target. It builds scene_intr = {fl_x,fl_y,cx,cy,w,h} once from the scene camera intrinsics intr. Returns None when there is no crop window or zero gaussians survive. The AnySplat round-trip is the long pole, so it runs outside the model_lock; the later insert is locked.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Crop windows around the change region (1 or 2 tiled)
DYNAMIC.idea: _crop_windows(cdn_np, pad) computes the change-mask bbox via np.where, then a SQUARE window of side size = min(max(bw,bh) + 2*pad, min(H,W)) centered on the bbox center, clamped inside the frame. pad = cfg.feedforward.crop_pad_px (default 50). If the bbox width bw exceeds the image short side min(H,W) it returns TWO square windows tiled at x0+size//2 and x1-size//2 (each its own AnySplat inference); otherwise ONE window. Square cropping avoids aspect distortion since AnySplat consumes a fixed 448x448 input. The window (left,top,size) is also passed downstream as scene_crop so pixels map back exactly.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: AnySplat input crop write + IPC round-trip
DYNAMIC.idea: For each window the code writes the square scene sub-image src_bgr[top:top+size, left:left+size] to a per-PID tmpfs PNG /dev/shm/dgs2_ff_crop_{pid}_{wi}.png (cv2.imwrite), calls anysplat.inference(crop_png, out_npz) which blocks on the worker, then pickle.load()s the worker's output from /dev/shm/dgs2_ff_ipc_{pid}_{wi}.npz. Both files are unlinked in a finally. The IPC is one JSON request line {'images':[crop],'output':npz} over the worker stdin and one JSON 'ok' reply line on stdout; the heavy gaussian arrays travel via the pickled npz on /dev/shm (tmpfs), NOT over the pipe. The worker uses pickle.dump (HIGHEST_PROTOCOL) instead of np.savez because np.savez CRC32-wraps each array (costly on the large features_rest); pickle is a flat dict-of-ndarrays memcpy. The crop is resized inside the worker's process_image to 448x448.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Single-view decode per window (the 'dual-view' is two crops, not stereo)
DYNAMIC.idea: AnysplatHandle.inference passes a list of ONE image ([crop_png]) to the worker, so each AnySplat forward in this live-sim path is monocular (one view). The 'two views' that appear are the two TILED crop windows from _crop_windows when the change bbox is wider than the image short side — each is a separate single-view inference whose decoded gaussians are concatenated. The worker still returns a (K,4,4) pred_extrinsic_c2w / (K,3,3) pred_intrinsic_norm but only index [0] is consumed (pred_extrinsic_c2w[0], pred_intrinsic_norm[0]).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Worker output conversion to Splatfacto conventions
DYNAMIC.idea: anysplat_worker._convert_gaussians_to_splatfacto turns the raw AnySplat gaussian into: means_canonical=g.means[0]; log_scales=log(g.scales clamped>=1e-12); opacity_logits=logit(opacity clamped to [1e-6,1-1e-6]); and harmonics sliced to the FIRST 16 SH coeffs ([...,:16]) then permuted (N,3,16)->(N,16,3), split into features_dc=harm[:,0,:] (N,3) and features_rest=harm[:,1:,:] (N,15,3) — dropping AnySplat's SH-4 band. _convert_pred_cameras emits pred_extrinsic_c2w and pred_intrinsic_norm (intrinsics NORMALIZED to [0,1], i.e. multiply by W/H to get pixels). Splatfacto uses SH up to degree 3 (16 coeffs); dropping the 4th band cuts the dominant payload before the H2D copy.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Camera convention: pred-pixel projection then canonical-CV->scene-GL flip
DYNAMIC.idea: reproject_anysplat_to_scene first projects each canonical gaussian into the AnySplat PRED camera (OpenCV: p_cam_cv = (means-t_pred)@R_pred, z forward, u=fx_p*x/z+cx_p, v=fy_p*y/z+cy_p with fx_p=pred_K_norm[0,0]*W_any etc.) to get pred-pixel (u,v). For ORIENTATION it maps the canonical-CV gaussian rotation into the scene OpenGL basis via M_rot = R_scene @ diag(1,-1,-1) @ R_pred^T applied to each gaussian rotmat before re-quaternizing. The diag(1,-1,-1) is the OpenCV->OpenGL axis flip (y and z negated). AnySplat predicts in an OpenCV-convention canonical frame; the scene/Nerfstudio camera is OpenGL (forward=-z, y up), so the rotation must be rebased or splats render mirrored/rotated.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Reproject through SCENE intrinsics + sensor depth, NOT AnySplat's predicted K
DYNAMIC.idea: The 3D placement IGNORES AnySplat's depth/scale. Each gaussian's pred-pixel (u,v) is mapped back to a true scene pixel (scene_crop branch: u_scene=u*(size/W_any)+left, v_scene=v*(size/H_any)+top, the exact inverse of the square crop+resize), the metric depth d_per_gauss is read from the live sensor_depth at (u_scene,v_scene) (fallback z_cam*global_s for no-depth pixels when drop_no_sensor_depth is False), and the world mean is BACK-PROJECTED through the SCENE intrinsics fx_s/fy_s/cx_s/cy_s in OpenGL form: p_cam_gl = [d*(u-cx)/fx, -d*(v-cy)/fy, -d], means_world = R_scene@p_cam_gl + t_scene. AnySplat's predicted focal length is wrong (~28% lateral error per the module docstring), so the scene K + real sensor depth pin inserts on the true surface. W_any=H_any=448 (_H_ANY/_W_ANY).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Per-gauss scale rescale to preserve image-space footprint
DYNAMIC.idea: Because each splat is repositioned to sensor depth d_per_gauss instead of its canonical pred depth z_cam, its scale is multiplied by s_per_gauss = d_per_gauss / z_cam (added in log-space: log_scales_world = log_scales + log(clip(s_per_gauss, 1e-9, None))). A splat moved twice as far must double its metric size to subtend the same pixel footprint, keeping the rendered silhouette consistent after the depth swap. An extra global log(scale_multiplier) is added if scale_multiplier != 1.0 (default 1.0 = no inflation).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Discard gates folded into ONE keep mask in reproject
DYNAMIC.idea: reproject composes all per-gaussian drops into a single boolean keep applied once to the six heavy arrays: (1) opacity gate opac=sigmoid(opacity_logits) >= opacity_min (default 0.05); (2) background gate — drop splats whose decoded color rgb_pred=features_dc*0.28209479177387814+0.5 is within background_tol=0.08 (per-channel abs, all-axes) of the Gazebo sky (0.86,0.92,1.0), killing sky-colored splats; (3) component-mask gate — keep only splats whose scene pixel (vs_idx,us_idx) lands inside the CDN change mask cdn_np (resized NEAREST to scene res if needed); (4) in-image gate (z_cam>1e-6 and (u,v) inside 448). Folding into one mask avoids re-indexing the (N,15,3) features_rest multiple times. SH_C0=0.28209479177387814 is the degree-0 SH basis constant.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: ICP refinement of scene_c2w before decode (live-sim default ON)
DYNAMIC.idea: When cfg.feedforward.icp_refine (default True, env DGS_FF_ICP) the decode first refines the scene camera pose: it builds the ICP target by _project_downsample(snap means, scene_c2w, scene_intr, stride=icp_stride) — projecting the full scene cloud through the scene camera and keeping, per stride-spaced pixel cell, the camera-NEAREST gaussian (front surface only, like a depth sensor) — then icp_refine_scene_c2w runs GPU point-to-plane ICP of the live sensor depth cloud against that target (max_iters=30, max_correspondence_distance/max_dist_m=0.02 m, min_pts=1000) and left-multiplies the result into scene_c2w (refined = T @ scene_c2w). icp_stride=4 (default) for BOTH source-depth and projected-target subsampling. Failure is caught and skipped (decode continues with the raw c2w).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.idea: _project_downsample projects means world->camera (p_cam=(means-t)@R, z=-p_cam[:,2] since OpenGL forward=-z), keeps in-frame points (z>1e-6 and 0<=u<W, 0<=v<H via u=fx*x/z+cx, v=-fy*y/z+cy), buckets them into stride-spaced cells cell=(u//stride)*(H//stride+2)+(v//stride), and per cell keeps only the camera-NEAREST gaussian using argsort-by-z then a stable argsort-by-cell so the first row per cell is the closest. Feeds ICP only the front surface the live depth sensor sees, not the full volumetric cloud. Returns all means unchanged if nothing is in view.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: voxel_dedup disabled in reproject; density shaping done in decode_fn
DYNAMIC.idea: decode_fn calls reproject with voxel_dedup_m=0.0 explicitly so reproject does NOT thin the cloud; instead the parts from each crop window are concatenated on the device into a g-dict (means/features_dc/features_rest/scales/quats/opacities) and density shaping runs once in decode_fn. reproject's voxel_dedup is a first-occurrence np.unique pick (no merge), whereas decode_fn wants the moment-match voxel_merge, so dedup is deferred to one place that sees all windows together.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Density-shaping subsample ceiling before corner kNN
DYNAMIC.idea: Before any kNN, if the concatenated insert count exceeds cfg.feedforward.density_max_points (default 80000) decode_fn randomly subsamples to that cap (torch.randperm[:cap] applied to every g array). The corner-detection GPU kNN spikes on a large revealed region; density shaping is cosmetic flat-fill so a capped subsample bounds the worst case. cap=0 disables (DGS_FF_DENSITY_MAX_PTS).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Cornerness gating: crease + boundary score (max of two signals)
DYNAMIC.idea: _corner_score gives each point a [0,1] cornerness = max of: (1) CREASE = local PCA surface-variation l0/(l0+l1+l2) from the covariance of its k neighbours (~0 flat, large where two surfaces fold), normalized by corner_var_scale=0.10; (2) BOUNDARY = ||mean(neighbours)-point|| / mean_neighbour_distance (~0 interior, large at a silhouette), normalized by corner_boundary_scale=3.0 (the config value decode_fn passes; the function's own default arg is 0.80). A point is a CORNER if score >= corner_merge_threshold=0.13. The kNN uses corner_knn_k=80 neighbours via _knn_indices (ONE Open3D CUDA NN build shared by score+halo; CPU cKDTree fallback). The boundary term catches flat boundary patches the crease/PCA metric is blind to.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.idea: _dilate_corner_mask grows the corner set by ONE neighbour hop: a point also becomes corner if ANY of its corner_halo_k nearest neighbours (default 50) is a detected corner, computed on the ORIGINAL mask (never fed back, so no cascade) via the SAME shared kNN sliced to halo_k+1. Decoupling from corner_knn_k lets the protective halo width be tuned independently of detection sharpness. halo_k=0 disables.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Flat vs corner split: voxel-merge + in-plane grow flats, pass corners raw
DYNAMIC.idea: After cornerness, decode_fn splits g into flat (~is_corner) and corner (is_corner). FLATS get: voxel_merge(flat, voxel_merge_m=0.001) then _grow_inplane(scales, grow_inplane_factor=2.0). CORNERS are concatenated back RAW (not merged, not grown). A 1mm voxel straddling an edge would fuse two surfaces into one splat poking past the corner, and growing an edge splat fills the void behind it. If there are too few points for cornerness (g count <= corner_knn_k) it just voxel_merges the whole set.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: _grow_inplane: enlarge the two surface axes, not the normal
DYNAMIC.idea: _grow_inplane(log_scales, factor) adds log(factor) to all three log-axes EXCEPT the SMALLEST (argmin per row = the surface-normal axis, set to +0.0 via scatter), so only the two in-plane axes grow. Enlarging the in-plane footprint fills sub-splat surface gaps without thickening the surface. factor<=1 is a no-op; default factor=2.0.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: voxel_merge moment-match fusion (fill voxel without inflating)
DYNAMIC.idea: voxel_merge buckets means by floor(means/voxel_m) int64 voxel, and for each multi-point voxel fuses members into ONE gaussian: opacity-weighted mean position/color; covariance = mean(member covariances Sigma_i = R diag(exp(2*log_s)) R^T) PLUS the covariance OF the member means about the cluster mean (the EXTENT/spread term that sizes the merged splat to fill the voxel); merged scale = 0.5*log(eigvals) and quat from eigvecs (_rotmat_to_quat_wxyz); merged opacity = cluster MAX (preserve coverage). Inputs are nan_to_num-sanitized (NaN log-scale->-7.0~=0.9mm), covariance symmetrized + ridged 1e-10*I, with a CPU eigh fallback to avoid a CUSOLVER crash on a degenerate cluster. Single-member voxels pass through. voxel_merge_m default 0.001 (1mm).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Final hard insert-scale clamp (uniform shrink, not per-axis)
DYNAMIC.idea: _clamp_log_scale is the definitive boundary cap applied last (decode.clamp stage): any gaussian whose LARGEST axis exp(log_max) exceeds max_scale_m=0.02 (2cm, default; DGS_FF_MAX_SCALE_M) is UNIFORMLY shrunk — shift=(log_max-log(max_scale_m)).clamp_min(0) subtracted from ALL three log-axes so the biggest axis becomes exactly the cap and the splat SHAPE is preserved (NOT a per-axis clamp that flattens it, NOT a cull). max_scale_m<=0 disables. Warns ONCE per process (global _clamp_warned). reproject already applies the same uniform-shrink with the same max_scale_m, plus an optional min_scale_m cull floor (default 0.0 = off).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: Decode output = GaussTensors handed back for insertion
DYNAMIC.idea: decode_fn returns a GaussTensors(means, features_dc, features_rest, scales, quats, opacities) built from the shaped+clamped g-dict on anysplat.device, or None if 0 rows. Optional debug hooks: DGS_DENSITY_DEBUG=1 prints a one-shot _density_report (N, bbox, NN spacing, 1/2/3mm dedup survivors); DGS_DUMP_INSERT writes one insert's means+scales npz; DGS_CORNER_DEBUG=1 prints corner-score quantiles. The returned tensors are the new gaussians for the changed region; the FF worker then inserts them (insert/cull lives in dynamic_feedforward, not here).

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.topic: AnysplatHandle: persistent worker wrapper + idempotent spawn
DYNAMIC.idea: AnysplatHandle wraps the persistent AnySplat subprocess in conda env 'anysplat_dynamic_gs' (default), timeout_s=60.0. _ensure() lazily constructs PersistentAnysplatWorker under a threading.Lock so a concurrent prewarm thread and the first inference cannot both spawn a worker; the worker is reused across all decodes. inference([crop_png], out_npz) delegates to the live worker. The worker is launched by invoking the env's python directly (~/miniconda3/envs/<env>/bin/python anysplat_worker.py --persistent) with that env's lib prepended to LD_LIBRARY_PATH and PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF defaulting to expandable_segments:True (shared-GPU fragmentation). AnySplat's pinned wheels are incompatible with the main env's torch stack, hence the sibling env.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.idea: prewarm() spawns+loads+self-warms the worker on a daemon background thread (non-blocking) so the model load overlaps the rest of pipeline/static setup instead of stalling the first FF decode; it is a no-op if already spawned or already prewarming. wait_ready() joins that thread (or spawns synchronously if prewarm wasn't used) so the model load is honest STARTUP latency rather than a mid-episode stall on the first decode. The worker itself runs a dummy 448x448 forward before reporting 'ready' (warm-up) so the FIRST real decode is at steady-state, not a cold start. pipeline.py creates AnysplatHandle(device) and calls prewarm() at load time (and wait_ready() before opening the live source); only spawned when ff_enabled.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.idea: PersistentAnysplatWorker startup blocks reading the worker's stdout until a {'status':'ready'} JSON line appears (model in VRAM), bounded by startup_timeout_s; if the process exits first it raises with the stderr tail. Each inference writes one JSON line {'images':[crop],'output':npz} to stdin, flushes, then readline-loops stdout for a {'status':'ok',...} (raises on 'error' or death), with a per-call timeout_s. The reply carries the worker's own t_forward_ms which decode_fn records separately (decode.worker_forward) so in-subprocess GPU cost is visible apart from IPC/pickle overhead. A FIFO-mode adopt() variant exists for cross-process handoff but the live-sim path uses the stdin/stdout persistent worker.

DYNAMIC.title: AnySplat feed-forward decode & reprojection
DYNAMIC.idea: This decode path is camera-source-agnostic: it consumes d.rgb_bgr/d.depth_m/d.camera regardless of source, so the DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini real-hardware variants (which only change how those frames are produced upstream) do not alter make_decode_fn or AnysplatHandle. They exist but are not part of this decode module.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: GaussianSet is the single owner of all live scene state: the 6 Gaussian params and 4 identity buffers. It does NOT own the tensors by copy — at construction it adopts the wrapped model's `gauss_params` dict in place (`self._params()` returns `self._model.gauss_params`, no copy) so the same Parameter objects are the SSOT. Every count-or-identity mutation funnels through ONE locked surgery API (cull / insert / cull_and_insert / write_object_pose / set_object_flags / write_instance_ids / reload_from_state_dict / enable_freelist), and every non-owning thread reads through an immutable atomic snapshot(). This chokepoint exists to eliminate unlocked-read races and surgery drift across the static->dynamic boundary. All surgery methods take `self._lock` (a threading.RLock passed in at construction — the SAME lock that guards the render/tracker/FF), and every count-changing method ends with `_sync_buffer_attr()` + `self._model.rebind()` + `_assert_invariant()` + `_bump()`.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: The 6 trainable params are named in `PARAM_NAMES = ("means", "features_dc", "features_rest", "scales", "quats", "opacities")`. This order is LOAD-BEARING and must never be reordered: optimizer groups, state_dict keys, and the inner nerfstudio SplatfactoModel all key off it. Shapes (n rows): means (n,3); features_dc (n,3) canonical band-0 SH; features_rest (n, sh_rest_dim, 3) where sh_rest_dim = `features_rest.shape[1]`; scales (n,3) in LOG-space; quats (n,4) wxyz with identity = [1,0,0,0]; opacities (n,1) as LOGITS (pre-sigmoid). `scales`/`quats`/`opacities` are stored in the same activation domain the renderer expects (log-scale, logit-opacity), so insert contracts must supply them already transformed.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: The 4 identity buffers: specs, dtypes, allocation
DYNAMIC.idea: `IDENTITY_BUFFER_SPECS` fixes 4 per-row identity buffers, each shape (n,1): `object_flags` (float32), `sam3d_init_target_flags` (float32), `object_instance_ids` (torch.long — the ONLY long buffer), `inserted_flags` (float32). They are owned by GaussianSet (NOT the nn.Module): persistence flows through GaussianSet.state_dict()/reload_from_state_dict(), not model.state_dict(). At construction all 4 are zero-allocated on the model's device and ALSO setattr'd onto the model (`model.object_flags`, etc.) purely as a convenience read accessor; `_sync_buffer_attr()` re-points those attrs after every surgery since surgery replaces the buffer tensors. A 5th buffer `current_active_mask` was intentionally dropped (all writers dead).

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: Identity buffer semantics + who writes each
DYNAMIC.idea: What each buffer means and its writer: (1) `object_instance_ids` (long) = per-object segmentation ID 1..K, stamped on insert via the `instance_id` arg and also bulk-rewritten by `write_instance_ids(mask, id)`; written by Phase-0b fusion (static_phase0b inserts survivors with object_flag=0.0 then scatters matched IDs via write_instance_ids) and by every FF/Phase-0b insert. (2) `inserted_flags` (float32) = 1.0 on any row added by `insert`/`cull_and_insert` (hardcoded `"inserted_flags": 1.0` in id_vals), 0.0 on the original seed; marks FF/Phase-0b-added rows so FF purge can target them (`inserted_flags & instance_id==insert_id`). (3) `object_flags` (float32) = the tracked-object/inserted-object flag; in dynamic_gs2 it is set ONLY by insert's `object_flag` arg (FF inserts pass object_flag=1.0; Phase-0b survivor inserts pass object_flag=0.0). `set_object_flags(mask,value)` exists but has NO production caller in dynamic_gs2 (only tests call it); object_flags is NOT written by the static seed pipeline. (4) `sam3d_init_target_flags` (float32) = always all-zeros; it is absent from id_vals so `id_vals.get(name, 0.0)` returns 0.0 and there is no value-writer anywhere — its expected runtime state is all zeros.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: snapshot() takes the lock, reads `c = self._count`, and returns a frozen GaussianSnapshot dataclass whose `params`/`buffers` are `.detach()[:c]` slices (live rows only) of every param + buffer, PLUS `buffers["gauss_uid"] = self._uid.detach()[:c]`, and carries `num_points=c` + `version=self._version` captured atomically under the lock. The dataclass is `frozen=True` (immutable bindings). Tensor STORAGE is shared-detached (O(1), no copy): because surgery REPLACES param tensors (cull/insert allocate new tensors or write into dead rows), an old snapshot keeps its old complete tensors and stays self-consistent. The accepted caveat: an in-place value write by the owner (write_object_pose / set_object_flags) mutates the shared storage, so an outstanding snapshot can eventually see those value changes — acceptable because the authoritative render holds the lock and in-place writes only touch the tracked object's rows. `__len__` returns num_points.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: Free-list: over-allocation, capacity vs count, _count==shape only when packed
DYNAMIC.idea: Two book-keeping ints: `_count` = live row count (logically present rows), `_capacity` = physically allocated rows (= `means.shape[0]`). Free-list mode (`freelist=True`, dynamic phase) over-allocates the param/buffer tensors (first insert grows via _grow_capacity) and keeps the `_count` live rows packed at [0:_count]; dead capacity rows [_count:_capacity] hold stale data invisible to every reader. Non-freelist (static phase) keeps the EXACT reallocating path: every cull/insert reallocates so `_count == _capacity == shape[0]` always. The freelist path is only safe in the dynamic phase because LR=0 + no_grad render make the over-allocated Parameter rows harmless (no gradient on dead rows). `num_points`/`count` both return `_count`; the dead tail is excluded from every read, persistence, mask, and snapshot. The ONLY consumer that sees the full capacity tensor is the render, which is given a [:count] VIEW.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: `enable_freelist()` flips the SSOT from exact-realloc (static) to free-list (dynamic) IN PLACE for the single-process handoff — no scene reload, keeps the warm models. It asserts `_count == _capacity` (rows must be packed, no dead tail) which is exactly the post-static state; then sets `_freelist=True`. From there the next insert begins over-allocating, identical in effect to a fresh `reload_from_state_dict(...) + freelist=True`. This is what lets the static-trained scene become the live dynamic scene without serializing/reloading.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: Because both swap-remove cull and tail-write insert REORDER rows, NO consumer may key on row position across surgeries. Every row carries a unique int64 `_uid` (shape (cap,1)) initialized as `arange(n)` and extended by a monotonic counter `_next_uid` that is NEVER reused (`_fresh_uids(m)` returns `arange(_next_uid, _next_uid+m)` then advances the counter). The uid is moved in LOCKSTEP with the 6 params + 4 buffers by every surgery (carried through swap-remove `_uid[holes]=_uid[tail_keep]`, through boolean-keep culls `_uid=_uid[keep]`, and assigned fresh on inserts). The uid is NOT persisted — it's rebuilt fresh as `arange(num_points)` on every reload, because the tracked-object reference (ReferenceObjectPose, captured at runtime in dynamic_track) is captured against the current uid space. This is the invariant that makes row reordering harmless: the tracked object is matched by uid, not index.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: cull() — boolean-keep vs swap-remove, protect_mask, dedup
DYNAMIC.idea: cull(indices, protect_mask) deletes rows. Input handling: indices are cast long+flattened, then clamped to valid `idx[(idx>=0)&(idx<n)].unique()` (out-of-range and duplicate indices are silently dropped). If `protect_mask` (a full length-n bool) is given, protected indices are silently removed from the cull set (`idx = idx[~pm[idx]]`). Two code paths: freelist -> `_cull_swap_remove`; non-freelist -> build a length-n keep-mask, set keep[idx]=False, and rebuild every param via `_set_param(name, param.detach()[keep])` + every buffer (`_buffers[name][keep]`) + the uid via `[keep]`, then `_capacity=_count=n-k`. Returns k = number actually culled. Always ends with sync+rebind+assert+bump.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: Swap-remove deletes k rows without realloc, copying <= k rows. Mechanism: new_n = n-k. Build `del_mask` (length n, True at idx). `holes = idx[idx < new_n]` are the deleted positions that survive truncation (need backfill). `tail = arange(new_n, n)` are the k rows about to fall off the end. `tail_keep = tail[~del_mask[tail]]` are the still-LIVE tail rows. By construction |holes| == |tail_keep|: every hole in the kept region is backfilled by a live tail row, while deleted tail rows simply vanish on truncation. For each param (`with torch.no_grad(): p[holes]=p[tail_keep]`), each buffer, and the uid, the live tail rows are moved down into the holes; then `_count=new_n`. Dead rows [new_n:] are left as stale data (invisible). This REORDERS rows — correctness depends entirely on the gauss_uid identity-key invariant.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: insert() — add rows, stamp identity, tail-write vs concat
DYNAMIC.idea: insert(tensors, object_flag, instance_id) adds m new Gaussians. First `tensors.validate(self.sh_rest_dim)` coerces shapes; m=0 returns an empty index range. Identity stamping uses `id_vals = {object_flags: float(object_flag), object_instance_ids: int(instance_id), inserted_flags: 1.0}` (sam3d_init_target_flags absent -> defaults to 0.0). Freelist path -> `_insert_tail_write` (write into the [count:count+m] dead region, grow x2 only on overflow). Non-freelist path -> `torch.cat([cur, new], dim=0)` for each param (new tensor cast to cur's dtype/device), `torch.cat` a `torch.full((m,1), id_vals.get(name,0.0))` tail for each buffer, `torch.cat` fresh uids, and set `_capacity=_count=old+m`. Returns `arange(old, old+m)` (the inserted index range, post-state coordinates). Ends with sync+rebind+assert+bump.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: Free-list insert core (no lock/rebind — caller owns those): if `old+m > _capacity`, call `_grow_capacity(old+m)`, then write the m new rows into [old:old+m] for each param (`with torch.no_grad(): p[old:old+m]=add[name].to(...)`), each buffer (`id_vals.get(name,0.0)`), and fresh uids; set `_count=old+m`. `_grow_capacity(need)` reallocates to `new_cap = max(int(need), _capacity*2, 1)` (grow by factor 2 -> amortized O(1) inserts): for each param/buffer/uid it allocates `torch.zeros((new_cap, *shape[1:]))` of the same dtype, copies the live [0:_count] rows into the front (`big[:c]=cur[:c]`), and sets `_capacity=new_cap`. New rows [_count:new_cap] are zero-filled (buffers) or stale/overwritten (params).

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: cull_and_insert() — atomic single-rebind surgery, no count-dip
DYNAMIC.idea: cull_and_insert folds a cull + insert into ONE locked surgery with ONE rebind, so nothing ever observes a culled-but-not-yet-filled scene (no flicker). Used by the FF Option-A flow. `new_count = n - k` is computed once; `_count` is written EXACTLY ONCE at the end (`_count = new_count + m`), so even a LOCKLESS num_points poll never sees the intermediate cull dip. Freelist path: (1) swap-remove DATA moves only (holes/tail_keep computed against new_count) while `_count` stays pinned at the old n; (2) grow if `new_count+m > _capacity`; (3) write inserts into [new_count : new_count+m] for params/buffers/uids; (4) the single `_count = new_count+m`. Non-freelist path does boolean-keep cull then concat insert and sets `_capacity=_count=new_count+m`. Returns `(k, arange(new_count, new_count+m))` (inserted range in POST-cull coordinates). The FF flow uses this to fold three deletes into one atomic op.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: write_object_pose() — uid->live-row resolve under lock, FF-race-safe
DYNAMIC.idea: write_object_pose(means_subset, quats_subset, subset_uid) writes the tracker's transformed pose ONTO the tracked object's live rows, matched by stable gauss_uid (NOT row index). The caller snapshots, computes transformed means/quats off the lock, and passes the uids those rows belong to. Inside the lock it resolves uid->row against the CURRENT `_uid[:n]`: `order = argsort(live_uid)`, `pos = searchsorted(live_uid[order], want).clamp(max=n-1)`, `rows = order[pos]`, then `valid = live_uid[rows] == want` to drop any uid culled since the snapshot. Only means + quats are written (`with torch.no_grad(): mp[rows]=...; qp[rows]=...`), cast to the param dtype/device. Asserts shapes match and that means/quats are finite. This is the in-place value write that is race-safe against concurrent FF cull/insert/reorder: a culled uid is simply skipped, and reordering can't misplace the pose since the match is by identity. Bumps version, returns rows written.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: set_object_flags / write_instance_ids — masked in-place value writes
DYNAMIC.idea: Both take a FULL-length (== count) bool mask and write into the live-row VIEW of a buffer in place, under the lock, bumping version (value-only writes, no count change, no rebind). `set_object_flags(mask, value)` does `self._buffers["object_flags"][:c][m] = float(value)` (exists but has no production caller in dynamic_gs2 — only tests call it). `write_instance_ids(mask, instance_id)` does `self._buffers["object_instance_ids"][:c][m] = int(instance_id)` — used by static_phase0b to scatter the matched segmentation ID onto fused rows. Both assert `mask.shape[0] == c` (the count). The `[:c]` slice ensures writes never touch dead capacity rows.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: rebind() coupling — GaussianSet does surgery, scene_model owns optimizer/LR
DYNAMIC.idea: WRAP seam: GaussianSet does the pure tensor surgery, then calls `self._model.rebind()` ONCE per count-changing surgery (inside the shared lock). GaussianSet itself NEVER sets LRs and NEVER renders. scene_model.rebind() re-points the inner nerfstudio model's optimizer param_groups at the new gauss_params Parameter objects (`o.param_groups[0]["params"] = [...]`), clears `o.state` (stale Adam moments would be wrong after row count changed), re-binds the means-grad hook (`_bind_means_grad_hook`), and re-asserts the phase LR policy (`enforce_phase_lr`). This separation is why GaussianSet has no nerfstudio knowledge — it replaces tensors, scene_model re-hooks the optimizer.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: snapshot() / GaussianSnapshot freelist book-keeping (count-provider render view)
DYNAMIC.idea: Render stays O(count) despite over-allocation: scene_model holds a `_count_provider` callable set via `set_count_provider(fn)` where fn() returns the live `_count`. When set, the render builds a param override (`_render_param_override`) that slices every gauss_param to `[:c]` (copy-free VIEWs) before handing them to gsplat, so dead capacity rows [_count:] never rasterize. When the provider is None (static), the render uses the full physical tensor. The pipeline pairs `enable_freelist()` + `set_count_provider(gset.count)` to wire the dynamic phase. The same [:count] slice is applied in the projection/mask helpers (`c = int(count_provider()) if set else means.shape[0]`).

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: reload_from_state_dict / state_dict — warm-cache persistence (live rows only)
DYNAMIC.idea: reload_from_state_dict(state_dict, num_points) reallocates the 6 params at exactly num_points (asserting each `shape[0]==num_points`, keys accepted as either bare name or `gauss_params.<name>`) and rebuilds the 4 buffers: present buffers are loaded (cast to the spec dtype, unsqueezed if 1-D), ABSENT buffers are zero-filled (legacy caches). It then sets `_capacity = _count = num_points` (packed, no dead tail), rebuilds `_uid = arange(num_points)` and `_next_uid = num_points`, syncs attrs, rebinds, asserts, bumps. The export `state_dict()` is the mirror: it exports ONLY the `[:count]` live rows (`.detach()[:c].cpu()`) as `gauss_params.<name>` for params + bare-name buffers — dead capacity rows are NEVER persisted, so the cache round-trips a clean packed scene.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: GaussTensors insert contract + validate() shape coercion
DYNAMIC.idea: GaussTensors is the decoder->insert contract: 6 tensors already in scene frame / log-scale / logit-opacity (so FF decoders and Phase-0b produce identical shapes). `validate(sh_rest_dim)` enforces/coerces: means must be (n,3); scales (n,3); quats (n,4); features_dc reshaped (n,1,3)->(n,3) and asserted (n,3); features_rest replaced with `zeros((n, sh_rest_dim, 3))` if empty OR if its width != sh_rest_dim (auto-coerce to the scene's SH width); opacities unsqueezed 1-D->(n,1) and asserted (n,1). `as_dict()` returns the 6 in PARAM_NAMES order. This guarantees every insert path agrees on layout before touching the SSOT.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: `activated_opacity(logits)` maps stored opacity LOGITS to [0,1] via sigmoid (`torch.sigmoid` for tensors, `1/(1+exp(-x))` numpy fallback) — opacities are stored as logits so the activated value is what masks/purges threshold against. `_set_param(name, tensor)` replaces a param in the model dict by wrapping `tensor.contiguous()` in a fresh `torch.nn.Parameter(..., requires_grad=<old param's requires_grad>)`, preserving leaf-ness and the grad flag across surgery (so the static phase keeps trainable params and the dynamic phase keeps them as it found them). `_assert_invariant()` (run at every surgery exit) checks `_capacity == means.shape[0]`, `0 <= _count <= cap`, and that uid + all 6 params + all 4 buffers share exactly `cap` rows.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.topic: build_default_gauss_tensors — seed/test default GaussTensors with constants
DYNAMIC.idea: build_default_gauss_tensors(new_xyz, new_rgb, sh_degree, sh_rest_dim, device, dtype) builds a default GaussTensors for the seed + tests (FF/Phase-0b build their own). Mechanics: log-scales from kNN spacing via `_knn_mean_dist` (k=3 nearest, `torch.cdist` then `topk(k+1, largest=False)` excluding self col 0, `clamp_min(1e-6)`; degenerate n<=1 -> 0.01) repeated across 3 axes in log-space (`log(spacing)`); features_dc = RGB2SH `((rgb-0.5)/_RGB2SH_C0).reshape(n,3)` with `_RGB2SH_C0 = 0.28209479177387814` (SH band-0 constant); features_rest = zeros (n, sh_rest_dim, 3); quats = identity (col 0 = 1.0); opacities = `full(-2.1972246)` = logit(0.1) (so activated opacity seeds at 0.1). Also `uniform_shrink_log_scales(log_scales, max_scale_m, min_scale_m)` is the shared scale-hygiene helper: rows whose largest exp(scale) axis > max_scale_m are uniformly shrunk in log-space (`out += log(max_scale_m/largest)`), and a keep-mask drops rows whose largest axis < min_scale_m.

DYNAMIC.title: Gaussian scene representation & surgery (SSOT)
DYNAMIC.idea: GaussianSet itself contains NO real-hardware branches — it is source-agnostic tensor surgery and identity book-keeping. The sim vs real-HW divergence (DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini) lives upstream in the source/mask/publisher layer, not in this module; the SSOT behaves identically for the live-sim path described above.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: SceneModel holds an inner nerfstudio SplatfactoModel whose `gauss_params` ARE the GaussianSet tensors (the same Python Parameter objects, no copy). At construction it builds a SplatfactoModelConfig and `.setup(...)` with `seed_points=(sxyz, srgb)` so the model's initial gauss_params come from the seed point cloud, then exposes `self.model.gauss_params` directly via a `gauss_params` property. WHY: GaussianSet owns all count/identity surgery on the tensors; SceneModel only provides render/train behavior over those exact tensors, shielding every other module from nerfstudio internals. The 6 gauss param names it operates on are fixed: `means, features_dc, features_rest, scales, quats, opacities` (`_PARAM_NAMES`).

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `rebind()` re-points the inner model's optimizers at the (possibly NEW) Parameter objects after GaussianSet replaces a tensor: for each optimizer named in gauss_params it sets `o.param_groups[0]['params'] = [self.model.gauss_params[name]]` and calls `o.state.clear()` (drops stale Adam moment buffers that referenced the old tensor); it also updates `model._optimizers_wrapper.parameters[name]` if present. Then it re-binds the means-grad hook and re-asserts the phase LR policy. WHY: count/identity surgery (insert/purge/free-list compaction) creates new Parameter objects, so the optimizer must be re-aimed at them WITHOUT copying the tensor data; called BY GaussianSet (gaussian_set.py calls `self._model.rebind()` after surgery) inside the shared lock so the swap is atomic.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `render(camera, restrict_idx)` -> `(rgb HxWx3, depth HxWx1, alpha HxWx1)`. It calls `_render` which moves the camera to device, reshapes a 2D `camera_to_worlds` into a batch of 1 (`cam.reshape((1,))`), sets `model.eval()`, then runs `self.model.get_outputs(cam)` under `torch.no_grad()` (gsplat rasterization producing the rgb/depth/accumulation dict). It reads `out['rgb']`, `out['depth']`, and alpha as `out.get('accumulation', out.get('alpha'))` (accumulation IS the alpha channel). MUST be called under the render_lock. WHY: a single uniform forward-render entry point that the viser-direct render thread + mask + Phase-0b all funnel through.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `_render_param_override(restrict_idx)` builds an `nn.ParameterDict` to render IN PLACE OF the full gauss_params, combining three copy-cheap transforms over the 6 param names: (1) free-list `[:c]` slice where `c = count_provider()` so over-allocated dead capacity rows `[c:]` never rasterize (pure views, no copy); (2) deferred-cull hide: clone ONLY the (N,1) `opacities` tensor and set hidden rows to `-30.0` so `sigmoid(-30)~0` makes them vanish without deleting from the SSOT; (3) restrict_idx: gather only those live rows so the rasterizer projects+sorts only that subset. Returns `None` (fast path = render full tensor) when `c>=phys` AND no hidden rows AND no restrict_idx. _render swaps `model.gauss_params` to the override, renders, and restores the saved params in a `finally`. WHY: must keep gauss_params an nn.Module child (override is an nn.ParameterDict), and avoid full-tensor copies for these cheap masking ops. The -30 logit is load-bearing: it relies on opacities being pre-sigmoid.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `set_count_provider(fn)` stores a callable `fn() -> live row count`. When set, every render path reads `c = int(self._count_provider())` and feeds gsplat a `[:c]` VIEW of each gauss_param; when None (default, static phase), it uses the full physical `means.shape[0]`. WHY: in the dynamic phase GaussianSet over-allocates capacity and uses a free-list (swap-remove), so the physical tensor has dead rows past `count`; the count slice ensures only the live prefix rasterizes. In dynamic, pipeline sets it to `lambda: gset.count`.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `set_hidden_indices(idx)` stores a long-tensor of row indices to VIRTUALLY hide (zero opacity) at render time without deleting them from the SSOT; None clears it. In `_render_param_override` the render clones only the (N,1) opacity, filters indices to in-range `(hide>=0)&(hide<N)`, and sets those rows to `-30.0`. WHY (FF Option A): when re-CDN must render the scene as-if-culled but the real cull is held back to commit atomically with the feedforward insert, this avoids a cull-without-insert flicker. MUST be set/cleared under render_lock around the render that should honor it; pipeline passes `sm.set_hidden_indices` as the set_hidden_fn and clears it with `set_hidden_indices(None)` after the atomic op.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `set_phase(phase)` flips `self.phase` in place then re-binds the means-grad hook and re-asserts the phase LR policy (no model rebuild). Static->dynamic hand-off in one process: pipeline pairs `sm.set_phase('dynamic')` with `gset.enable_freelist()` + `sm.set_count_provider(lambda: gset.count)` to reach the same state a fresh dynamic-phase load would produce. WHY: avoids reloading the scene; the phase change is purely about LR policy + means-freezing, not geometry.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `_bind_means_grad_hook()` removes any prior hook, then in the DYNAMIC phase registers a backward hook on `means` that returns `torch.zeros_like(g)` — hard-zeroing the means gradient so no optimizer step can move seed positions even if a stray backward fires. In STATIC phase no hook is bound (it relies on means LR=0 instead). Re-bound on every set_phase and rebind. WHY: belt-and-suspenders against the seed point positions drifting during the dynamic runtime, which is a tracker-only/FF-only mutation regime.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: Background composite color is the fixed Gazebo sky `_GAZEBO_SKY = (0.86, 0.92, 1.0)`. __init__ calls `model.set_background(tensor(_GAZEBO_SKY))`, then OVERRIDES `self.model._get_background_color = lambda: _sky.to(device)`. WHY the override: Splatfacto's default `background_color='random'` returns a RANDOM background while `self.training` is True, which would train against the wrong photometric bias; forcing the constant sky makes the composite background deterministic even during static training. `_empty_outputs` and the public `_get_background_color()` also return this sky color (reshaped to (1,1,3) and expanded to HxWx3).

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: When a region-restricted render selects zero gaussians (`restrict_idx.numel()==0`), `_render` short-circuits to `_empty_outputs(cam)` instead of calling gsplat with an empty tensor: it reads camera H/W, fills rgb with the background sky `expand(H,W,3).clone()`, and returns depth and accumulation as `zeros(H,W,1)`. WHY: gsplat rasterizing an empty gaussian set is undefined/crashy; this returns a valid all-background image (rgb=bg, alpha=0, depth=0).

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `render_object_mask(camera, instance_mask, alpha_thr=0.5)` -> bool HxW silhouette of ONLY the gaussians selected by a boolean `instance_mask` (len==count). It slices each param to the live prefix `[:c][m]`, detaches, swaps `model.gauss_params` to that subset nn.ParameterDict, renders, reads alpha = `out.get('accumulation', out.get('alpha'))`, restores the saved params in `finally`, and thresholds `alpha[...,0] > alpha_thr` (default 0.5). Returns all-False (zeros HxW bool) if the subset is empty (`m.sum()==0`) or alpha is None. WHY: gives a per-instance occupancy mask by rendering the object alone; pipeline.py and Phase-0b use it to localize a tracked/segmented object in image space. The 0.5 default alpha threshold is the silhouette cutoff.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `means_in_bbox_idx(camera, bbox=(l,t,r,b), pad=0)` projects each live mean into the image and returns the long-tensor indices whose projection falls inside the padded pixel bbox — a cheap project-only (no rasterize) used to build `restrict_idx`. Math: takes c2w `R,t`, computes camera coords `mc = (means - t) @ R` (OpenGL convention), `z = -mc[:,2]`, front-face gate `z > 1e-6`, then `u = fx*(mc[:,0]/zz)+cx`, `v = fy*(-mc[:,1]/zz)+cy` (note the Y flip, where zz clamps non-front z to 1), and keeps fronts with `u in [l-pad, r+pad)` and `v in [t-pad, b+pad)`. WHY: lets the re-CDN render only project+sort gaussians inside the changed region, skipping the rest. Called by dynamic_ff_backends with a pad.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `get_outputs_with_info(camera)` -> (outputs, info): runs a no-grad full-tensor `model.get_outputs(cam)` (which sets `self.model.info` as a side effect) and returns `model.info`, the gsplat per-gaussian meta dict containing `means2d/radii/depths` (radius is ONLY available here, not in the rgb outputs). It asserts `radii.reshape(-1).shape[0] == c` (count consistency between gsplat output and the live row count) when `radii` is present. WHY: Phase-0b's existing-object-subset and slab queries need projected center/radius/depth per gaussian; must be regenerated per object because insert() changes N and stales a prior info.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.topic: scene box (aabb) sizing + seed normalization + SH degree
DYNAMIC.idea: __init__ derives the SceneBox aabb from the seed extent: `ext = sxyz.abs().max()`, `a = max(ext*1.0, 1.0) * aabb_scale` (aabb_scale default 4.0), giving a symmetric box `[[-a,-a,-a],[a,a,a]]`. Seed rgb is normalized to Splatfacto's expected [0,255] range: if `srgb.max() <= 1.0+1e-6` it multiplies by 255. `sh_degree` is read from `cfg.static_train.sh_degree` (default 3). The model is configured with `random_init=False` (use the provided seed points), and SH render is forced full-band via `model.step = 30000`, with `crop_box=None`. WHY: a metric, non-recentered scene box scaled to the seed; full SH bands at render time.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: SplatfactoModelConfig is built with `num_downscales` and `resolution_schedule` (defaults 0 and 100). These drive Splatfacto's coarse-to-fine image resolution: `1 + 100` means half-resolution for the first 100 steps then full; `num_downscales=0` = full-res always (the render/dynamic path always uses 0). Image size itself is taken from the camera (H/W read from `camera.height`/`camera.width` in `_empty_outputs`/`render_object_mask`), not hard-coded here. WHY: the static-train coarse-to-fine schedule is a config detail SceneModel passes through; in render-only/dynamic phase it is disabled (0).

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: If `dynamic_gs.utils.no_refine_strategy.NoRefineStrategy` imports (`_HAVE_NOREFINE`), __init__ sets `model.strategy = NoRefineStrategy()` and `model.strategy_state = strategy.initialize_state(scene_scale=1.0)`; otherwise falls back to whatever Splatfacto defaults to. WHY: Splatfacto's default clone/split/prune densification would add/remove gaussians on its own, but in this pipeline ALL count changes are surgical (GaussianSet), so the post-backward refine must be a no-op to keep the SSOT the single owner of the row count.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: `attach_render_lock(lock)` stores an RLock; render/render_object_mask/get_outputs_with_info all document MUST-hold-render_lock, and set_hidden_indices must be set/cleared under it. WHY: every render temporarily swaps `model.gauss_params` (override/subset/restore) which is not thread-safe against concurrent tracker writes + FF inserts; a single lock guards every tracker write + FF insert + render in the live pipeline so a render never sees half-mutated tensors.

DYNAMIC.title: Scene rendering wrapper (Splatfacto bind)
DYNAMIC.idea: This module is camera-convention/source-agnostic: it renders whatever Camera it is handed and contains NO DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson / ZED-Mini branches — the real-vs-sim camera mount differences are handled upstream in ros_mask.py, not in the render wrapper. The sim live path and recorded path both call the same `render`/`render_object_mask` here.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: The live viewer never ships Gaussian data to the browser for client-side WebGL; instead a dedicated server-side render thread (`_render_loop`, daemon thread named 'viser-direct-render') reads each connected client's viser camera, rasterizes the scene to an RGB image on the GPU via the pipeline's `render_fn`, composites a canvas, and pushes it as the client's background with `client.scene.set_background_image(canvas, format='jpeg', jpeg_quality=self.jpeg_quality)`. The browser only displays a JPEG. WHY: keeps all Gaussian state + the model on the server (the bridge holds NO model — `render_fn` is the only handle), so the same `SplatfactoModel` tensors the tracker mutates are exactly what is shown, with no per-frame upload of point clouds.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.topic: single shared model_lock guards tracker write + FF insert + render
DYNAMIC.idea: There is ONE lock (constructed in the static-phase build, returned as `lock` from `build_loaded_scene`, threaded into the `DynamicLoop`, the `FeedforwardWorker`, and the viewer). The viewer's `render_fn` is `def _render_fn(cam): with lock: rgb,_,_ = sm.render(cam); return rgb` — i.e. the render thread acquires the SAME lock the tracker and feedforward inserts hold while mutating Gaussians. The bridge itself holds NO lock; it carries only `render_fn`, so all serialization lives in that closure. WHY: a render must never read half-mutated Gaussian tensors (tracker rigid transform or an FF insert mid-write), so the lock makes 'apply a mutation' and 'render a frame' mutually exclusive against the live model state.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.topic: event-driven render coalescing via a single wake Event
DYNAMIC.idea: Rendering is event-driven, not fixed-Hz. `request_render()` (and every GUI callback, client-connect, finger/feed/mode change) calls `self._wake.set()`. The render loop blocks on `self._wake.wait(timeout=1.0)`, then immediately `self._wake.clear()`s and renders once per wake. Because a threading.Event coalesces (multiple `set()`s before the loop wakes collapse to one), a burst of N tracker ticks that each request a render yields at most one render pass, and the 1.0 s timeout guarantees a periodic liveness/stop check even with no events. WHY: avoids busy-polling and avoids rendering faster than mutations actually occur, while never lagging behind the latest model state (each pass pulls live state).

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.topic: in-place background replacement avoids per-call new-node white flash
DYNAMIC.idea: Every push reuses the SAME mechanism — `client.scene.set_background_image(...)` — which atomically replaces the single background image rather than adding a new scene-graph node per frame. The bridge keeps no growing list of handles; each render overwrites the background in place. WHY: creating a fresh scene-graph node per update would broadcast a new node and momentarily blank the view (a visible white flash); a single atomic image swap has no intermediate empty state.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: The pipeline calls `bridge.update_tracked_camera(c2w_4x4)` once per tracker tick, storing `self._follow_c2w` (under `self._lock`); this call rate also drives the HUD tracker-Hz EMA. Render-panel-1 default source is 'Top' (`self._gui_r1_src.value='Top'`), a bird's-eye ORBIT of that tracked capture pose — NOT the user's free viser camera. When a panel's source is 'Cam' the panel renders directly at the tracked c2w; 'Top/Left/Right' orbit it; only 'Manual' uses the dragged viser orbit camera. WHY: the operator wants to watch the moving tracked object from a stable, scene-following viewpoint, independent of where the browser camera happens to point.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.topic: set_initial_camera on first frame fixes the 'object looks misplaced' bug
DYNAMIC.idea: On the first live frame the pipeline calls `bridge.set_initial_camera(fr.c2w_4x4)` (guarded by a one-shot `_cam_init` flag). The bridge stores `_initial_c2w` and `_apply_initial(client)` snaps each client's viser camera to it AT MOST ONCE (tracked in `self._applied` by `client_id`), converting nerfstudio OpenGL c2w to viser via `R_viser = R_nerf @ _FLIP_YZ` and `client.camera.wxyz = _rotmat_to_quat_wxyz_np(R_viser)`, `client.camera.position = c2w[:3,3]`. WHY: viser otherwise opens at an arbitrary default pose, so a correctly-placed object renders against a mismatched viewpoint and LOOKS misplaced versus the camera-feed thumbnail; snapping to the live frame-0 pose aligns the two. The at-most-once guard prevents overriding the operator once they start navigating.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: `_compose` builds a canvas of shape `(2*render_h, 2*render_w, 3)` uint8 (via np.empty then filled with the Gazebo sky `(0.86,0.92,1.0)*255`). Layout by `VIEW_MODES`: 'Camera' = feed resized to fill the whole 2H x 2W canvas (no render call at all); '1 render' = render-1 in bottom-left `[H:2H, 0:W]` + camera feed (cv2.resize to WxH) in bottom-right `[H:2H, W:2W]`; '2 render' = additionally render-2 in the top-centre at `x0 = W//2`, `[0:H, x0:x0+W]`. Canvas footprint is constant across modes. Default mode is '1 render' (`DEFAULT_VIEW_MODE`). WHY: side-by-side render vs real camera feed lets the operator visually validate alignment; constant footprint avoids the browser viewport resizing when switching modes.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: `ViserBridge.__init__` defaults: `render_size=(1280, 800)` -> `self.render_w=1280, self.render_h=800` (each panel's render resolution; the composite canvas is therefore 1600 tall x 2560 wide), and `jpeg_quality=88` passed to every `set_background_image(..., format='jpeg', jpeg_quality=88)`. The pipeline constructs `ViserBridge(cfg.viser, device=device)` WITHOUT overriding render_size/jpeg_quality, so these defaults are the live-sim values. `cfg.viser` (ViserConfig) supplies only `enabled=True` and `port=8081`. WHY: JPEG (lossy) keeps the pushed-image bandwidth low for the browser; 88 trades quality vs size; 1280x800 per panel is the per-view render resolution fed to the rasterizer.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: The viser server binds `viser.ViserServer(port=self.port)` where `self.port = int(getattr(cfg,'port',8081))` and `ViserConfig.port = 8081` by default. The viewer URL printed on attach is `http://localhost:8081`. WHY: a fixed dedicated port distinct from nerfstudio's viewer port keeps the viser-direct surface separate; the operator always connects to 8081.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: `update_camera_feed(rgb_or_bgr, is_bgr=True)` early-returns if disabled or `not self._server.get_clients()` (no point storing a feed nobody is watching), else converts BGR->RGB via `rgb_or_bgr[..., ::-1]` when `is_bgr` and stores a contiguous copy in `self._feed_rgb` under `self._lock`. The pipeline feeds `fr.rgb_bgr` each tick. The render thread snapshots `self._feed_rgb` under the lock and `cv2.resize`s it into the bottom-right (or full canvas in 'Camera' mode). WHY: the real-vs-render side-by-side needs the live camera image in RGB; the no-client guard avoids wasted copies; the contiguous copy decouples the producer from the render thread.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: `update_finger_points(finger_l, finger_r)` stores two world points (each (3,) or None); `_clean` rejects non-(3,) and all-zero points (a point at the world origin is treated as 'unavailable'). `_draw_finger_markers` projects each into the panel using the SAME math as the FF cull: camera coords `xc = R.T @ (X - t)` from the panel's OpenGL c2w, `fwd = -xc[2]` (skip if `fwd <= 1e-4`, behind camera), then `u = fx*(xc[0]/fwd)+cx`, `v = fy*(-xc[1]/fwd)+cy`. Intrinsics are taken from the render template and scaled to the panel by `sx=W/tw, sy=H/th` if sizes differ. Drawn as a filled circle radius `r = max(4, round(0.012*min(W,H)))` with a white halo of `r+2`; left pad green `(60,220,60)` BGR, right pad red `(60,60,235)`. Drawn LAST so markers sit on top. A GUI checkbox 'Gripper markers' (default True) gates them; when off, `finger_world=(None,None)`. WHY: overlays where the gripper fingertips are in every scene render, validating tracker/FF placement against the actual contact points.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: `_secondary_view_c2w` builds an orbit camera from the tracked OpenGL c2w looking at a pivot `TOP_VIEW_PIVOT_M = 0.5` m ahead (`pivot = p + fwd*pivot_dist`, `fwd = -R[:,2]`). 'Top' (bird's-eye) pitches `-deg` about the camera's OWN right axis via Rodrigues `_axis_angle_to_R(right, deg2rad(-deg))` and orbits the eye about the pivot. 'Left'/'Right' are LEVEL side views: it projects fwd onto the horizontal plane (removing the `WORLD_UP=(0,0,1)` component), rotates azimuth `-deg` (Left) or `+deg` (Right) about world-up, places the eye at `pivot - new_fwd*pivot_dist` (target height), and builds a lookAt c2w with columns right/up/back = (x=cross(U,back), y=cross(back,x), back=-new_fwd). Default angles `ORBIT_DEFAULT_DEG={'Top':45,'Left':90,'Right':90}`, slider range 0..180 step 5; switching a panel to an orbit dir snaps its slider to that default (`_snap_angle`). WHY: gives stable, gravity-levelled inspection views of the tracked object (flat horizon despite the capture camera's down-tilt) without the operator manually flying the camera.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: On the READ path, `_build_camera_from_viser` turns a viser client camera (position, wxyz quaternion, vertical `fov` radians, default 60deg) into a nerfstudio Cameras: `R_nerf = R_viser @ _FLIP_YZ` (where `_FLIP_YZ = diag(1,-1,-1)`, mapping viser's Y-down/Z-forward local frame to nerfstudio OpenGL Y-up/Z-back), `c2w[:3,3]=position`, and intrinsics `fy = 0.5*H/tan(fov/2)`, `fx = fy`, `cx=0.5*W`, `cy=0.5*H`. The WRITE path (`_apply_initial`) applies the same `R_viser = R_nerf @ _FLIP_YZ` since `_FLIP_YZ` is its own inverse. WHY: the server renders nerfstudio Cameras but viser supplies/consumes OpenGL-at-local-frame poses; without this flip the rendered view would be wrong-handed (upside-down/mirrored).

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.topic: HUD overlay (tracker Hz, FF Hz, view/source labels) via EMA
DYNAMIC.idea: `update_tracked_camera` and `note_ff_tick` each timestamp with `time.perf_counter()` and update an EMA of the inter-call interval (`_ema(prev,sample,a=0.2)` = `0.8*prev + 0.2*sample`). `_hud_lines` converts to `1/dt_ema` Hz ('-- Hz' until a sample exists; FF shows 'off' until `_ff_active`) and emits ['track ...','FF ...']. The render thread appends `view: <mode>`, and per active render `R1:/R2:` source labels (`'<src> <deg>deg'` for orbit dirs), then `cv2.putText` draws each line at `(16, 42+i*36)`, FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX scale 1.0, color `(20,20,20)`, thickness 2. WHY: gives the operator a live readout of tracker/feedforward rates and exactly which view each panel is showing, with EMA smoothing so the numbers don't jitter per tick.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.topic: 'Camera' mode skips render_fn entirely (lock-contention escape hatch)
DYNAMIC.idea: When the live view mode is 'Camera', the render loop pushes only the resized camera feed and `continue`s WITHOUT ever calling `render_fn` (the comment notes 'NO render_fn call at all (compute saved)'). This means the render thread never takes the shared model lock in that mode, so it cannot contend with the tracker/FF. The other modes call `render_fn` once (1 render) or twice (2 render: `_render_for` for R1 and R2). WHY: lets the operator drop to a zero-render mode to maximize tracker throughput / eliminate render-side lock contention when they only need to watch the raw feed.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: `_on_connect` immediately pushes a placeholder background filled with Gazebo sky `(0.86,0.92,1.0)*255` (`format='jpeg'`), calls `_apply_initial` to snap the camera, and `self._wake.set()` so the first real frame renders without waiting for a tracker tick. All GUI handlers (view-mode click, render-source click, angle sliders, gripper-marker checkbox) call `_sync_gui_visibility` (showing render-N controls only when that render is active and its angle slider only for orbit sources) and `self._wake.set()`. WHY: a connecting client sees an immediate, correctly-coloured screen and the live scene on the next pass; GUI changes take effect instantly via the same wake mechanism rather than waiting for the next mutation.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
