DYNAMIC.topic: WHY NOT the nerfstudio viewer — no render-interrupt under the shared lock
DYNAMIC.idea: This module is the ONLY sanctioned live-viz surface (per its docstring, Invariant #9); the nerfstudio viewer is never used. The bridge's render path calls `render_fn` -> `with lock: sm.render(cam)` directly, with no render-state-machine and no render-interrupt exception wrapping. WHY (per CLAUDE.md Invariant #9): the nerfstudio viewer wraps get_outputs in an IOChangeException render-interrupt that, combined with this single shared model_lock, can deadlock; viser-direct's plain render-thread-with-Event design has no interrupt and no state machine, so it cannot deadlock against the FF/tracker lock.

DYNAMIC.title: Live visualization (viser-direct)
DYNAMIC.idea: `close()` sets `_closing` + `_stop` + wakes the loop, joins the render thread (timeout 3.0 s), then `self._server.stop()`. `request_render` is a no-op once `_closing`. If viser is unavailable (`_HAVE_VISER` False) or `cfg.enabled` is False, the bridge sets `self.enabled=False`, never starts a server/thread, and the push methods early-return (guarded by `if not self.enabled`) — so the pipeline runs headless unchanged. WHY: graceful teardown avoids orphaned threads/servers between runs, and the headless guard lets the same pipeline run without a display.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: The sensor unit is a frozen dataclass `Frame` = one synced RGB-D-mask-pose tuple in the producer's CPU/numpy domain. Fields: `seq:int` (monotone, source-assigned, starts at 1), `stamp_sec:float` (capture event-time of the sensor/sim clock, explicitly never now()), `rgb_bgr` (H,W,3) uint8 in cv2 BGR order, `depth_m` (H,W) float32 in METRES with 0 meaning invalid/no-return, `mask_keep` (H,W) uint8 in {0,1} where 1==keep (robot pixels excluded), `c2w_4x4` (4,4) float64 OpenGL camera->world, and two optional gripper-pad world points `finger_l`/`finger_r` (3,) float64 each defaulting to zeros (zeros == not-available, e.g. recorded data; viewer skips a marker at the world origin). Frozen so the object survives the SHM copy-out boundary unchanged. Depth being float32 metres at this boundary (not uint16-mm) means every downstream consumer is unit-agnostic; the uint16-mm-on-disk form is internal to ReplaySource only.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `Intrinsics` is a frozen dataclass carrying the pinhole camera model: `width,height` (ints) and `fx,fy,cx,cy` (floats). It is the per-segment camera contract: written once into the SHM header by the producer and re-derived on attach by every reader, so consumers never hardcode resolution or focal length.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: Cross-process safety is gated by three constants: `LAYOUT_VERSION=2` (bumped on any change to Frame fields or slot layout), `SHM_MAGIC=b"DGS1"` (4-byte tag; a mismatch means a foreign/stale segment), and `DEFAULT_SHM_NAME="dgs_frame_v1"` (the POSIX segment name). On attach `read_header` raises ValueError if magic != SHM_MAGIC or version != LAYOUT_VERSION, so a producer/consumer schema drift fails loudly instead of reading garbage. `frame.py` is the single owner of these; shm_channel/adapters import them, never redefine.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: The ring has `DEFAULT_NUM_SLOTS=4` slots; it is a drop-oldest / latest-wins ring, NOT a queue. A frame is written into slot `seq % num_slots` (so slot reuse wraps every 4 frames) and the consumer always reads only the freshest slot via `header.latest_seq % num_slots`. There is no backpressure: a slow consumer simply misses intermediate frames (mirrors live drop-behaviour). num_slots is propagated from the producer into the header and recomputed identically on the consumer so both sides agree on the modulus.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: The segment begins with a fixed header packed little-endian, no-padding, format `_HDR_FMT="<4sIIIIddddqII"` = magic(4s), version(I), height(I), width(I), num_slots(I), fx(d), fy(d), cx(d), cy(d), latest_seq(q), ready(I), shutdown(I); `_HDR_SIZE=68` bytes. Mutable control fields are written in place at precomputed offsets: `_OFF_LATEST_SEQ=52`, `_OFF_READY=60`, `_OFF_SHUTDOWN=64`. `pack_header` writes the immutable intrinsics + num_slots once with latest_seq=ready=shutdown=0; `set_latest_seq`/`set_ready`/`set_shutdown` poke the int fields afterward. Putting intrinsics in the header is why a reader can fully reconstruct the camera model from just the segment.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: Each slot is `_SLOT_META_SIZE + rgb_bytes + depth_bytes + mask_bytes`. The meta block (precedes the payload) is packed with `_SLOT_META_FMT="<qd16d3d3d"` = seq(q), stamp(d), c2w flattened 16 doubles (row-major, C-order), finger_l 3 doubles, finger_r 3 doubles; `_SLOT_META_SIZE=192` bytes. The payload region holds, contiguously, rgb=`H*W*3` uint8 bytes, then depth=`H*W*4` float32 bytes, then mask=`H*W*1` uint8 bytes. `compute_layout(h,w,num_slots)` computes these sizes purely arithmetically and `total_size = _HDR_SIZE + num_slots*slot_size`. `_slot_payload_views` returns zero-copy numpy views (`np.ndarray(..., buffer=buf, offset=...)`) over each region so writes/reads alias the shared buffer directly. Carrying c2w + fingertips in the small meta block (not the image payload) keeps the pose/marker data cheap to read separately.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `write_frame` is a single-writer lock-free seqlock: (1) compute slot_idx = seq % num_slots; (2) pack the slot meta (which tags `slot.seq` first inside the meta block at the slot base), copying c2w/finger arrays as contiguous float64; (3) copy rgb/depth/mask into the slot's numpy views with `view[:] = frame.field`; (4) ONLY THEN publish by writing `header.latest_seq = seq` (the release barrier — done last). Ordering (tag slot.seq -> fill payload -> publish latest_seq) is what lets the reader detect a torn read. Non-blocking; assumes exactly one writer.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `read_latest` is a lock-free consumer read with `_READ_RETRIES=5` attempts. Each attempt: read `header.latest_seq`; if <=0 return None (nothing published). Compute slot_idx = latest % num_slots, read the slot's leading seq `s1`; if s1 != latest the slot is mid-overwrite so `continue`. Otherwise unpack meta and `copy()` rgb/depth/mask out of the views (so the returned Frame OWNS its arrays and survives the next write), then re-read the slot seq `s2`; if s2 != latest the writer lapped the ring during the copy, so `continue`. The double-check (s1==latest before, s2==latest after) is the seqlock validity test. After 5 torn reads it returns None; callers tolerate None. c2w is reshaped from the flat 16 doubles back to (4,4) float64, fingertips to (3,).

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `ShmProducer` creates and solely owns the POSIX segment sized to `layout.total_size`. Its __init__ calls `_unlink_stale(name)` BEFORE create — opening and unlinking any leaked `/dev/shm/<name>` from a SIGKILLed prior producer (the real crash-recovery path), then creates fresh, packs the header, and sets ready=True (latest_seq stays 0 until the first write). An `atexit` hook handles the normal-exit unlink. `mark_shutdown()` sets the header shutdown flag without clearing slots or unlinking; `close(unlink=True)` detaches and unlinks (owner reclaims the name). Stdlib+numpy+frame.py only (no torch/rospy) so this is importable from the minimal py3.8 ROS env.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `ShmConsumer` attaches read-only (create=False) and NEVER unlinks. It calls `resource_tracker.unregister(self._shm._name, "shared_memory")` so the reader's atexit can never reclaim a segment it didn't create (works around CPython bug #38119 where the resource tracker over-eagerly unlinks). On attach it validates magic+version via `read_header` and caches `intrinsics` + recomputes `layout`. A `threading.Lock` (`_io_lock`) serializes `read_latest` vs `close` so an in-flight read is safe against a concurrent close. `is_shutdown()` re-reads the header shutdown flag; both return safe defaults (None / False) when closed.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `ShmRing` is the pipeline-facing reader: it wraps a `ShmConsumer` and exposes `intrinsics()` (the cached header intrinsics), `peek_latest()` -> Optional[Frame] (delegates to consumer.read_latest, the lock-free seqlock peek), `is_shutdown()`, and `close()`. It is explicitly NOT a FrameSource — the whole rest of the pipeline only ever READS the ring through this, while a FrameSource adapter fills it. This is the single ingest seam that makes live and replay identical downstream.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `FrameSource` is a Protocol with `intrinsics()`, `attach(shm_name)`, `next_frame()`, `close()`. `open_source(kind, data_dir, shm_name=DEFAULT_SHM_NAME, replay_mode="paced", attach=True, **opts)` is the factory: kind=='replay' -> ReplaySource(data_dir, mode=replay_mode) (data_dir required else ValueError), kind=='live_bridge' -> LiveBridgeSource (the recommended live producer), kind=='ros1' -> Ros1Source, kind=='ros2' -> NotImplementedError (Noetic/ROS1 only), else ValueError. If attach=True it immediately calls `src.attach(shm_name)` which spins up the producer (and, for live, spawns the publisher subprocess). The factory is the one source-agnostic entry point the pipeline uses.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.topic: ReplaySource: dataset -> SHM, intrinsics + frame ordering
SHARED.idea: `ReplaySource(data_dir, mode="paced", replay_fps=15.0, transforms_name="transforms.json", num_slots=DEFAULT_NUM_SLOTS, loop=False)` drives a recorded dynamic dataset through the SHM so it 'feels live'. It picks `<data_dir>/dynamic_scene` if that dir exists else data_dir, loads transforms.json, and builds Intrinsics from meta keys `w,h,fl_x,fl_y,cx,cy`. Frames are sorted by the LAST integer found in each `file_path` (regex `\d+`, takes nums[-1]) so numeric capture order is preserved regardless of zero-padding. `__len__` is the frame count. attach() creates the ShmProducer; in paced mode it writes frame 0 immediately (so a reader can peek right away) then starts the daemon pacing thread.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.topic: ReplaySource: per-frame disk decode into a Frame
SHARED.idea: `_load(i)` reads the unit off disk: rgb via cv2.imread COLOR (stays BGR uint8); depth path = explicit `depth_file_path` else derived by replacing 'rgb'->'depth' and '.png'->'.tiff' in the rgb path, read UNCHANGED and converted to metres as `d.astype(float32)*1e-3` (uint16-mm -> float32-m; zeros (H,W) if missing); mask via `mask_path` read GRAYSCALE and binarized `(m>0).astype(uint8)`, or all-ones if no mask path/file. c2w = `transform_matrix` as float64 (the OpenGL c2w, used as-is, no conversion here). It increments `self._seq` (so seq starts at 1) and returns a Frame with contiguous arrays. The 1e-3 factor is the load-bearing depth-unit conversion that satisfies the float32-metres Frame contract.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.topic: ReplaySource paced vs fast modes + stamp synthesis
SHARED.idea: Two modes. paced (DEFAULT): a daemon thread `_paced_loop` writes EVERY frame on its capture-stamp schedule; the consumer's peek_latest naturally drops/trails like live (honest real-time proxy). The pacing timeline `_rel_t` is the per-frame `stamp_wall` minus stamp[0] when all stamps are present and len>1, ELSE synthesized as `i/replay_fps` (default replay_fps=15.0); env `DGS_REPLAY_UNIFORM_FPS=1` forces the uniform-fps cadence even when real stamps exist (to strip capture jitter). The loop sleeps `target - now` (target = pass-start-wall + rel_t[idx]-t0) via `_stop.wait(dt)`; if `loop=True` it wraps idx->0 and republishes (object snaps back to its frame-0/D0 pose) restarting the wall clock each pass, else it calls `mark_shutdown()` at end-of-dataset. fast mode: NO thread; the harness calls `next_frame()` each step (lock-step, frame-exact, deterministic — the pose A/B path); next_frame writes one frame and returns it, returning None + mark_shutdown at end. In paced mode next_frame() is a no-op returning None.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.topic: LiveBridgeSource: spawn proven publisher writing the new layout directly (sim live path)
SHARED.idea: `LiveBridgeSource` is the recommended live producer for the sim: its attach() imports `_spawn_publisher` from dynamic_gs.utils.live_shm_reader and spawns the proven py3.8 ROS publisher with `new_layout=True`, telling it to write THIS frame.py SHM segment (the same `shm_name` ShmRing reads) DIRECTLY — no forwarder thread, no intermediate LiveFrame/SHM-A->SHM-B copy. Spawn kwargs default `keyframe_translation_m=0.02`, `keyframe_rotation_deg=20.0`, `wipe_live_root=True`, `max_hz=0.0` (0 == full rate, >0 throttles). It then performs a JSON line handshake on the publisher's stdout: loops until `ready_timeout_s=30.0`, parses one-line JSON events, raises on `init_error`, and on `event=="ready"` builds Intrinsics from `width,height,fx,fy,cx,cy` in the message. next_frame() returns None (publisher writes SHM directly; pipeline reads via ShmRing). The reader thus gets live intrinsics from the SHM header / handshake, never hardcoded. (A non-sim DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA / Jetson-ZED path also exists; out of scope here.)

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: close() uses `_proc.terminate()` (SIGTERM to proc.pid) then `kill()` after a 5.0s wait, and deliberately does NOT use killpg: `_spawn_publisher` does not start a new session so the publisher shares the parent's process group, and the spawn cmd is `bash -c "... exec python ..."` so exec replaced bash — SIGTERM hits the python publisher directly, whose own handler drops the rospy node and unlinks the SHM. killpg here would kill the parent too.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.idea: `Ros1Source` spawns the ROS1 publisher (`python -m dynamic_gs2.ros_publisher --shm-name <name>`) inside the py3.8 `dynamic_gs_ros` conda env via `bash -lc "source conda.sh && conda activate <env> && source /opt/ros/noetic/setup.bash && exec python -m ..."`, with `preexec_fn=os.setsid` (own session). `_ros_publisher_env` strips `_STRIP_ENV_VARS=("LD_LIBRARY_PATH","CPATH","CUDA_HOME","PYTHONPATH")` and sets `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` so the parent dynamic_gs env doesn't shadow the ROS env. It does NOT import rospy (stays env-portable); intrinsics come from the SHM header (read via ShmRing), and next_frame() returns None. close() uses killpg SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 5.0s (it owns its session, unlike LiveBridgeSource).

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.topic: camera_from_frame: build a nerfstudio Cameras from a Frame
SHARED.idea: `camera_from_frame(frame, intr, device, cam_idx=0)` builds ONE nerfstudio `Cameras` for rendering/training. It takes the top-3x4 of the OpenGL c2w (`frame.c2w_4x4[:3,:4]`), casts to contiguous float32, and unsqueezes to a (1,3,4) batch as `camera_to_worlds`; sets fx/fy/cx/cy from Intrinsics, width/height as ints, `camera_type=CameraType.PERSPECTIVE`, moves to device, and tags `cam.metadata={"cam_idx":cam_idx}`. NOTE (verified against the code body): this function does NOT apply any diag(1,-1,-1,1) flip — it passes the OpenGL c2w straight into the Cameras object. The OpenGL->camera-space handedness is consumed downstream where the projection math negates z/y (e.g. scene_model world->camera uses z=-mc[:,2], v uses -mc[:,1]); the Frame/SHM layer stores and forwards the OpenGL c2w verbatim.

SHARED.title: Frame data unit & SHM transport
SHARED.topic: Coordinate convention carried, not converted, at this layer
SHARED.idea: The data-path layer treats geometry as: metric scene units, depth float32 metres, and `c2w_4x4` as OpenGL camera->world float64 stored row-major flattened (16 doubles) in slot meta and round-tripped via reshape(4,4). No recentering/rescaling/orientation change happens in frame.py/shm_channel.py/adapters_source.py; the c2w from transforms.json (replay) or the publisher (live) is forwarded unchanged. The OpenGL->OpenCV `diag(1,-1,-1,1)` conversion the project relies on is applied later in the rendering/projection code (nerfstudio Splatfacto / scene_model), not in the SHM transport. So the SHM unit is convention-faithful but convention-neutral.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: ROS topic names (sim ZED-X camera + robot)
SHARED.idea: All sim source topics are string constants. RGB image = `/dynaarm_arm/dynaarm_arm/camera1/image_raw` (subscribed as its JPEG `/compressed` sub-topic, sensor_msgs/CompressedImage); depth = `/dynaarm_arm/dynaarm_arm/camera1/depth/image_raw` (sensor_msgs/Image, raw); camera intrinsics = `/dynaarm_arm/dynaarm_arm/camera1/camera_info` (sensor_msgs/CameraInfo); robot joints = `/dynaarm_arm/joint_states_full` (sensor_msgs/JointState); and the ground-truth Gazebo camera world pose = `/dynaarm_arm/dynaarm_arm/camera1/gazebo_pose` (geometry_msgs/PoseStamped). These are the inputs that become a Frame.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: The publisher runs in a minimal ROS python-3.8 env (no torch/nerfstudio) and is launched as a standalone script, so it importlib-loads `dynamic_gs2/ros_mask.py` by absolute PATH (parents[2]/dynamic_gs2/ros_mask.py) and pulls its converters + RobotMaskGenerator + topic constants from it; likewise it path-loads `zed_depth_noise.py` and `depth_filter.py` from its own dir. ros_mask.py is thus the single source of truth for topics, intrinsics dataclass, and mask render logic shared between the live publisher and dynamic_gs2.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Intrinsics resolution from CameraInfo (with Gazebo lazy-publish workaround)
SHARED.idea: Intrinsics come from CameraInfo: fx=K[0], fy=K[4], cx=K[2], cy=K[5], width/height from the message, packed into a CameraIntrinsics dataclass. Because Gazebo's camera plugin only publishes camera_info while something subscribes to the image stream, `_wait_for_camera_info_primed` holds a primer subscriber on `IMAGE_TOPIC+'/compressed'` for the whole wait and polls `wait_for_message(camera_info)` in <=2 s slices up to a 20 s deadline. On success it also writes a sticky cache to `~/.cache/dgs_camera_intrinsics.json`. On timeout it falls back, in order, to static_scene/transforms.json, dynamic_scene/transforms.json, the cache, then any transforms.json under the datasets root.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Depth decode to float32 metres (raw, NOT compressed)
SHARED.idea: Depth is subscribed RAW (not via compressedDepth transport) and decoded by `_decode_raw_depth`: encoding '32FC1' is read straight as float32 metres via np.frombuffer reshaped to HxW; '16UC1' is read as uint16 then multiplied by 1e-3 to metres. Raw is used deliberately because image_transport's compressedDepth uses inverse-depth log encoding for 32FC1 sources, which a naive PNG-as-uint16-mm decoder misreads ~32x too large and destroys downstream RANSAC pose fits. Gazebo's openni_kinect plugin emits 32FC1 metres.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: RGB arrives JPEG-compressed (CompressedImage on the /compressed transport, ~50 KB vs 1.9 MB raw). `_decode_compressed_rgb` decodes to BGR uint8 HxWx3 using libjpeg-turbo (PyTurboJPEG, pixel_format=TJPF_BGR) if importable, else falls back to cv2.imdecode(IMREAD_COLOR). The TurboJPEG instance is probed once and cached on the class (None=unprobed, False=unavailable).

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Sim ZED-X depth noise injection (ON by default in sim)
SHARED.idea: After depth decode, sim-clean depth is corrupted to ZED-X realism by `apply_zed_depth_noise` (gated by `_ZED_NOISE.enabled()`, ON unless DGS_SIM_ZED_NOISE=0). Per-pixel axial Gaussian noise with std sigma_z(z)=SIGMA0 + K*z^2, SIGMA0=0.00147 m (1.47 mm flat term), K=0.000500 m/m^2 (fit to real ZED scene_dataset p90 upper bound); added only to valid (>0) pixels via z + N(0,1)*sigma. Then a range gate nulls depth outside [0.05, 3.0] m (_Z_MIN/_Z_MAX, matching the fusion DEPTH_MIN/MAX), and a random hole rate of 0.01 (_HOLE_RATE, 1% of still-valid pixels) is set to 0. This closes the sim-to-real gap (Gazebo's z-buffer depth is essentially noise-free). The RNG is owned per-publisher (np.random.default_rng()).

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Camera world pose from Gazebo ground-truth pose topic (sim path)
SHARED.idea: In sim (not real-HW), camera c2w is interpolated by `_interpolate_c2w` from the `gazebo_pose` PoseStamped buffer keyed by image stamp: exact stamp within TIME_EPS_SEC=1e-6 uses that matrix; otherwise it SLERPs the bracketing quaternions (quaternion_from_matrix -> quaternion_slerp at alpha=(t-t_prev)/(t_next-t_prev)) and linearly interpolates translation. The interpolated pose is the gazebo camera body frame, so it is right-multiplied by a static link offset `_static_link_offset(camera_pose_link -> camera_link_optical)` (from zero-config URDF FK) to reach the optical frame, then converted optical->OpenGL/nerfstudio via `rotate_camera_frame_only`. So the sim does NOT use FK for the pose itself; it uses the Gazebo ground-truth pose plus one static FK offset. (NOTE: the SLERP/interp lives in _interpolate_c2w, not _on_gazebo_pose, which only buffers samples.)

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: `rotate_camera_frame_only` converts a ROS optical c2w (+X right, +Y down, +Z forward) to nerfstudio/OpenGL (+X right, +Y up, +Z back) by right-multiplying only the 3x3 rotation by ROS_OPTICAL_TO_NERFSTUDIO=diag(1,-1,-1); translation is preserved. This is applied to every camera pose written to SHM and to saved transforms.json.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Joint-state / pose buffering and time sync
SHARED.idea: `_on_joint_state` and `_on_gazebo_pose` keep time-sorted buffers (bisect_left insert) of joint dicts and 4x4 pose matrices respectively, throttled to drop samples within _POSE_JOINT_MIN_DT_SEC=0.02 s of the last (50 Hz storage is enough to bracket ~33 ms image stamps). In sim, stamps are the message header stamps (msg.header.stamp.to_sec()). pose_msg_to_matrix builds the 4x4 from the PoseStamped quaternion (tf quaternion_matrix) + position. JointState position arrays are zipped name->value into a dict.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: RGB (/compressed) and depth (raw) Subscribers are paired by a message_filters ApproximateTimeSynchronizer with queue_size=SYNC_QUEUE_SIZE (20) and slop=SYNC_SLOP_SEC=0.02 s. The publisher overrides ros_mask.py's default 0.1 s slop down to 0.02 s because Gazebo co-stamps RGB and depth within microseconds (same sim step), and a large slop forces the synchronizer's pivot-wait to cost ~slop per match, capping throughput. Subscribers use tcp_nodelay=True with buff_size 2 MB (rgb) / 16 MB (depth) and queue_size 30.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: The rospy sync callback `_on_synced` is minimal: it just enqueues (image_msg, depth_msg, t) into a bounded `_frame_queue` (maxsize=4) with drop-oldest semantics (on full, pop one then push the newest) so the receive thread always drains the socket and keeps the freshest frame. A `_worker_loop` thread drains the queue and runs `_process_synced_pair` (pose interp + rgb/depth decode + noise + mask collect + SHM write). A separate `_mask_thread_loop` owns the pyrender GL context and renders one mask per request. The worker submits a mask request (stamp + monotone _mask_req_seq) FIRST, then decodes rgb/depth concurrently, then waits (_mask_done_event, timeout 1.0 s) — overlapping mask render with decode so frame time is max(mask, decode) not their sum. DGS_PUB_MASK_THREAD=0 forces inline rendering on the worker.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Stale-mask seqlock between worker and mask thread
SHARED.idea: Each mask request is tagged with a monotone `_mask_req_seq`; the mask thread snapshots that id, renders, stores `_mask_result` and tags `_mask_result_seq` BEFORE setting `_mask_done_event`. The worker, after waiting, rejects the result if `_mask_result_seq != req_seq` and drops the frame. This prevents a slow render that overran a previous frame's wait from being consumed for the wrong (newer) frame, which would otherwise desync rgb/depth vs mask by one frame permanently.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: RobotMaskGenerator: URDF load + mesh-path resolution + scene build
SHARED.idea: RobotMaskGenerator loads the arm+gripper URDF (URDF_PATH constant) via urdfpy. `_make_temp_resolved_urdf` rewrites every `package://pkg/rest` mesh reference: it first tries `STL_DIR/<basename>.stl` (a flat local STL dir), else maps the package via PACKAGE_MAP to its catkin source path, writing a temp resolved URDF. `_build_scene` walks every link's visuals, converts each geometry to a trimesh (mesh file via cached `_load_trimesh`, or box/cylinder/sphere primitives via trimesh.creation), and adds each as a pyrender mesh node tagged (link_name, visual, node). Meshes are cached by (path|scale) key. The render material is opaque red (baseColorFactor (0.9,0.2,0.2,1.0)) — color is irrelevant since only the depth buffer is used.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: `_ensure_renderer` builds a pyrender.OffscreenRenderer at a fraction of full resolution: scale from DGS_MASK_RENDER_SCALE (default 0.25), clamped to [0.1, 1.0], giving render_w=round(W*scale), render_h=round(H*scale). The IntrinsicsCamera fx/fy/cx/cy are scaled by the achieved per-axis ratios sx=render_w/W, sy=render_h/H, with znear=0.001, zfar=100.0. The robot keep-mask is a coarse silhouette, so rendering small and NEAREST-upscaling the binary result to full res is visually identical for the gripper cut-out while cutting fill cost. DGS_MASK_RENDER_SCALE=1.0 restores full res. Scene bg_color is opaque black (0,0,0,1).

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Mask camera pose for render (sim body-frame remaps)
SHARED.idea: The mask is rendered from the camera link FK, not the Gazebo pose topic. `_camera_pose_from_link_fk` looks up the FK of the mask camera frame link (camera_pose_link); if absent it composes the default link pose with `_static_link_offset`. `_build_render_camera_pose` (sim path, optical=False) maps that body-style frame — whose +X is the viewing direction and -Z is up — onto pyrender's convention by right-multiplying optical_to_opengl (diag(1,-1,-1)) then rot_y_(-90) then rot_z_(+90). The camera_pose_link is a body frame, NOT optical, hence the two extra 90-deg remaps before the optical->OpenGL flip.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Joint sampling for FK (interpolation at image stamp)
SHARED.idea: `_sample_joint_positions_raw` bisects the joint-time buffer at the image stamp: exact match within TIME_EPS_SEC=1e-6 returns that sample (filtered to actuated joints); otherwise it linearly interpolates each actuated joint between the bracketing samples at alpha=(t-t_prev)/(t_next-t_prev). Out-of-buffer queries return the boundary (oldest/newest) sample and log a throttled (2 s) warning that the camera pose may be frozen. The resulting joint dict feeds urdfpy `robot.link_fk(cfg=joints, use_names=True)` to pose every link for the render. (Note: _sample_joint_positions wraps _raw and, only on the real-HW path, adds the +45 deg WRIST_2 offset.)

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Silhouette extraction from depth buffer + flip + upscale
SHARED.idea: `_render_robot_exclusion_mask` poses each robot mesh node by its link FK (`_update_robot_poses`: node pose = base_to_link @ link_to_visual), sets the camera node pose, and renders. Only the depth buffer is used: robot_keep = (depth==0)*255, i.e. 255 (keep scene) where nothing was drawn, 0 where the robot occupies pixels. The sim render is upside-down (GL origin), so it is cv2.flip(_, 0) vertically (the real-HW optical render skips the flip). If the rendered size differs from full intrinsics resolution it is cv2.resize'd up to (W,H) with INTER_NEAREST to keep the binary edges crisp.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: After upscaling, the robot (black) region is grown by MASK_ROBOT_GROW_PX (env DGS_MASK_ROBOT_GROW_PX; default 0 in sim, 16 on real-HW) to cover silhouette under-coverage. It is an OUTER-ONLY grow: a full erode(keep) with an elliptical kernel of size (2*grow+1) would also fill the gripper's concave jaw gap and hide a grasped object, so the code computes pixels the erode turned from keep->robot (`ate`), flood-fills the keep mask from every image-border keep pixel to find the outer background, and RESTORES eaten pixels that are NOT border-reachable (enclosed interior keep, e.g. the jaw gap). Net: outer silhouette grows, concavities stay open. In sim default (grow=0) this whole block is skipped.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Live keep-mask convention vs disk-refine path
SHARED.idea: The LIVE publisher path uses the raw robot-exclusion keep mask (255=keep scene, 0=robot) directly and does NOT call `_refine_keep_mask`. `_refine_keep_mask` (used only by the on-disk `save_mask` recorder path) additionally erodes the keep region by MASK_KEEP_ERODE_RADIUS_PX=4 (elliptical kernel size 2*4+1=9) and drops keep connected-components smaller than MASK_MIN_KEEP_COMPONENT_AREA_PX=64 px via connectedComponentsWithStats (8-connectivity). Background color masking (BACKGROUND_COLOR_THRESHOLD=10.0 against Gazebo world colors) exists in code but `save_mask` disables it — only the robot is excluded.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Finger-pad tip world points stashed per frame
SHARED.idea: During the same FK pass, `_render_robot_exclusion_mask` computes each gripper inner-finger-pad's distal tip world point for the viewer overlay: tip = link_origin + R_world @ FINGER_PAD_TIP_LOCAL where FINGER_PAD_TIP_LOCAL=[0,0,0.0375/2] (half the 0.0375 m pad length along local +Z) for links left/right_inner_finger_pad (FINGER_PAD_LINKS). These are stored on `last_finger_world` and read back by the publisher (`_finger_world_points`, zeros if unavailable) to write into the SHM frame alongside the mask, so they are perfectly synced with the rendered pose at zero extra FK cost.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: Default SHM layout: name DEFAULT_SHM_NAME='/dgs_live_shm', NUM_SLOTS=4, HEADER_BYTES=4096. Header (_HDR_FMT) stores magic b'DGS\0', version, H, W, num_slots, fx/fy/cx/cy (f64), latest_seq (u64), slot_bytes, and per-slot field offsets. Each slot holds pose(16 f64), seq(u64), stamp(f64), rgb(H*W*3 u8), depth(H*W f32), mask(H*W u8), ordered largest-aligned-first and padded to 64 B. The writer fills slot[seq % 4] via prebuilt zero-copy numpy views (np.frombuffer into shm.buf), then bumps header.latest_seq atomically via struct.pack_into. A reader samples latest_seq, reads that slot, re-checks slot.seq; 4 slots give the reader >100 ms before reuse.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: With --new-layout (passed by LiveBridgeSource), the publisher path-loads `dynamic_gs2/frame.py` and writes its layout DIRECTLY so the tracker reads the segment with no bridge/forwarder/extra copy. It builds frame.py Intrinsics + Layout (compute_layout(H,W), DEFAULT_NUM_SLOTS=4, magic b'DGS1'), pack_header + set_ready(True), then per frame calls `frame.write_frame(buf, layout, Frame(...))` which seqlock-writes into slot (seq % num_slots). Crucially the Frame.mask_keep contract is uint8 {0,1} (1=keep), while the render returns {0,255}, so the publisher passes `mask_keep != 0` (cheap bool that slice-assign casts), and passes finger_l/finger_r world points. On shutdown it calls set_shutdown(True).

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: On startup the publisher unlinks any pre-existing SHM region of the same name (FileNotFoundError ignored) before creating a fresh one sized to the layout's total bytes, guarding against a previous crash leaving a stale segment. It signals readiness by writing ready=1 in the header (set_ready in new layout). On shutdown it deliberately does NOT clear slot views or unlink the segment (a reader may still be reading; rospy callbacks can fire during teardown) — it only sets header.shutdown=1 as a polite signal and relies on process exit to release memory; it also unregisters all four subscribers and calls rospy.signal_shutdown to drop the node registration so the next publisher run doesn't fight a zombie /camera_info subscriber.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: Each processed pair becomes a `_StoredFrame(seq, stamp_sec, rgb_bgr u8 HxWx3, depth_m f32 HxW, mask_keep u8 (255=keep), c2w_4x4 f64)` under `_state_lock`, stored as `_latest` and given a monotonically incremented `_frame_seq`. The image-msg header stamp is the canonical stamp_sec. On the first frame produced, `_first_frame_event` is set so the reader's `wait_first_frame` command unblocks. `_latest` also backs the reader's capture_anchor / save_anchor_* commands.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: `_spawn_depth_republisher` always launches `rosrun image_transport republish raw in:=<DEPTH_TOPIC> compressedDepth out:=<DEPTH_TOPIC>` in a new session, because Gazebo's openni_kinect advertises raw depth but not the compressedDepth transport, and it never checks for an existing republisher (rosmaster often holds stale registrations after unclean kills that would short-circuit the spawn and leave the depth subscriber waiting forever). It waits up to 5 s for the /compressedDepth topic to appear and logs loudly if not. (Note: _spawn_depth_republisher is defined but NOT called anywhere in this file — the publisher itself subscribes RAW depth, so the republisher is dead code on the current sim path.)

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: During disk recording the publisher accepts keyframes via `_KeyframeFilter` (ORB-SLAM-style greedy motion dedup). In sim (motion mode, interval_s=0) a frame's (3x4) c2w is accepted only if, vs EVERY kept frame, it is past at least ONE threshold (translation > keyframe_translation_m default 0.02 m, OR rotation angle > keyframe_rotation_deg default 20 deg) — i.e. it is rejected only if some kept frame is within BOTH thresholds (near = (dt<=t) & (dr<=r); reject if near.any()). Rotation distance is dr=arccos(clip(0.5*(trace(R_i^T R_k)-1),-1,1)). (The time-interval mode interval_s>0 is the real-HW fixed-camera path.) Right for an operator sweeping the camera by hand so the static dataset isn't flooded with redundant near-duplicate views.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Disk recording: paths, depth filter, transforms.json
SHARED.idea: On start_recording the publisher creates static_scene/{rgb,depth,masks} and writes accepted keyframes via `_write_frame_to_disk`: RGB as BGR PNG (arm_NNNNN.png), depth as uint16-mm TIFF (clip(depth_m*1000,0,65535)), mask as PNG (255=keep). If DGS_DEPTH_FILTER!=0, raw depth is saved to depth_raw/ and the median+bilateral-filtered depth is written to depth/ — median kernel 5 (cv2 float32 supports 3/5 only), bilateral diameter 5, sigma_color 0.01 m (1 cm), sigma_space 5.0, weight-normalized by a validity mask so zeros never bleed into valid pixels. transforms.json is rebuilt atomically (tmp + os.replace) per frame with intrinsics + a frames list (file_path, depth_file_path, mask_path, transform_matrix = OpenGL c2w). In-flight writes are tracked so stop_recording can quiesce them.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: TSDF-seed PLY build from recorded keyframes
SHARED.idea: `build_static_init_pointcloud` back-projects recorded keyframes into a world-frame point cloud written as depth_camera_init_points.ply (INIT_CLOUD_NAME), capped at MAX_INIT_CLOUD_POINTS=600000 points distributed evenly across frames by valid-pixel count (`distribute_point_budget_evenly`). For sampled valid pixels (keep-mask & depth>0), it back-projects with x=(u-cx)*z/fx, y=-(v-cy)*z/fy, xyz_cam=[x,y,-z] (OpenGL camera convention), homogenizes, and transforms by the frame's OpenGL c2w to world; colors are BGR->RGB. This is the geometry seed the static Gaussian fit locks means onto.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: Two throttle mechanisms reduce GPU/CPU contention. (1) Output-rate cap: DGS_PUB_MAX_HZ (default 0=off) drops frames in `_on_synced` before enqueue if within 1/max_hz of the last kept frame, skipping the whole heavy worker path; set only for the static-sweep publisher. (2) RGB-only mode: once the static pipeline touches `<live_root>/.rgb_only` (polled ~2x/s), the worker latches into rgb-only — it decodes RGB for the viser UI feed but writes zeros for depth and a full-keep (255) mask, skipping the mask GL render and depth decode entirely, and caps output to ~10 Hz (_rgb_only_min_dt=1/10). This frees the GPU for the concurrent TSDF-seed build + Splatfacto static train. The sentinel lives in live_root (wiped at each spawn) so the separate dynamic publisher never inherits it.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.idea: Control flows over line-delimited JSON: stdin commands (wait_first_frame, capture_anchor, start_recording, stop_recording, num_recorded, save_anchor_for_sam3, save_anchor_depth_intrinsics, build_init_pcd, pause/unpause_gazebo, shutdown) -> one JSON reply per line. To stop rospy/urdfpy/pyrender info logs from corrupting that stream, fd 1 is dup'd to a private IPC writer (_IPC_OUT) and the real stdout (fd 1) is redirected onto stderr (dup2(2,1)) at import time, so all third-party prints land in the parent's stderr log instead of the JSON channel. The first 'ready' reply carries shm_name + intrinsics + slot/header sizes (0 in new-layout, where frame.py owns sizing).

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: numpy alias shim for urdfpy under numpy>=1.24
SHARED.idea: Because the env's urdfpy 0.0.22 still calls removed numpy aliases (np.float etc.), the publisher restores np.float/int/bool/object/str/long/complex/unicode at import time. Without this the lazy RobotMaskGenerator construction throws AttributeError on every synced frame and no SHM slot is ever published. Load-bearing for the mask path to function at all.

SHARED.title: Sim camera publisher & robot self-masking
SHARED.topic: Real-HW path exists (out of sim scope)
SHARED.idea: A real-hardware branch exists gated by DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA (REAL_HW_CAMERA): when set, the camera is treated as bolted to the ELBOW link (REAL_HW_CAMERA_PARENT_LINK='dynaarm_ELBOW') with a fixed measured optical offset (REAL_HW_CAMERA_XYZ, REAL_HW_CAMERA_ROT, +45 deg WRIST_2 correction), poses derived from FK instead of the Gazebo pose topic, frames receipt-re-stamped with rospy.Time.now() for cross-machine clock-skew robustness, and a launch-time clock-skew check. This is documented here only as existing — the sim pipeline takes the else-branches throughout.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: config.py is the SINGLE place os.environ is read; everything else receives a frozen, immutable sub-config (no lock needed across the 3 threads). All config dataclasses are `@dataclass(frozen=True)`. Four typed env-readers do all parsing with try/except fallback to the default: `_envs(name,default)->str` (os.environ.get), `_envf->float` (float() or KeyError/ValueError fallback), `_envi->int`, and `_envb(name,default)->bool` where a missing var returns default and ANY value other than the literal string "0" is True (so DGS_X=anything-but-0 enables). The shipped DEFAULT of every field IS the value in the dataclass body; load_runtime_config() overlays DGS_* env on top. Module constants: STATIC_NUM_STEPS=500, DEFAULT_DYNAMIC_RECORDED_STEPS=5000, DEFAULT_DYNAMIC_LIVE_STEPS=1_000_000.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: RuntimeConfig is the root frozen tree. Top-level scalar fields with defaults: source="sim" ("sim"|"real"; sim->depth-noise on, real->off), resolution=(1920,1200), background_color=(0.86,0.92,1.0) (Gazebo sky, hard-validated, Invariant #6 — _validate raises if changed), shm_name="dgs_frame_v1". All sub-configs are attached via field(default_factory=...): tracker, pose_filter, change_mask, feedforward, budget, depth, fusion, sim_noise, segmentation, viser, static_train, debug. World/metric convention: poses are metric and NOT recentered/rescaled — the live-sim path does NOT use a nerfstudio dataparser at all; camera_from_frame builds a single nerfstudio Cameras directly from the Frame's OpenGL camera-to-world 4x4 plus raw intrinsics (fx,fy,cx,cy,width,height, CameraType.PERSPECTIVE), so orientation/center/scale are identity by construction.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: Camera poses are OpenGL camera-to-world (c2w). When projecting world points into the image (means_in_bbox_idx), the code computes camera-space coords as mc=(means - t)@R where R,t are the c2w rotation/translation — i.e. world->camera is the c2w transpose applied on the right. Because it is OpenGL (camera looks down -Z, +Y up), depth is z=-mc[:,2] and the pixel mapping flips the v axis: u=fx*(mc[:,0]/z)+cx, v=fy*(-mc[:,1]/z)+cy, with a front-of-camera test z>1e-6. This is the internal OpenGL->OpenCV-pixel conversion (the explicit diag(1,-1,-1,1) flip lives in the rasterizer path; here it is folded into the -z / -y signs).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: Depth unit convention (uint16 mm -> float32 m)
SHARED.idea: Depth on disk is uint16 millimetres (TIFF, read with cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED); the replay loader converts to float32 metres by multiplying by 1e-3 (depth_m = d.astype(float32)*1e-3). RGB on disk is BGR uint8 (cv2.IMREAD_COLOR). Masks are read grayscale and binarized as (m>0).astype(uint8), defaulting to all-ones when no mask path is present. The SHM boundary therefore carries depth already in metres; there is no separate depth_unit_scale_factor read in the dynamic_gs2 live-sim path (the 1e-3 is applied inline at load).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: XFeat/LighterGlue tracker config: top_k=1024 (DGS_XFEAT_TOP_K), ransac_iterations=68 (DGS_XFEAT_RANSAC_ITERS; higher=stabler inlier consensus), ransac_inlier_threshold=0.004 m (DGS_XFEAT_RANSAC_INLIER_M; lower=stricter), lighterglue_depth_confidence=-1.0, crop_to_object_bbox=True, crop_padding_px=150, object_mask_filter=True, rotation_gate_deg=22.5, scale_gate_ratio=1.3, scale_select=False (DGS_XFEAT_SCALE_SELECT), static_hold_window=15 (DGS_HOLD_WINDOW), static_hold_trans_mm=25.0 (DGS_HOLD_TRANS_MM), static_hold_rot_deg=10.0 (DGS_HOLD_ROT_DEG), min_track_points=12. The static_hold_* trio is a stillness gate: if motion over the last 15 ticks stays under 25mm/10deg the object is considered static (kills steady-state shake).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: Constant-acceleration pose Kalman filter, DEFAULT OFF (enabled=False, DGS_KF_ENABLED=1 to turn on) so the deterministic A/B matches the old pipeline. fixed_fps=9.0 feeds event-time dt (never wall-clock time.time()) making it rate-invariant. Process noise: accel_sigma=0.005 (DGS_KF_ACCEL_SIGMA), alpha_sigma=0.025 (DGS_KF_ALPHA_SIGMA). Measurement noise: meas_trans_mm=20.0 (DGS_KF_MEAS_TRANS_MM), meas_rot_deg=10.0 (DGS_KF_MEAS_ROT_DEG). Innovation snap-gate: snap_trans_m=0.05 and snap_rot_deg=10.0 — a jump exceeding these is treated as a reacquisition and the filter SNAPS to the measurement rather than smoothing through it.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: Change-detection-network params operate on a DOWNSAMPLED grid: downsample_target_side=150 (DGS_CDN_TARGET_SIDE) sets the longest side, rgb_threshold=0.2 (DGS_CDN_RGB_THRESHOLD) is the 1-SSIM dissimilarity cutoff, blur_sigma=0.75 (DGS_CDN_BLUR_SIGMA) Gaussian pre-blur with blur_kernel_size=5 (DGS_CDN_BLUR_KERNEL_SIZE), ssim_window=5 (DGS_CDN_SSIM_WINDOW; single-scale, small to keep detection tight on the ds grid). Post-processing: block_valid_min_frac=0.0 (keep any pooled block with a valid pixel), min_component_area=40 ds-cells (drop smaller change blobs), morph_close_px=2 (DGS_CDN_CLOSE_PX, fill <=2px interior holes), morph_open_px=1 (DGS_CDN_OPEN_PX, remove single-px speckle), keep_largest_only=False, scene_coverage_threshold=0.5, gripper_erode_px=6 (DGS_CDN_GRIPPER_ERODE_PX; FF-only: enlarge the gripper EXCLUSION by eroding the keep-mask 6 full-res px so the gripper silhouette never leaks into the change region; tracker reads the raw mask). Live depth window: live_depth_min_m=0.05, live_depth_max_m=3.0.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: FeedforwardConfig (AnySplat insert) — cadence, scale & cull defaults
SHARED.idea: FF dispatch fires AnySplat decode every cadence_ticks tracker ticks; DEFAULT in the dataclass is 10 but load_runtime_config OVERRIDES the shipped default to 20 (DGS_FF_CADENCE=20, fires AnySplat less so it doesn't starve the render). icp_refine=True (DGS_FF_ICP; runtime-reloadable), icp_stride=4 (DGS_FF_ICP_STRIDE; pixel stride for both ICP clouds). Insert hygiene: opacity_min=0.05 (AnySplat opacity-logit keep floor), scale_multiplier=1.0, max_scale_m=0.02 (DGS_FF_MAX_SCALE_M; hard per-axis cap, uniform-shrink gross blobs), min_scale_m=0.0 (DGS_FF_MIN_SCALE_M; tiny-splat cull, 0=off), voxel_merge_m=0.001 (DGS_FF_VOXEL_MERGE_M; moment-match merge per voxel, 0=off), density_max_points=80000 (DGS_FF_DENSITY_MAX_PTS; subsample ceiling on the O(N^2) corner-kNN input). Occlusion culls: cull_before_decode=True, cull_in_front_depth_tol_m=0.01 (delete a gaussian only if >10mm in front of the live surface), cull_replaced_enabled=True (DGS_FF_CULL_REPLACED; second cull of the overwritten old slab), cull_replaced_depth_tol_m=0.0 (DGS_FF_CULL_REPLACED_TOL_M; slab thickness behind the surface, 0=OFF). object_mask_scale=1.1, object_mask_dilate_px=0, crop_pad_px=50, insert_id=999.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: After voxel-merge, FF grows the 2 in-plane (surface) axes by grow_inplane_factor=2.0 (DGS_FF_GROW_INPLANE, 1=off) leaving the normal axis, to fill sub-splat surface holes without blur. The grow is CORNERNESS-GATED via a kNN-PCA score so it tapers to no-grow at edges/creases and doesn't leak past silhouettes. Corner detection params: corner_knn_k=80 (DGS_FF_CORNER_KNN_K; neighbours for crease+boundary detection), corner_var_scale=0.10 (DGS_FF_CORNER_VAR_SCALE; surface-variation mapping to corner_score=1 for CREASES), corner_boundary_scale=3.0 (DGS_FF_CORNER_BOUNDARY_SCALE; neighbour-centroid-offset/spacing ratio mapping to 1 for silhouette BOUNDARIES; 3.0 keeps gently curved surfaces from being mistaken for edges), corner_halo_k=50 (DGS_FF_CORNER_HALO_K; one non-iterative hop — flag a point if any of its 50 NN is a detected corner, 0=no halo), corner_merge_threshold=0.13 (DGS_FF_CORNER_MERGE_THR; corner_score>=0.13 -> CORNER passed RAW, not merged/grown so edges keep geometry; flat points <0.13 are downsampled+hole-filled).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: GaussianBudgetConfig defaults — ceiling, purge & static scale-clamp
SHARED.idea: Gaussian budget (no env overrides; frozen at boot): live_gaussian_ceiling=2_000_000 caps total live count. Dynamic periodic FF-purge is OFF: dynamic_purge_every_n_ff=0 (purge every N FF inserts, 0=disabled), dynamic_purge_opacity_below=0.05 (would-drop opacity floor). Static one-shot purge: static_opacity_purge_threshold=0.05. Static scale-clamp (runs every static_scale_clamp_every_n=10 steps): static_scale_clamp_max_m=0.05 is the max axis, and any gaussian exceeding it is reset to static_scale_reset_value_m=0.01. _validate enforces static_scale_reset_value_m < static_scale_clamp_max_m (0.01<0.05) so a reset can't immediately re-trip the clamp boundary.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: DepthConfig defaults — median+bilateral filter & far-clip invariant
SHARED.idea: Depth filter (DGS_DEPTH_FILTER, default on): median_ksize=5 (DGS_DEPTH_MEDIAN_KSIZE; kills stereo flying-pixels), then a bilateral with bilateral_sigma_color_m=0.01 (DGS_DEPTH_BILATERAL_SIGMA_COLOR_M), bilateral_sigma_space=0.0, bilateral_d=0 (OpenCV auto from sigma). Valid depth window: depth_min_m=0.05, depth_max_m=2.0 (DGS_TSDF_DEPTH_MAX_M). scene_depth_max_m=2.0 MUST equal depth_max_m and is set equal by construction in load_runtime_config; _validate raises 'scene_depth_max_m must equal depth_max_m (loss-mask invariant)' if they ever diverge.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: TSDF fusion config for the seed: device="auto" (DGS_FUSION_DEVICE, lowercased), tsdf_voxel_m=0.002 (DGS_TSDF_VOXEL_M; near voxel size), far_voxel_m=0.01 (coarser far voxels), near_radius_m=1.0 (boundary between near/far voxel sizing), tsdf_trunc_m=0.008 (8mm truncation band), defer_tsdf=True (DGS_LIVE_DEFER_TSDF; defer TSDF integration in the live path).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: SimNoiseConfig — sim depth noise model, source-derived enable
SHARED.idea: Synthetic ZED depth-noise applied to SIM depth only. enabled is DERIVED: noise_on = (source=="sim") AND _envb(DGS_SIM_ZED_NOISE, True) — so it auto-enables for sim and DGS_SIM_ZED_NOISE=0 forces it off; on a real source it is forced off and _validate RAISES if sim_noise.enabled is True with source=='real' (would double-noise real depth). Noise model params: sigma0_m=0.00147 (DGS_SIM_ZED_SIGMA0_M; base stddev), k_m=0.000500 (DGS_SIM_ZED_K_M; range-dependent stddev coefficient), hole_rate=0.01 (DGS_SIM_ZED_HOLE_RATE; fraction of pixels dropped to holes), z_min_m=0.05, z_max_m=3.0 (valid range outside which noise/holes aren't applied).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: Segmentation: backend="fastsam" (DGS_SEGMENTATION_BACKEND; default 2D segmenter), prompt_text="" (DGS_SAM3_PROMPT; empty by default), sam3d_no_trim=False (DGS_SAM3D_NO_TRIM; trim the Fast-SAM3D weights by default to save VRAM), sam3d_registration_backend="ndp" (no env override; point-cloud registration method). Near-surface object gating (no env override): near_surface_max_object_slope_deg=70.0 and near_surface_window_frac=0.012.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: ViserConfig: enabled=True, port=8081 (viser-direct server, no env override in load path — NS viewer port 7007 is never used). StaticTrainConfig: num_steps=STATIC_NUM_STEPS=500, early_stop_enabled=True (DGS_STATIC_EARLY_STOP), early_stop_loss=0.02 (DGS_STATIC_EARLY_STOP_LOSS; stop when loss below this), early_stop_patience=8 (DGS_STATIC_EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE; ticks under threshold before stopping), early_stop_min_steps=100 (DGS_STATIC_EARLY_STOP_MIN_STEPS; never stop before this). DebugConfig (all default False): enabled (DGS_DEBUG master), ff_debug_images (DGS_FF_DEBUG), fusion_debug (DGS_FUSION_DEBUG), track_traj_log (DGS_TRACK_TRAJ_LOG).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: _validate runs after every load_runtime_config and reload_overrides and raises on: (1) source not in {'sim','real'}; (2) depth.scene_depth_max_m != depth.depth_max_m (loss-mask invariant); (3) static_scale_reset_value_m >= static_scale_clamp_max_m (reset must be below clamp_max to avoid boundary re-trip); (4) source=='real' AND sim_noise.enabled (would double-noise real depth); (5) background_color != (0.86,0.92,1.0) (Invariant #6, must stay Gazebo sky). These are hard guards that make a misconfigured boot fail loudly rather than silently produce wrong output.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: Almost all config is frozen at boot; only a whitelist of knobs can be re-read at runtime without relaunch for live A/B tuning. _RELOAD_WHITELIST = (DGS_FF_ICP, DGS_FF_MAX_SCALE_M, DGS_FF_MIN_SCALE_M, DGS_HOLD_WINDOW, DGS_HOLD_TRANS_MM, DGS_HOLD_ROT_DEG, DGS_KF_ACCEL_SIGMA, DGS_KF_ALPHA_SIGMA). reload_overrides(cfg) returns a NEW frozen config built with dataclasses.replace, re-reading ONLY those env vars into feedforward (icp_refine, max_scale_m, min_scale_m), tracker (static_hold_window/trans_mm/rot_deg) and pose_filter (accel_sigma, alpha_sigma); it re-validates and never mutates in place (the caller atomically swaps it in so the 3 threads keep seeing an immutable object).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: Config fingerprint for warm-cache drift detection
SHARED.idea: config_fingerprint(cfg) is a stable 16-hex-char hash (first 16 chars of sha256) of json.dumps(dataclasses.asdict(cfg), sort_keys=True, default=list) — sort_keys makes it order-independent and default=list serializes the tuple fields. It is stamped into the .pt warm-cache so a later load can detect config drift and warn loudly rather than silently mixing geometry built under different constants.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: Gazebo-sky background enforcement at render & train time
SHARED.idea: Background color is the Gazebo sky _GAZEBO_SKY=(0.86,0.92,1.0). SceneModel calls model.set_background(tensor(_GAZEBO_SKY)) AND monkeypatches model._get_background_color = lambda: _sky.to(device). The patch exists because Splatfacto's default background_color='random' returns a RANDOM composite color while self.training, which would train the static scene against a fluctuating photometric bias; forcing the fixed sky even during training prevents the renderer from compensating with opacity tweaks at silhouettes. Empty/region-restricted renders fill rgb with this same background.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: Warm-cache: the SSOT persisted — 6 params + 4 identity buffers
SHARED.idea: Persistence goes through GaussianSet (the SSOT), NOT nerfstudio model.state_dict(). The 6 gauss params (PARAM_NAMES) persisted are: means, features_dc, features_rest, scales, quats, opacities. The 4 identity buffers (IDENTITY_BUFFER_SPECS, fixed order+dtype) are: object_flags (float32), sam3d_init_target_flags (float32), object_instance_ids (long), inserted_flags (float32). GaussianSet.state_dict() exports ONLY the [:count] live rows (dead free-list capacity rows are never persisted): params keyed as 'gauss_params.<name>', buffers keyed by raw name, all detached and moved to CPU.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: save_warm_cache writes a torch.save blob to <data_dir>/static_scene/static_state.pt (DEFAULT_CACHE_NAME='static_state.pt', path via warm_cache_path). The blob dict is: model_state_dict = gset.state_dict() (the gauss_params.<name>+buffer layout, deliberately mirroring the old package's layout so old viewers/tools can still read it, but SOURCED from GaussianSet), num_points = int(gset.num_points), config_fingerprint = config_fingerprint(cfg) or None, layout='dynamic_gs2.v1'. The parent dir is mkdir'd if missing. The seed PLY (depth_camera_init_points.ply, via seed_ply_path) is a separate sibling file, not in this blob.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: load_warm_cache torch.loads the blob (weights_only=False, map_location='cpu'), reads num_points (falling back to model_state_dict['gauss_params.means'].shape[0]), then warns-but-does-not-fail on config drift: if stored config_fingerprint != current config_fingerprint(cfg) it prints a 'config fingerprint drift ... loading anyway (geometry intact; tuning knobs differ)' warning; if the stored fingerprint is None it prints a 'legacy cache (no fingerprint) — accepting' warning. It then calls gset.reload_from_state_dict(sd, num_points). reload_from_state_dict reallocates the 6 params at num_points (accepting either 'name' or 'gauss_params.name' keys, asserting each tensor's row count == num_points), rebuilds the 4 buffers (zero-filling any buffer ABSENT from the dict — legacy caches), resets capacity=count=num_points, regenerates per-row UIDs as arange(num_points), rebinds the optimizer, and re-asserts invariants.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.idea: build_loaded_scene(cfg, device, cache_path, phase='dynamic', lock=None) is the warm-restart path. It first calls _read_cache_seed(cache_path) which pulls means and per-point DC color (decoded from SH band-0 to rgb via rgb = features_dc * 0.28209479177387814 + 0.5, clamped [0,1]) so the inner SplatfactoModel is seeded at the right N and scale. It builds SceneModel(seed_xyz, seed_rgb, phase), attaches a shared render lock (creating an RLock if none passed), then sets freelist = (phase=='dynamic'). For the dynamic phase it enables the over-allocated free-list and installs sm.set_count_provider(lambda: gset.count) so the render slices gauss_params[:count] and dead capacity rows never rasterize; this is safe ONLY because the dynamic phase has LR=0 and renders under no_grad. Finally load_warm_cache reloads the exact tensors. Returns (scene_model, gset, lock).

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: Phase LR policy: static vs dynamic (Invariants #1 & #4)
SHARED.idea: SceneModel.phase in {static,dynamic} drives two enforced gates. enforce_phase_lr() zeroes the Adam LR of a group of param-groups: in STATIC only ('means',) is forced to lr=0.0 (means locked on the TSDF seed; the other 5 params still train); in DYNAMIC ALL of PARAM_NAMES (means,features_dc,features_rest,scales,quats,opacities) are forced to lr=0.0 (dynamic is a runtime, not a training loop — only the tracker's rigid transform + FF inserts mutate the scene). Additionally _bind_means_grad_hook installs, in the dynamic phase only, a backward hook on means that returns zeros_like(g) so a stray backward can never move seed positions even if LR were nonzero. set_phase flips both gates in place for the single-process static->dynamic handoff. rebind() re-asserts both after any count/identity surgery and clears optimizer state.

SHARED.title: Config defaults, conventions & warm-cache
SHARED.topic: SHM frame contract constants & seed-model build params
SHARED.idea: SHM ring defaults (frame.py): DEFAULT_SHM_NAME='dgs_frame_v1' (matches RuntimeConfig.shm_name), DEFAULT_NUM_SLOTS=4 (ring depth, drop-oldest/latest-wins). Frame carries seq, stamp_sec, rgb_bgr, depth_m (already metres), mask_keep, c2w_4x4 (plus finger_l/finger_r gripper-pad points for the viewer overlay). SceneModel seed-build constants: SplatfactoModelConfig(sh_degree default 3 via a getattr fallback since StaticTrainConfig has NO sh_degree field, random_init=False, num_downscales=0 default, resolution_schedule=100); the SceneBox AABB half-extent a = max(|seed_xyz|.abs().max,1.0)*aabb_scale with aabb_scale=4.0; seed_rgb is normalized to [0,255] for Splatfacto (multiplied by 255 if max<=1); model.step is set to 30000 so all SH bands are active at render time.

SHARED.topic: Real-HW branch note (out of sim scope)
SHARED.idea: A real-hardware path exists (source='real' disables sim depth-noise via the derived noise_on gate and is hard-validated against sim_noise.enabled; the ZED-Mini/Jetson camera-mount reparenting lives in ros_mask.py behind DGS_REAL_HW_CAMERA).
